8. clinical_documents — /data/clinical_documents.csv
   Source: [private path]
   Required columns: 患者主索引, 就诊号, 主诉, 现病史, 既往史, 个人史, 月经史, 婚育史, 家族史, 入院诊断, 入院情况, 入院诊断.1, 诊疗经过, 出院情况, 出院诊断, 手术名称, 手术经过.
   The source has two columns both originally named 入院诊断; pandas-style loading yields 入院诊断 and 入院诊断.1. Use note fields only for blinded medication/treatment-intent adjudication, never as automated recurrence truth.

Vitals and transfers contain identifiers only; the front-page source is unusable. Non-drug orders are deferred. None may define contact A or severity.

## Exposure, anchors, outcomes, and estimands

Define A(t)=1 only when an encounters-table start-to-valid-discharge interval overlaps week t. If an interval cannot be formed, use admission, else visit, else discharge as a point date. Define A0 using start dates only. A is a covariate, never an eligibility restriction. Labs, examinations, procedures, medications, every target/control mark, and treatment T must never define A.

Among marker-observed patients, H is the train-scaled pre-landmark marker history: high/persistently elevated versus low/clearing, prespecified from preoperative rank and the latest day-15:60 to preoperative log ratio. Continuous rank and ratio are primary model inputs; the dichotomy is for standardized contrasts. Marker-observed versus marker-absent is a separate full-cohort ascertainment-state contrast. Do not impute a biomarker value for marker-absent patients.

Primary target/control pairs are:

- Laboratory: L-M (AFP/PIVKA-II/AFP-L3 measurement) versus N-L (sodium/creatinine/hemoglobin measurement).
- Imaging: S (hepatic/upper-abdominal CT/MR) versus N-I (nonhepatic CT/MR).

Treatment occurrence T and injury-panel measurement L-I are secondary. Do not infer treatment intent from occurrence.

For mark k estimate standardized 365-day risk R_k(H) by g-computation over empirical covariates and observed A histories. Use only history through t− except contemporaneous A. Report component risks, risk differences, and ratio-of-risk-ratios with patient-cluster bootstrap 95% intervals:

- Δ_lab = [R_L-M(high) − R_L-M(low)] − [R_N-L(high) − R_N-L(low)].
- Δ_img = [R_S(high) − R_S(low)] − [R_N-I(high) − R_N-I(low)].

These are standardized descriptive associations, not causal effects.

## Required baseline and substantive alternative

Fit one transparent stacked discrete-time recurrent-mark model on the full grid. Include mark-type indicators for L-M, S, N-L, N-I; a common spline of week; a common covariate basis; mark-specific intercepts; current-A and lagged-A interactions; and marker-history by mark-type interactions. Select elastic-net regularization on validation only, then refit the selected basis with GEE or patient-cluster-robust inference. Use patient-cluster bootstrap for standardized risks and paired specificity intervals. Fit A separately with pooled logistic regression using only baseline variables and lagged A; never use it for inverse-probability selection. Report calibration-in-the-large, calibration slope, Brier score, and log loss by mark and split. Add L-I and T secondarily and report the A=1 encounter-choice estimand only as secondary.

Use these same patients, weeks, marks, covariates, and split for an anchored discrete-time multivariate state-space marked-process model:

- observed A anchors a generic-contact state U with fixed positive loading +1;
- U may affect every mark and transitions use baseline variables and lagged A only;
- target-selection state V loads +1 on L-M, exactly zero on A, N-L, and N-I, and has estimated loadings on S and secondary T;
- injury-recovery state W uses dated ALT/AST/bilirubin/INR positively and albumin/platelets negatively, with label/era offsets;
- marker state M uses within-label ranks/ratios for AFP and optional PIVKA-II/AFP-L3 and must never be called tumor;
- emissions are multilabel and preserve target-only, control-only, co-marked, and A=0 mark weeks;
- transitions and emissions use t− history except observed contemporaneous A.

Compare U-only against U+V. Evaluate held-out marked-process log likelihood, target/control Brier and calibration, posterior predictive counts in all six observed week states, loading/seed stability, and simulation recovery. Use three seeds. Require U/V recovery correlation at least 0.8, no factor swap, and 90–98% interval coverage in prespecified null, target-specific, and shared-contact simulations. Select U+V only if it reduces validation targeted-mark deviance by at least 1% relative to U-only, does not reduce control-mark deviance by at least 1%, remains calibrated, and passes simulation and seed gates. Otherwise retain the transparent model as primary. A learned-model failure does not invalidate a completed transparent association analysis; it limits latent-state claims.

The baseline exposes pair-specific contrasts but loses irregular within-week ordering, continuous coupling of values and observation, and residual patient-level contact heterogeneity. The alternative can reveal whether residual longitudinal covariance is concentrated in HCC-targeted marks. It still cannot identify intent, outside care, or biology.

Planned resources are 8–16 CPUs and 64 GiB for 1–2 hours for the transparent model, and one allocated A100, 16 CPUs, and 128 GiB for 4–6 hours for the state-space model, with checkpoints. These are unverified estimates within the 16-CPU, 8-GPU, 256-GiB, 8-hour planning envelope. Use cuda:0 only inside an allocated GPU run. A CPU hierarchical recurrent-event implementation is the fallback if GPU infrastructure fails; infrastructure failure is not evidence about the hypothesis.

A generic transformer remains deferred because predictive gain alone would not distinguish shared contact from target selection. Inverse-intensity weighting remains deferred because these sources cannot recover outside care or death.

## Mandatory audits, gates, sensitivities, and falsification

Before final interpretation:

- Confirm at least 20 patients with each primary mark in validation and test. The frozen audit reported validation/test support L-M 145/145, S 48/43, N-L 154/155, N-I 47/35.
- Report every A-by-mark cross-cell by split and retain all A=0 marks. The audit reported 14 A=0 target-only weeks and one A=0 control-only week.
- Require at least 100 effective patients per dichotomous exposure contrast after standardization. Otherwise use continuous association only and classify the dichotomous contrast inconclusive.
- Blind-review at least 100 sampled laboratory labels and at least 100 examination titles. Each target and control dictionary requires PPV and NPV at least 0.90.
- For treatment interpretation, require at least 100 medication-positive and 100 oncology-like dictionary-negative snippets reviewed by pharmacy/hepatobiliary experts, with PPV and NPV at least 0.85. Otherwise describe T only as unclassified treatment occurrence.
- Verify that no target/control field enters A and no current/future outcome enters predictors.
- Repeat with lagged-A-only, A0, assay-era handling, and the broad cytotoxic dictionary.
- Permute marker history in train only, within era and observation strata. Target specificity must disappear while generic contact structure is retained. Report the permutation metrics rather than only a boolean assertion.
- Report timestamp/interval disagreements, duplicate keys, source/header checks, cohort flow, all mark supports, and hashes of cohort/grid/dictionaries/code.

A clinically material specificity signal is Δ at least 0.02 absolute standardized 365-day risk and ratio-of-risk-ratios at least 1.25. Apply Holm adjustment across the two primary pairs.

The inherited biological report-content route remains prohibited unless there are at least 300 first untreated reports, at least 100 adjudicated affirmative and 100 adjudicated explicit-negative reports, at least 20 of each in locked test, and PPV/NPV at least 0.85. Meeting this gate still requires a separate scientifically approved study; do not add recurrence as an outcome here.

## Interpretation rules

Supportive: at least one Holm-adjusted pair has lower 95% bounds above 0 for Δ and above 1 for the ratio-of-risk-ratios; its point estimates meet Δ ≥0.02 and ratio-of-risk-ratios ≥1.25; direction replicates in locked test; absolute calibration error is at most 0.02; and the stratified train-only permutation no longer satisfies this supportive specificity pattern while retaining generic contact structure. This supports only a residual target-specific recording/selection association in this institution. Stable U+V improvement additionally supports longitudinal concentration in target marks, but is not required for the transparent association and is never causal or biological.

Adverse: for both pairs, upper 95% bounds are below Δ=0.02 and ratio-of-risk-ratios=1.25; marker-history associations are no greater for targets than controls; and U+V does not improve held-out targeted-mark deviance over U-only by at least 1%. This supports generic contact/severity as an adequate observed explanation and argues against a clinically material target-specific selection signal.

Inconclusive: use this for an imprecise null, failed dictionary or effective-support gate, test-direction reversal, material encounter timestamp inconsistency, assay-era sensitivity reversal, failed calibration, failed U/V recovery when making latent claims, too-sparse A=0 sensitivity cells, unreconciled cohort/grid counts, incomplete fitting, or any other unmet mandatory gate. Baseline support with failed U/V recovery permits only a transparent association claim and no latent-state claim.

Negative-control falsification is intrinsic to the paired estimands. Posterior-predictive excess concentrated in controls, or comparable U+V improvement in controls, falsifies the target-specific latent interpretation.

## Required deliverables

Place all outputs under /workspace. Source code is part of the submission; do not output row-level clinical data.

1. /workspace/run.sh — executable entry point that performs the complete study.
2. /workspace/analysis.py — substantive implementation, with all dictionaries and transformations versioned or loaded from solver-created files.
3. /workspace/results.json — UTF-8 JSON using schema hcc-surveillance-selection-results-v1.
4. /workspace/run_manifest.json — source snapshot and eight source SHA-256 values, code hash, start/end times, resources, random seeds, package versions, and hashes of results plus any model/checkpoint artifacts.
5. /workspace/report.md — concise scientific report with cohort flow, audit results, baseline and learned-model estimates, uncertainty, sensitivities, falsification results, one interpretation class, and limitations.

results.json must contain these top-level objects: schema, status, sources, cohort, split_support, anchor_audit, dictionary_audit, leakage_audit, baseline, learned, sensitivities, permutation, conclusion, and output_index.

Required computable content includes:

- cohort.n_patients, cohort.n_weeks, cohort.flow, cohort.cohort_sha256, cohort.grid_sha256, and discrepancy explanations;
- split_support for train, validation, test, reserve with patient and primary-mark support;
- anchor_audit with A/A0 patient and week counts, every A-by-mark cross-cell by split, A=0 target/control-only counts, linked-key and timestamp disagreement counts;
- dictionary_audit sample sizes, confusion matrices, PPV/NPV, blinding method, and reviewer-role metadata for laboratory, imaging, and treatment dictionaries;
- leakage_audit booleans and field-level feature provenance;
- baseline model specification, validation selection, fit status, component risks, Δ and ratio-of-risk-ratios with unadjusted and Holm-adjusted cluster-bootstrap intervals for both pairs, locked-test direction, calibration, Brier, and log loss by mark/split;
- learned U-only and U+V fit status, held-out target/control deviance, relative improvements, calibration/Brier, six-state posterior-predictive checks, all three seeds, loading stability, factor-swap result, and all three simulation recovery/coverage results;
- all required sensitivities with direction and materiality changes;
- permutation estimates, intervals, whether the supportive specificity pattern survives, and evidence that generic-contact structure remains;
- conclusion.classification exactly supportive, adverse, or inconclusive; conclusion.claim_scope exactly institutional_recording_association, generic_contact_adequate, or no_resolved_claim; conclusion.evidence_links naming exact result fields; and booleans causal_effect=false, biological_recurrence=false, clinician_intent=false, outside_care_complete=false, alive_at_risk=false.

Set status=complete only if the cohort/grid, transparent model, U-only/U+V comparison, uncertainty, audits, required sensitivities, and falsification analyses were computed. Otherwise set status=inconclusive_prerequisite and explain every missing component; such a submission does not complete the task, even if its scientific interpretation is honestly inconclusive.

The verifier checks source declarations, fixed design invariants, split isolation, required fit/evaluation fields, numerical/internal consistency, thresholds, claim scope, and whether the interpretation follows the computed result. It does not reward confirmation. A structurally complete adverse or inconclusive result is as valid as a supportive result.

The verifier cannot establish whether clinical adjudicators were qualified or blinded, whether lexical dictionaries capture clinical meaning beyond reviewed samples, true recurrence, treatment indication, clinician motivation, outside contact/death, assay equivalence, causal surveillance effects, or a biological interpretation of V. Those require expert review, linked mortality/claims and assay metadata, prospective scheduled surveillance, or another study.

## Exact results.json mechanical contract

The verifier uses the following exact nested names in addition to the scientific requirements above.

- `sources` maps each of `encounters, procedures, diagnoses, pathology, labs, examinations, medications, clinical_documents` to an object containing `sha256` and `target`.
- `split_support.<split>` contains `n_patients` and `marks` with integer `L-M, S, N-L, N-I`.
- `anchor_audit` contains `a_patients, a_weeks, a0_patients, a0_weeks, a_eq_0_target_only_weeks, a_eq_0_control_only_weeks, linked_key_missing_rows, timestamp_disagreement_rows`, plus `cross_cells` by split.
- Each `dictionary_audit.<laboratory|imaging>.<target|control>` object contains `n_reviewed, ppv, npv, blinded, confusion_matrix`. `dictionary_audit.treatment` contains `interpretation_attempted`; when true it additionally contains `n_positive_reviewed, n_negative_reviewed, ppv, npv, blinded, reviewer_roles`, and when false it contains `status="unclassified_treatment_occurrence"`.
- `leakage_audit` contains booleans `anchor_outcome_independent, predictors_use_no_current_or_future_outcome, test_locked_until_freeze, reserve_unused` and nonempty `feature_provenance`.
- `baseline.fit_status` is `complete`; `baseline.pairs.lab` and `baseline.pairs.imaging` each contain:
  - `delta: {estimate, ci95: [lower, upper], holm_reject_positive}`;
  - `risk_ratio_ratio: {estimate, ci95: [lower, upper], holm_reject_above_one}`;
  - `component_risks` with finite `target_high, target_low, control_high, control_low` in [0,1];
  - `test_direction_replicates`, `target_association_no_greater_than_control`, and `effective_patients`.
- `baseline.metrics` contains all four primary marks, each with validation and test `calibration_abs_error, calibration_slope, brier, log_loss`.
- `learned.u_only.fit_status` and `learned.u_plus_v.fit_status` are complete. `learned.comparison` contains `target_deviance_relative_improvement, control_deviance_relative_improvement, calibrated, seed_count, uv_recovery_correlation, factor_swap, simulations_pass`, and `six_state_posterior_predictive`.
- `sensitivities` contains `lagged_a_only, a0_start_only, assay_era, broad_cytotoxic`, each with `complete` and `direction_reversal`.
- `permutation` contains `complete, supportive_pattern_survives, generic_contact_retained, estimates`.
- `conclusion` has `classification, claim_scope, evidence_links, reasons` and the five required false claim booleans. `output_index.model_artifacts` maps `baseline, u_only, u_plus_v, bootstrap, simulation` to nonempty aggregate/checkpoint files below `/workspace`; `run_manifest.artifact_sha256` hashes those exact files, and `run_manifest.code_sha256` hashes `/workspace/analysis.py`.

All numeric values must be JSON numbers, not strings, NaN, or infinity. Every evidence link must be a valid dot path into results.json. The report classification and scope must match results.json.

## Key references

[K1] Liang L, Wang MD, Zhang YM, et al. Association of Postoperative Biomarker Response with Recurrence and Survival in Patients with Hepatocellular Carcinoma and High Alpha-Fetoprotein Expressions (>400 ng/ml). Journal of Hepatocellular Carcinoma. 2021;8:103–118. https://doi.org/10.2147/JHC.S289840

[K2] Agniel D, Kohane IS, Weber GM. Biases in electronic health record data due to processes within the healthcare system: retrospective observational study. BMJ. 2018;361:k1479. https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj.k1479

[K3] Sisk R, Lin L, Sperrin M, et al. Informative presence and observation in routine health data: A review of methodology for clinical risk prediction. Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association. 2021;28(1):155–166. https://doi.org/10.1093/jamia/ocaa242

# Outcome-independent contact anchoring for postoperative HCC surveillance selection

Status: substantive child of candidate-606e4062a9517dea8102d8a1. A bounded aggregate audit repaired the parent’s outcome-derived opportunity definition and verified support for encounter-only anchors, target-only weeks, and common target/control risk sets. No hypothesis model has been fitted. The biological recurrence route remains frozen.

## Scientific opening, supported claim, unresolved claim, and advance

The strongest evidence-supported clinical claim is that, in 549 selected resected HCC patients with preoperative AFP >400 ng/mL, incomplete AFP response measured at a 4–6-week postoperative visit was associated with worse recurrence-free and overall survival [K1]. This does not establish that persistent AFP is residual tumor, that follow-up AFP availability is ignorable, or that changing surveillance improves outcomes.

Routine EHR observation is generated by care: in 669,452 patients at two hospitals, the presence and timing of many common laboratory orders were strongly associated with survival independently of recorded values [K2]. A methodological review distinguishes patient presence from longitudinal observation, describes explicit observation-process and latent-structure methods, and warns that prediction and explanation require different interpretations [K3]. These works support treating observation as data; they do not identify why a specific HCC patient was measured.

The unresolved claim tested here is: among adults at a day-60 landmark after first observed HCC resection, pre-landmark marker history is associated with subsequent HCC-targeted measurement or imaging beyond an independently recorded institutional encounter process and measured severity, and that association is stronger than the same marker-history association with comparable generic laboratory and nonhepatic-imaging outcomes. The leading explanation is residual target-specific surveillance selection. The strongest rival is ordinary local contact/severity: patients with more recorded encounters or greater illness burden receive all tests, without a distinct HCC-targeting process.

This matters because biomarker studies conditioned on observed follow-up can select a highly monitored subgroup and overstate transportability. The parent attempted to address this but defined generic opportunity G partly from non-marker labs and nonhepatic imaging while also using those same events as negative-control outcomes. Conditioning on G could therefore select deterministically on modeled outcomes, induce collider bias, and omit target-only weeks. This child’s substantive advance is an outcome-independent at-risk process: every eligible patient contributes the same 44-week grid; encounter contact comes only from the encounters table; no target or control event creates eligibility or contact; and targets and controls use identical denominators and feature bases.

This is an ascertainment study. It does not test biological recurrence or a treatment effect.

## Hypothesis and estimands

Primary hypothesis: on the fixed day-61:365 patient-week grid, high/persistently elevated versus low/clearing pre-landmark marker trajectory is associated with greater standardized cumulative incidence of:

1. AFP/PIVKA-II/AFP-L3 measurement (L-M) relative to sodium/creatinine/hemoglobin measurement (N-L); and/or
2. hepatic/upper-abdominal CT/MR (S) relative to nonhepatic CT/MR (N-I),

after adjustment for an outcome-independent encounter anchor A, lagged encounter history, calendar and measured severity.

A is not a restriction. For every patient-week, A(t)=1 only if an encounters-table interval from admission/visit/start through valid discharge overlaps the week; when an interval cannot be formed, the admission, else visit, else discharge fallback date lies in the week. A start-date-only version is prespecified sensitivity A0. Labs, examinations, procedures, medications, L-M, S, treatment T, N-L and N-I never define A.

All eligible patients are operationally at risk for a *recorded local-system mark* in every one of 44 weeks from day 61 through day 365, regardless of A and regardless of previous marks. There is no death field, complete outside-care capture, or enrollment-end field, so “no mark” means no mark in these institutional sources—not alive, disease-free, or absent from care. This fixed local-capture estimand is preferable to censoring at last contact, which would again make follow-up depend on observed care.

Let H be the train-scaled marker-history exposure among marker-observed patients: persistent/high versus low/clearing, prespecified from preoperative rank and latest day-15:60/preoperative log ratio; continuous rank and ratio are primary model inputs, and the dichotomy is used for standardized contrasts. Do not pool raw values across labels or eras because lab units and assay platform are unavailable. Marker-observed versus marker-absent is a separate full-cohort ascertainment-state contrast; no biomarker value is imputed for absent patients.

For mark k, estimate standardized 365-day risk (R_k(H)) by g-computation over the empirical covariate and observed A histories, using history through t− only except contemporaneous A. The two primary specificity estimands are:

- laboratory specificity: Δ_lab = [R_L-M(high)−R_L-M(low)] − [R_N-L(high)−R_N-L(low)];
- imaging specificity: Δ_img = [R_S(high)−R_S(low)] − [R_N-I(high)−R_N-I(low)].

Also report ratio-of-risk-ratios, each component risk and cluster-bootstrap 95% intervals. These are standardized descriptive associations, not causal effects of marker level or testing. Treatment T and injury-panel measurement L-I are secondary marks; T intent is not inferred from occurrence.

## Population and temporal boundaries

Retain the audited parent population. Include age ≥18; earliest dated liver resection during 2012–2023 within 30 days of linked encounter date and in the same encounter as non-uncertain “肝细胞癌” or “原发性肝癌”; exclude transplant, donor, biopsy/puncture, cyst/abscess, explicit recurrent/repeat wording, and duplicate index-encounter procedure rows. Retain the earliest qualifying resection per patient.

Exclude recorded TACE/embolization, ablation, transplant, separate repeat resection, or strict-dictionary systemic HCC therapy from index+1 through day 60. Prior recorded treatment in days −180:−1 is a measured state, not an exclusion. Repeat the full analysis under the broader cytotoxic medication dictionary. Predictor history is day −90 through +60; the day-60 landmark prevents predictor/outcome overlap. Outcomes and encounter anchoring are day 61 through 365. All index surgeries end by 2023; inspected maxima reach 2025-12-31 for labs and 2026-01-02 for examinations, but source-calendar coverage does not prove complete follow-up.

The biological report-content route remains prohibited unless the inherited gate is met: ≥300 first untreated reports, ≥100 adjudicated affirmative and ≥100 adjudicated explicit-negative reports, ≥20 of each in locked test, and PPV/NPV ≥0.85.

## Observed outcome-independent-anchor audit

The attached aggregate-only audit ran against HCC snapshot `3f97e661e1884c34c1e2cdbf74ba0cf6d6c8995853e85f1857c3d72b82ccf521` in 50.3 seconds on 4 CPUs/32 GiB. It reproduced N=15,575 strict-dictionary eligible patients and created 685,300 patient-weeks. These are feasibility counts, not hypothesis results.

Encounter-only support:

- 1,975 patients had at least one admission-to-discharge-overlap anchor after day 60; 7,056 weeks had A=1.
- The start-date-only sensitivity had 1,949 patients and 4,744 anchored weeks.
- There were 626 A=1 target-without-control weeks, including 76 validation and 64 locked-test weeks; 560 A=1 control-without-target weeks, including 44 validation and 52 test weeks.
- Fourteen target-only weeks had A=0 (9 train, 2 validation, 1 test, 2 reserve); one control-only week had A=0. They are retained, not dropped.
- All 8,906 L-M rows, 33,650 L-I rows, 17,163 N-L rows, 600 S rows and 642 N-I rows carried a `(患者主索引, 就诊号)` key present in encounters. Timestamp/interval disagreement explains the rare A=0 mark weeks and is a required data-quality report.
- Mark-week support was L-M 3,223 (22 A=0), S 583 (5 A=0), T 2,687 (0 A=0), N-L 3,917 (15 A=0), and N-I 594 (2 A=0). Validation/test patient support was L-M 145/145, S 48/43, N-L 154/155 and N-I 47/35.

Thus A can be defined independently, target-only weeks exist and are supported, and target/control outcomes can be compared on the same grid. The sparse A=0 mark cells preclude treating “given A=1” as the sole primary estimand; it remains a secondary encounter-choice analysis.

The earlier medication-aware audit remains applicable: paired marker+injury N=14,845; marker absent N=730 (56 validation, 73 test); two marker and two injury dates N=11,767; S-or-T N=1,616. The nonpositive four-state measurement outcome remains descriptive only.

## Exact HCC bindings

All sources are ordinary read-only CSV files, with no archive members. Join within encounter on `(患者主索引, 就诊号)`, link across encounters on `患者主索引`, audit duplicate keys before aggregation, and write only aggregate/derived files to the workspace.

- **encounters** — `[private path]`; columns `患者主索引`, `就诊号`, `年龄`, `性别`, `就诊时间`, `入院时间`, `出院时间`, `就诊科室`. This is the sole source of A/A0 and supplies age, sex, service and length of stay. Define start as admission, else visit, else discharge; define end as valid discharge ≥ start, else start. Do not extend an encounter beyond recorded discharge.
- **procedures** — `[private path]`; `患者主索引`, `就诊号`, `手术`, `开始时间`, `结束时间`, `手术来源`. Supplies index resection, locoregional T, transplant and repeat resection.
- **diagnoses** — `[private path]`; `患者主索引`, `就诊号`, `诊断名称`, `诊断类型`. It has no native time; inherit the encounter start only for baseline HCC support and comorbidity/severity proxies, never for a follow-up mark.
- **pathology** — `[private path]`; `患者主索引`, `就诊号`, `病理`, `检查所见`, `检查诊断`, `机器型号`. It has no native time and supplies baseline HCC support plus audited margin, vascular-invasion, satellite, cirrhosis, grade and tumor-burden proxies.
- **labs** — `[private path]`; `患者主索引`, `就诊号`, `检验`, `定性结果`, `定量结果`, `标本类型`, `检验时间`. L-M exact labels: `甲胎蛋白`, `异常凝血酶原`, `甲胎蛋白异质体`; L-I: `丙氨酸氨基转移酶`, `门冬氨酸氨基转移酶`, `总胆红素`, `白蛋白`, `国际标准化比值`, `血小板计数`; N-L: `钠`, `肌酐`, `血红蛋白`. There is no unit or assay-platform column; use label/era-specific ranks and within-label ratios.
- **examinations** — `[private path]`; `患者主索引`, `就诊号`, `检查`, `检查所见`, `检查诊断`, `开始时间`, `机器型号`, `检查号`. Supplies S and N-I from audited CT/MR title rules. Images are unavailable. Report text is not a recurrence label.
- **medications** — `[private path]`; exact inspected headers `患者主索引`, `就诊号`, `用药`, `单次用药计量`, `单次用药计量单位`, `频次`, `开始时间`, `结束时间`, `用药方式`, `药品类型`. Use start, else end, else linked encounter start for systemic T and PIVKA-related medication flags. Indication is unavailable.
- **clinical_documents** — `[private path]`; exact inspected headers `患者主索引`, `就诊号`, `主诉`, `现病史`, `既往史`, `个人史`, `月经史`, `婚育史`, `家族史`, `入院诊断`, `入院情况`, `入院诊断.1`, `诊疗经过`, `出院情况`, `出院诊断`, `手术名称`, `手术经过`. Normalize `入院诊断.1` as the second admission-diagnosis field. Use only in blinded medication/treatment-intent adjudication, never as automated recurrence truth.

Nominal vitals and transfers contain identifiers only, and the front-page file is unusable; none defines A or severity. Non-drug orders are deferred because order status needs label review and adding them to A would reintroduce a care-action-dependent opportunity definition.

## Frozen split and common preprocessing

Assign patients by `int(SHA256(患者主索引)[:8],16) mod 100`: 0–59 train, 60–69 validation, 70–79 locked test, 80–99 untouched reserve. Freeze cohort, event dictionaries, A construction, transformations, exposure thresholds, gates and model-selection rules before test access. Reserve is not used for fitting or selection. Both methods receive the identical 44-week grid, patients, dated marks, covariates and split.

Every mark is binary within week; multiple same-mark rows collapse to one, while different marks may co-occur. Features use information through t−: lagged A counts and recency, lagged mark counts/recency, baseline pathology/severity, age, sex, year, service, index length of stay, prior treatment, pre-landmark injury trajectory, marker-observation state, exact marker label/specimen, and medication flags. Contemporaneous A is allowed because it comes from independent encounter fields, but results must be repeated with lagged-A-only and start-date-only A0. No N-L or N-I outcome enters another outcome’s feature set at t.

## Matched transparent alternative

Fit one stacked discrete-time recurrent-mark model on the full grid with mark-type indicators for L-M, S, N-L and N-I, a common spline of week, common covariate basis, mark-specific intercepts, A/current and lagged-A interactions, and marker-history × mark-type interactions. Use elastic-net regularization chosen in validation, then refit the selected basis with GEE or cluster-robust estimation; use patient-cluster bootstrap for standardized risks and paired specificity intervals. Fit A itself in a separate pooled-logistic model using only baseline variables and lagged A; this describes institutional contact and is not used for inverse-probability selection.

Report Δ_lab, Δ_img, ratio-of-risk-ratios, all component risks, calibration-in-the-large, calibration slope, Brier score and log loss by mark and split. Secondary models add L-I and T with the same grid. Also report the encounter-choice estimand among A=1 weeks, but never substitute it for the primary grid result.

This baseline directly exposes whether the same marker-history contrast differs between target and control outcomes. It loses irregular within-week ordering, continuous coupling of evolving values and observation, and residual patient-level contact heterogeneity.

## Matched learned/mechanistic alternative

Fit an anchored discrete-time multivariate state-space marked-process model on the identical grid:

- observed A is an emission anchoring latent generic-contact state U with fixed positive loading +1;
- U may affect every mark; its transition uses baseline variables and lagged A only;
- target-selection state V has loading +1 on L-M, exactly zero on A, N-L and N-I, and estimated loadings on S and secondary T;
- injury-recovery state W uses dated ALT/AST/bilirubin/INR positively and albumin/platelets negatively, with label/era offsets;
- marker state M uses within-label ranks/ratios for AFP and optional PIVKA-II/AFP-L3 and is never called tumor;
- the weekly mark vector is multilabel, so A=1 target-only, control-only, co-marked and A=0 target-only weeks all contribute without deterministic conditioning;
- all transitions and emissions use only t− history except observed contemporaneous A.

Compare U-only with U+V. The alternative can reveal whether residual covariance is concentrated in HCC-targeted marks and preserve evolving irregular histories that the baseline compresses. It cannot identify clinician intent, outside care, or tumor biology. Evaluate held-out marked-process log likelihood, target/control Brier and calibration, posterior predictive counts in all six observed week states, loading/seed stability and simulation recovery. Require three seeds, U/V recovery correlation ≥0.8, no factor swap, and 90–98% interval coverage in prespecified null, target-specific and shared-contact simulations. Select U+V only if it reduces validation targeted-mark deviance by ≥1% relative to U-only without reducing control-mark deviance by ≥1%, remains calibrated, and passes simulation/seed gates. Otherwise prefer the transparent baseline.

Planned future-solver resources: transparent model 8–16 CPUs, 64 GiB, 1–2 hours; state-space model one allocated A100, 16 CPUs, 128 GiB, 4–6 hours, with checkpoints. These are unverified planning estimates within the 16-CPU/8-GPU/256-GiB/8-hour solver envelope. The measured discovery audit used 4 CPUs/32 GiB for 50.3 seconds. A CPU hierarchical recurrent-event model is the fallback if GPU dependencies fail; infrastructure failure is not scientific evidence.

A generic transformer is deferred because prediction gain alone would not distinguish shared contact from target selection. Inverse-intensity weighting is deferred as primary because no model can recover outside care or death absent from the sources.

## Gates, falsification, and interpretation

Before final fitting:

- retain ≥20 patient-level occurrences of each primary mark in validation and test (observed patient support passes: L-M 145/145, S 48/43, N-L 154/155, N-I 47/35);
- report all A/mark cross-cells by split, including the 14 audited A=0 target-only weeks; never drop or recode them;
- require ≥100 effective patients per exposure contrast after standardization; otherwise narrow to continuous association or declare the dichotomous contrast inconclusive;
- audit ≥100 sampled laboratory labels and ≥100 examination titles, blinded to marker exposure, with PPV/NPV ≥0.90 for each target/control dictionary;
- for T interpretation, require ≥100 medication-positive and ≥100 oncology-like dictionary-negative snippets reviewed by pharmacy/hepatobiliary experts with PPV/NPV ≥0.85; otherwise T remains unclassified treatment occurrence;
- verify no target/control field contributes to A and no current/future outcome leaks into predictors.

A clinically material specificity signal is prespecified as Δ ≥2 absolute percentage points in standardized 365-day risk and ratio-of-risk-ratios ≥1.25.

**Supportive:** at least one Holm-adjusted target/control pair has lower 95% bounds above zero for Δ and above 1 for the ratio-of-risk-ratios, point estimates meet both materiality thresholds, direction replicates in locked test, calibration is acceptable (absolute calibration error ≤0.02), and permutation of marker history within era/observation stratum removes the specificity. This supports a residual target-specific *recording/selection association* in this institution. Stable U+V improvement adds evidence that the dependence is longitudinally concentrated in target marks; it is not required to call the transparent association supportive and never makes it causal.

**Adverse:** for both pairs, upper 95% bounds exclude Δ=0.02 and ratio-of-risk-ratios=1.25, marker-history associations are no greater for targets than controls, and U-only predicts held-out target marks as well as U+V within the 1% deviance threshold. This supports ordinary contact/severity as the adequate observed explanation and argues against a clinically material target-specific selection signal.

**Inconclusive:** intervals include clinically material positive specificity; dictionaries fail review; effective support fails; test direction reverses; A construction is materially inconsistent with linked timestamps; assay-era sensitivity reverses results; calibration fails; U/V simulation or stability fails when making latent claims; or A=0 marks are too sparse for the lagged-A/start-only sensitivities. An imprecise null is not adverse evidence. Baseline support with failed U/V recovery permits only the transparent association claim.

Negative-control falsification is built into the paired estimands. Additional train-only marker-history permutation must erase target specificity while preserving generic contact structure. A V loading on A, N-L or N-I is fixed at zero by design; posterior predictive excess concentrated in controls, or comparable U+V control improvement, falsifies the intended target-specific interpretation.

## Required solver deliverable and verifier boundary

The solver must newly construct and hash the cohort/grid; produce cohort flow, source/header checks, dictionary review, A/mark cross-cells and split support; fit the transparent stacked model and U-only/U+V alternatives; generate standardized component risks and paired specificity estimates with clustered uncertainty; report held-out calibration/deviance, permutation results, simulations and three-seed diagnostics; and write a machine-readable supportive/adverse/inconclusive conclusion linked to exact output cells. No hypothesis result has yet been computed.

The verifier can check source hashes, joins, temporal boundaries, A independence from all modeled outcomes, preservation of target-only weeks, split isolation, model inputs, fits, uncertainty calculations, diagnostics, thresholds and whether the reported conclusion follows computed outputs. It cannot establish alive-at-risk status, outside contact, true recurrence, treatment indication, clinician motivation, causal effects of surveillance, assay equivalence or a biological meaning for V. Those require linked mortality/claims data, clinical adjudication, assay metadata, prospective scheduled surveillance or another study.

## Alternatives retained and revisit triggers

- Parent outcome-derived G: rejected because N-L/N-I both created opportunity and served as outcomes.
- A=1-only choice model: retained as secondary; rejected as primary because it omits 14 A=0 target-only weeks and changes the estimand to within-recorded-encounter choice.
- Fixed grid plus encounter-only A: selected because opportunity is independent of all outcomes and target/control denominators are identical.
- Transparent stacked model: selected as the primary completed analysis if learned recovery fails.
- Anchored U+V model: selected as the substantive alternative only after simulation recovery and target-specific held-out improvement.
- Orders-based opportunity: revisit only after order-status and order-purpose adjudication demonstrates a generic, outcome-independent scheduled-contact signal.
- Four-state measurement multinomial: remains rejected for nonpositivity (marker-only 0; neither 54).
- Biological recurrence route: remains frozen until the inherited adjudicated-report gate or prospective surveillance data is available.

## Compact bibliography

[K1] Liang L, Wang MD, Zhang YM, et al. Association of Postoperative Biomarker Response with Recurrence and Survival in Patients with Hepatocellular Carcinoma and High Alpha-Fetoprotein Expressions (>400 ng/ml). *Journal of Hepatocellular Carcinoma*. 2021;8:103–118. doi:10.2147/JHC.S289840.

[K2] Agniel D, Kohane IS, Weber GM. Biases in electronic health record data due to processes within the healthcare system: retrospective observational study. *BMJ*. 2018;361:k1479. doi:10.1136/bmj.k1479.

[K3] Sisk R, Lin L, Sperrin M, et al. Informative presence and observation in routine health data: A review of methodology for clinical risk prediction. *Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association*. 2021;28(1):155–166. doi:10.1093/jamia/ocaa242.

# Explicit nutrition interruption during charted IV insulin and short-horizon hypoglycemia in eICU

## Status, scientific opening, and deliverable

This is a substantive repair of expert seed `expert-20260913-eicu-09` / parent `candidate-8d57aa68820247ee4e4a8c93`. It is a planned observational experiment, not an executed result. The original all-insulin claim is not supportable: eICU `medication` records active orders and explicitly does not guarantee administration. The repair restricts exposure to repeated charted IV insulin rate states in `infusionDrug`, restricts nutrition comparison to explicit timestamped `nurseCare` state transitions, and never treats missing nutrition documentation as cessation.

The strongest evidence-supported claim is that inpatient insulin is a high-alert therapy, decreasing intake/NPO status changes insulin need and warrants monitoring [K2]; AKI was strongly associated with hypoglycemia in an insulin-treated two-ICU cohort [K1]; and a single-center cohort receiving continuous enteral nutrition had infrequent level-1 and level-2 hypoglycemia across compared subcutaneous regimens [K3]. These works do not establish whether an explicit nutrition interruption during charted IV insulin creates a reproducible short hazard window beyond current glucose, insulin rate, renal trajectory, severity and monitoring.

The unresolved hypothesis is:

> Among adult eICU stays at an explicit nutrition-state transition while a positive, unit-standardized IV insulin rate has been charted within 120 minutes, transition from documented carbohydrate-providing nutrition to documented NPO is followed by a higher six-hour hazard of glucose <70 mg/dL than documented nutrition continuation at otherwise comparable dynamic states; the excess is larger when creatinine has risen in the preceding 48 hours and is attenuated when insulin is promptly reduced or stopped.

This is a risk-window/decision-support hypothesis, not a causal effect of withholding nutrition. The leading rival is worsening illness: procedures, shock, organ failure or declining glucose may jointly prompt NPO, insulin adjustment, denser testing and dextrose. Documentation/interface timing is a second rival. The clinical advance is to decide whether a simple safety trigger—explicit NPO transition plus active IV insulin, especially with renal worsening—merits prospective protocol evaluation. A supported retrospective association alone does not authorize a bedside alert or insulin change.

The future solver must construct the cohort and all transitions; fit the transparent and temporal models below; estimate absolute and relative six-hour risk with uncertainty; execute reverse-timing, monitoring, rescue, severity, hospital and documentation checks; and emit auditable tables, predictions and conclusion labels. Confirmation is not required for completion.

## Audited feasibility and consequent narrowing

Snapshot: `896e1fb70d4e2d1a59c9fd87c64735dcfaff476fe89543643c08b7df637a15ec`.

Executed source-only audit (see attached CSVs/SQL):

- `infusionDrug` has 252,833 exact `Insulin (units/hr)` rows over 6,241 stays and 12,810 `Insulin 250 Units Sodium Chloride 0.9% 250 ml (units/hr)` rows over 408 stays. Labels in ml/hr, blank/unknown units, units/kg/hr, mg/mcg units, bolus and TPN-with-insulin are excluded.
- `nurseCare` has explicit Nutrition rows: NPO 114,898 rows/9,746 stays; enteral 82,371/2,138; regular diet 42,236/3,987; low-sodium 40,281/3,773; diabetic 29,598/2,857; clear liquids 19,067/3,348; calorie-controlled 8,508/1,012; TPN 6,111/203; enteral-and-IV 2,709/328.
- `lab` has 3,175,835 `bedside glucose` rows/130,639 stays and 1,319,496 `glucose` rows/189,702 stays, both mg/dL. Both are required.
- A bounded eligibility audit using a fed-state row followed within 12 hours by NPO, entry lag <=60 minutes, adult status, six remaining ICU hours, and positive units/hour insulin within 120 minutes found 425 interruption anchors from 312 stays/290 people in seven hospitals and 13,862 continuation anchors from 1,739 stays/1,446 people in 12 hospitals. After requiring pre-anchor glucose >=70 and at least one post-anchor glucose, there were 353 interruption anchors with 16 level-1 and five level-2 outcomes, versus 11,557 continuation anchors with 229 and 54. These are feasibility counts, not adjusted findings.
- Hospital 420 contributed 328/353 evaluable interruption anchors and all 16 observed post-interruption level-1 events. The effect therefore cannot honestly be called multi-hospital. Primary estimation is restricted to a hospital selected by exposure support alone: >=100 eligible interruption and >=500 continuation anchors, evaluated before outcome counts (the audit identifies hospital 420). Other hospitals are descriptive external-support checks.
- Of a less restrictive positive-insulin anchor frame, 753/785 interruptions had two creatinines in 48 hours and 106 met the provisional rise rule; renal trajectory is feasible.
- Enteral/enteral-and-IV-only sensitivity retained 257 evaluable interruptions, 12 level-1 and four level-2 outcomes. It distinguishes tube feeding from the broader documented-carbohydrate claim.
- Rescue administration is not reliably complete: explicit D10/glucagon infusion labels are sparse, while dextrose/glucagon `medication` rows are orders. Rescue analyses are timing diagnostics, not adjustment proving causality.

The observed crude counts must not be reported as hypothesis results. They were used only to establish support and reveal hospital concentration.

## Population, anchors, and temporal boundaries

Use adults age >=18 (`> 89` -> 90), first ICU visit `unitvisitnumber == 1`, with transition time `T >= 360` minutes, `unitdischargeoffset >= T+360`, a pre-anchor glucose >=70 available in [T-120,T], and at least one glucose in (T,T+360]. Keep repeated anchors; group all rows for a `uniquepid` in one split and cluster inference by patient and stay.

A nutrition state is a `nurseCare` row where `celllabel='Nutrition'` and `cellattribute='Nutrition'`, using `nursecareoffset` as clinical time and requiring `abs(nursecareentryoffset-nursecareoffset)<=60`. Freeze a clinician-reviewed exact state map before outcomes. Primary carbohydrate-present states are enteral, enteral and IV, regular diet, clear liquids, full liquids, calorie controlled, diabetic diet, renal diet, low sodium diet, and cardiac diet. TPN/PPN are excluded from primary analysis because composition/delivery is uncertain; include in a separately adjudicated sensitivity. Unmapped state values are unknown.

An interruption anchor is a carbohydrate-present state followed 1–720 minutes later by explicit NPO. A continuation anchor is a carbohydrate-present state followed 1–720 minutes later by another carbohydrate-present state. The later row defines T. Do not infer state between distant rows beyond 12 hours; no row, late entry, or a gap is unknown—not NPO. A secondary high-specificity analysis uses enteral/enteral-and-IV only.

Active insulin requires the last `infusionDrug` row at or before T to have `drugname` containing insulin and an explicit `units/hr` label, finite `drugrate >0`, and age <=120 minutes. Require a second insulin chart within the prior six hours to reject isolated entries. Exclude labels containing bolus, TPN, units/kg, ml/hr, mg or mcg. A zero rate is an observed stop, never a dose. The primary comparison is restricted to common support of prior glucose (70–300), insulin rate, time since last rate, ICU day, and renal trajectory.

Primary endpoint: first `labname in {'glucose','bedside glucose'}`, mg/dL, <70 in (T,T+360]. Severe endpoint: <54. Report 0–2, 2–4 and 4–6-hour cumulative incidence. A result is available only at `max(labresultoffset, nonmissing labresultrevisedoffset)`; the clinical event time remains `labresultoffset`. Exclude implausible <=10 or >1000 values and exact duplicate `labid`; retain simultaneous lab/bedside conflicts for adjudication sensitivity (minimum versus venous-only).

Renal trajectory uses all numeric creatinine values available by T in [T-2880,T]. Primary continuous features are latest value, 48-hour slope, absolute change and ratio from first to last. The prespecified modifier is >=0.3 mg/dL absolute rise or >=50% relative rise with >=2 values. This is an observed creatinine trajectory, not KDIGO AKI: baseline, urine output and dialysis timing are incomplete.

## Exact read-only bindings

All are ordinary gzip CSVs under `[private path]`; join on `patientunitstayid`.

1. `patient.csv.gz`, table `patient`, SHA-256 `2acf25f75144c5fc8a2a5b68c6741edac2dc7ca51021127f73e12f7428dc392b`: `patientunitstayid`, `uniquepid`, `patienthealthsystemstayid`, `hospitalid`, `age`, `gender`, `ethnicity`, `unitvisitnumber`, `unittype`, `unitadmitsource`, `unitstaytype`, `apacheadmissiondx`, `unitdischargeoffset`, discharge status/location.
2. `infusionDrug.csv.gz`, `infusionDrug`, `f1c958b92a676b932626638f52d0cd5bb13fa53bf5a0ec25606ff4beefc9fc3b`: row key `infusiondrugid`; time `infusionoffset`; `drugname`, `drugrate`, `infusionrate`, `drugamount`, `volumeoffluid`, `patientweight`. It supplies charted rate states; no end time or independent pump confirmation exists.
3. `nurseCare.csv.gz`, `nurseCare`, `c4981a382bd19ad537a07c245655d5a37990bb3e36542cbadff0f505b44c448f`: row key `nursecareid`; times `nursecareoffset`, `nursecareentryoffset`; `celllabel`, `cellattributepath`, `cellattribute`, `cellattributevalue`. This supplies explicit states, not delivered calories.
4. `lab.csv.gz`, `lab`, `91b55ed330015d31c424499cdae3b68e3b4cfe0c10e542548b5461520d93bc7a`: row key `labid`; times `labresultoffset`, `labresultrevisedoffset`; `labname`, `labresult`, `labresulttext`, `labmeasurenamesystem`, `labmeasurenameinterface`. Supplies glucose and creatinine.
5. `medication.csv.gz`, `medication`, `3d504b48375e264a47799ed6a5ea2328f7fc6f776395b5d6738693f69810ebc5`: row key `medicationid`; `drugorderoffset`, `drugstartoffset`, `drugstopoffset`, `drugordercancelled`, `drugname`, `dosage`, `routeadmin`, `frequency`, `prn`. Audit/order covariates only; never exposure or delivered rescue.
6. `intakeOutput.csv.gz`, `intakeOutput`, `f809b425ea89b25c735fa8a7486e204717a3bb4d5f256af0170318ce9baa5121`: row key `intakeoutputid`; `intakeoutputoffset`, `intakeoutputentryoffset`, `cellpath`, `celllabel`, `cellvaluenumeric`, `cellvaluetext`. Corroborates actual intake/flush/residual; absence cannot denote interruption.
7. `carePlanGeneral.csv.gz`, `carePlanGeneral`, `6bc1b6959c5a7666156a52cfff3c8ee2b02ec1d1859d2bb44f5fb405d6f33aa6`: row key `cplgeneralid`; `cplitemoffset`, `cplgroup`, `cplitemvalue`, `activeupondischarge`. Route-Status NPO/enteral is corroborative.
8. `apachePatientResult.csv.gz`, `apachePatientResult`, `f9870a5ad58b1519cf07f51cbe2717a8bf390f74159e2310e2bac3b6bb7a070a`: one audited IVa row; `acutephysiologyscore`, `apachescore`, `apacheversion`. Admission severity only.
9. `apacheApsVar.csv.gz`, `apacheApsVar`, `4dfa6d3d36c3f9a1853027e0ca84668cd6dd4dfae24c330e0ceae324cbfc41b4`: `dialysis`, `urine`, `vent`, `intubated`, admission creatinine/BUN/glucose; -1 is missing. Untimed, so sensitivity/baseline only.
10. `carePlanEOL.csv.gz`, `carePlanEOL`, `8c776d15fd944507c0b57e3e7974db03ad87ac435d27b3f406b3d1afd046ecb0`: `cpleolid`, `cpleolsaveoffset`, `cpleoldiscussionoffset`, `activeupondischarge`; pre-T EOL discussion is an exclusion/sensitivity.

The full catalog and headers were inspected. Narrative notes are unavailable in public eICU; structured fields remain. Sources stay read-only; all derived files stay in the workspace.

## Transparent baseline and estimand

Primary hospital: hospital meeting support thresholds selected without outcomes. For the prespecified baseline estimand, use all eligible primary-hospital anchors; no outcome-driven variable selection is allowed. Estimate coefficients and uncertainty with a patient-cluster bootstrap, and evaluate optimism with 10-fold grouped cross-fitting by `uniquepid`, stratified by ICU day and transition type. The temporal alternative uses the same ten frozen folds for out-of-fold predictions, tuning only within each training fold. Repeated anchors are allowed; a first-eligible-anchor-per-stay sensitivity removes informative repetition.

Fit pooled discrete-time complementary-log-log hazards in six one-hour intervals. Covariates available at T: interruption, hour since T, their interaction; restricted cubic splines for latest glucose, glucose slope and time since glucose; insulin rate, rate slope/AUC and time since rate; creatinine latest/change/slope; ICU day; age/sex; diabetes evidence; APACHE; ventilation/dialysis; corticosteroid and vasopressor evidence; nutrition state; hospital/site is fixed by primary restriction. Include interruption×renal-rise and interruption×post-T insulin-reduction time-varying interactions. The principal estimand is standardized six-hour risk difference and ratio for interruption versus continuation over common-support anchors, with 95% patient-cluster bootstrap CIs. The renal interaction is secondary and must report stratum-specific absolute risks.

A patient fixed-effect conditional logistic/self-controlled sensitivity compares interruption and continuation anchors among the 288 audited stays having both transition types, conditioned on stay and matched on ICU day, prior glucose and insulin rate. It controls time-invariant patient factors but not time-varying severity or monitoring.

Do not condition the primary model on post-T insulin reduction, glucose testing or rescue; they are responses/mediators. Use them only in stratified process analyses.

## Substantive temporal alternative

Fit a landmark discrete-time joint observation/outcome model on the identical anchors, splits, six-hour horizon and inputs. A 16–32-unit GRU (or causal temporal convolution if it wins development log loss) ingests 30-minute bins from T-12 h through T+6 h. Up to T it receives glucose/creatinine values and masks, insulin unit/hour rate and rate-change mask, explicit nutrition state, vitals, vasopressor/corticosteroid indicators and static covariates. After T it receives only insulin rate/stop, nutrition state/resumption and measurement masks—not post-T glucose values—to avoid leaking the outcome. Two heads estimate (a) interval hypoglycemia hazard and (b) glucose-measurement hazard. Inverse-intensity weighting, truncated at 10, is learned from the measurement head; an unweighted model and a joint shared-frailty sensitivity bound informative ascertainment. Five seeds, hidden sizes {16,32}, dropout {0,.2}, learning rates {3e-4,1e-3}, <=100 epochs/patience 10; tune only development/calibration log loss and calibration.

This alternative is scientifically useful only if it improves cross-fitted integrated Brier score/calibration and changes the inferred timing or renal/insulin-adjustment interaction, because the baseline loses ordered rate changes, nonlinear clearance-like accumulation and informative glucose-check timing. A merely higher AUROC does not justify it. Mechanistic PK simulation is deferred: eICU lacks formulation/concentration confirmation, delivered dose and nutrition carbohydrate rate needed to identify insulin action/clearance. Those data would justify revisiting a mechanistic model.

Expected future workload: preprocessing 4 CPU/32 GB for 1–2 h; baseline/bootstrap 8 CPU/32 GB for 2–4 h; temporal model one A100/32 GB host RAM for approximately 1–3 h plus five-seed/bootstrap inference. GPU estimate is unmeasured but well inside the configured envelope; CPU baseline remains mandatory.

## Bias, falsification, and interpretation

- **Order-versus-delivery:** primary insulin comes only from explicit unit/hour `infusionDrug`; `medication` insulin orders are a negative-control exposure. If order-only associations equal primary associations, reject delivery-specific interpretation.
- **Nutrition documentation:** require observed fed→NPO or fed→fed transitions and timely entry. Repeat with <=15-minute entry lag, enteral-only states, corroborating Route-Status/intake rows, and excluding simultaneous contradictory states. Missing remains unknown.
- **Reverse timing:** exclude any glucose <70 or dextrose/glucagon order/infusion in [T-120,T]; test pseudo-anchors at T-6 h and T+6 h. An effect preceding NPO or disappearing after entry-lag restriction supports reverse timing/documentation artifact.
- **Monitoring:** report testing probability, delay and counts by group; use measurement-hazard weighting and best/worst-case bounds for unobserved outcomes. If interruption predicts testing but not hypoglycemia under supported ascertainment, reject the biological hazard claim.
- **Renal severity:** adjust dynamic creatinine continuously; report APACHE/dialysis/urine and shock sensitivities. The interaction must be directionally stable and not wholly driven by dialysis or baseline severe illness.
- **Insulin response:** report insulin reduction/zero within 30/60/120 minutes. A hazard concentrated where insulin stays positive is supportive of a preventable mismatch; attenuation after prompt reduction is not causal proof because clinicians select actions.
- **Rescue:** medication dextrose/glucagon is order-only and D10/glucagon infusion capture is sparse. Post-T rescue is a positive-control consequence; pre-T rescue triggers exclusion. No claim of rescue effectiveness.
- **Hospital concentration:** primary is within hospital 420 selected by support. Other sites are descriptive. Failure to reproduce direction in any adequately supported future site is adverse to generalization.

Support requires: cross-fitted standardized six-hour risk higher after interruption with a two-sided 95% CI excluding zero; no pre-anchor/pseudo-anchor association; acceptable overlap and calibration; direction maintained under timely-entry, enteral-only and monitoring bounds; and renal stratum estimates compatible with a larger excess under rising creatinine. The renal interaction CI may include zero and is then inconclusive, not disproved.

Adverse results include no excess with sufficiently narrow CI (exclude >=3 percentage-point risk difference), an effect before rather than after T, disappearance under timely/corroborated documentation, order-only equivalence, or an association explained by measurement probability. Any of these rejects the corresponding hazard/interpretation even if another model predicts well.

Inconclusive results include fewer than 10 primary interruption outcomes overall, CI spanning both zero and +3 points, positivity failure, unstable hospital support, high model-seed variation, or discordant ascertainment bounds. The audit suggests sparsity is likely; severe <54 is descriptive unless support increases.

## Outputs and verifier limits

Required machine-readable outputs: source hashes; exact state/unit maps; row-exclusion flow; anchor/patient/hospital counts before outcomes; interval event/testing/rescue counts; overlap diagnostics; split manifest; fitted baseline and temporal artifacts; per-anchor predictions; clustered bootstrap estimates; calibration/Brier/AUROC; self-controlled results; all sensitivity/falsification tables; and `conclusion.json` labeling overall and renal claims as supportive/adverse/inconclusive with direct output keys.

Automatic verification can check hashes, joins, time inequalities, no use of medication orders as exposure, positive explicit-unit rates, explicit transitions, no missing-as-NPO, outcome thresholds, split isolation, recomputed metrics/CIs and whether conclusion labels follow prespecified rules. It cannot establish that charted rates were delivered, NPO timing equals carbohydrate cessation, unrecorded rescue was absent, residual severity/clinician intent was controlled, or an alert is safe. Those need chart/pump/dietary review, clinical experts, prospective validation and another hospital.

## References

[K1] Mahmoodpoor A, et al. *Predisposing Factors for Hypoglycemia and Its Relation With Mortality in Critically Ill Patients Undergoing Insulin Therapy in an Intensive Care Unit.* Anesth Pain Med. 2016;6:e33849. doi:10.5812/aapm.33849. Full text inspected.

[K2] Kolanczyk DM, Dobersztyn RC. *Challenges With Insulin in the Inpatient Setting.* Diabetes Spectr. 2016;29:146–152. doi:10.2337/diaspect.29.3.146. Full text inspected.

[K3] Ni K, et al. *Safety and Efficacy of Insulins in Critically Ill Patients Receiving Continuous Enteral Nutrition.* Endocr Pract. 2024;30:367–371. doi:10.1016/j.eprac.2024.01.009. Abstract only inspected.


# Executable task contract

This package asks you to execute the complete frozen investigation above, not merely repeat the feasibility audit or train a predictor. No reference solution, fitted model, or final scientific result is supplied. The audit counts in this document are support checks and must not be copied as study findings. Newly construct every anchor, freeze outcome-blind mappings and patient-grouped folds, fit both model families, quantify uncertainty, run every named falsification/sensitivity analysis, and report conclusions that follow from your computed outputs. An adverse or inconclusive result is a valid completion.

## Runtime data and additional frozen input realization

The ten sources listed above are mounted read-only at `/data/<filename>`. The temporal alternative's already-specified vital inputs are realized mechanically by one additional ordinary-gzip binding:

## Required implementation and resource envelope

The planned envelope is at most 16 CPU cores, 262,144 MiB host RAM, eight GPUs and eight hours. The GPU estimate is unmeasured. Use `cuda:0` when one GPU is allocated; do not select physical GPU IDs. The CPU baseline remains mandatory. Resource use is not evidence for scientific value.

`submission.json` must use schema `eicu-nutrition-interruption-v1`, state `status: "complete"`, record the exact source SHA-256 values, and map every required artifact below to its relative path, byte SHA-256 and byte size. It must also record analysis-code files and hashes, software versions, random seeds, bootstrap replicate count, runtime/resource summary, and whether CUDA was used. A completed submission must contain:

- `results/state_map.json`: exact clinician-reviewed nutrition map frozen before outcome modeling, with primary fed, NPO, excluded parenteral and unknown values.
- `results/unit_map.json`: exact included and excluded insulin-label rules and encountered-label counts.
- `results/exclusion_flow.csv`: ordered cohort/anchor exclusions with remaining anchors, stays and people, before outcomes wherever required.
- `results/counts.csv`: transition, outcome, testing and rescue counts by primary/external hospital, exposure and interval.
- `results/anchors.csv.gz`: one row per eligible anchor, retaining source row IDs and times needed to audit patient eligibility, explicit prior/current nutrition states, two insulin charts, pre-anchor glucose, post-anchor ascertainment, outcomes, renal trajectory, hospital, fold and common-support/analysis flags. Required columns are `anchor_id,patientunitstayid,uniquepid,hospitalid,T,exposure,prev_nursecareid,prev_nutrition_time,prev_nutrition_value,anchor_nursecareid,anchor_nutrition_time,anchor_nutrition_value,insulin_row_id,insulin_time,insulin_drugname,insulin_rate,prior_insulin_row_id,prior_insulin_time,pre_glucose_labid,pre_glucose_time,pre_glucose_value,first_post_labid,first_post_time,first_post_value,primary_outcome,severe_outcome,first_hypo_labid,first_hypo_time,first_hypo_value,latest_creatinine,creatinine_abs_change,creatinine_ratio,creatinine_slope,renal_rise,split_fold,common_support,analysis_included`.

- `results/models/baseline.json`: fitted baseline specification, coefficients, fold/tuning metadata and preprocessing parameters.
- `results/models/temporal.pt`: temporal model checkpoint or checkpoint bundle.
- `results/code_manifest.json`: entry point and SHA-256 for all submitted analysis files used to produce results.
- `results/conclusion.json`: overall and renal claim labels, each one of `supportive`, `adverse`, or `inconclusive`, plus component claim labels for timing, delivery specificity, documentation robustness, ascertainment robustness and generalizability. Every reason must cite keys in `estimates.json` or another required output. Distinguish association, prediction and causation.

Do not report the severe <54 endpoint as confirmatory unless support has increased enough to escape the frozen descriptive limitation. Do not call hospital 420 multi-hospital evidence. Do not interpret a better AUROC as evidence of mechanism or as sufficient justification for the temporal model.

## Computable evaluation and conclusion discipline

The evaluator can recompute artifact hashes, source/anchor time inequalities, explicit state transitions, positive unit/hour insulin rules, duplicate handling, patient-fold isolation, prediction-derived standardized risks, bootstrap intervals and reported metrics. It will deterministically spot-check source row IDs against the mounted gzip CSVs. It rejects missing-as-NPO logic, medication-order exposure, post-`T` glucose leakage, outcome-informed site/state/split selection, copied feasibility counts presented as adjusted results, malformed/canned artifacts, internally inconsistent uncertainty, or conclusions unsupported by the computed diagnostics.

For the overall short-horizon claim, `supportive` is permitted only when all frozen support conditions hold. A narrow estimate that excludes an increase of at least 0.03, reverse/pseudo timing, disappearance under timely/corroborated documentation, order-only equivalence, or ascertainment explanation is adverse to the corresponding claim even when prediction is good. Fewer than ten interruption outcomes, an interval spanning both 0 and +0.03, positivity failure, unstable hospital support, high seed variation or discordant ascertainment bounds makes the relevant claim inconclusive. If adverse and imprecision conditions coexist, label components separately and justify the overall label without converting imprecision into proof of no effect. The renal interaction is inconclusive when its interval includes zero unless another prespecified adverse criterion directly falsifies that component; absence of significance is not evidence of no modification.

Passing mechanical checks does not establish that charted insulin was delivered, that the NPO timestamp equals carbohydrate cessation, that unrecorded rescue was absent, that residual severity/intent was controlled, or that an alert is safe. Those require pump/dietary/chart adjudication, clinical review, prospective validation and an adequately supported second hospital.

## Frozen key references and public locators

[K1] Mahmoodpoor A, Hamishehkar H, Beigmohammadi M, et al. *Predisposing Factors for Hypoglycemia and Its Relation With Mortality in Critically Ill Patients Undergoing Insulin Therapy in an Intensive Care Unit.* 2016. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.5812/aapm.33849).

[K2] Kolanczyk DM, Dobersztyn RC. *Challenges With Insulin in the Inpatient Setting.* 2016. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.2337/diaspect.29.3.146).

[K3] Ni K, Hawkins RM, Smyth HL, et al. *Safety and Efficacy of Insulins in Critically Ill Patients Receiving Continuous Enteral Nutrition.* 2024. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.eprac.2024.01.009). Only the abstract was inspected for the frozen mapping.


### Required decision fields

For deterministic checking, `results/estimates.json` must contain these exact finite numeric/boolean fields (additional fields are encouraged): `primary.baseline.risk_interruption`, `risk_continuation`, `risk_difference`, `risk_ratio`, `ci_low`, `ci_high`; `primary.temporal` with the same fields; `primary.interruption_outcomes`; and `diagnostics.no_pre_or_pseudo_association`, `acceptable_overlap`, `acceptable_calibration`, `direction_timely_entry`, `direction_enteral_only`, `direction_monitoring_bounds`, `renal_direction_larger`, `narrow_excludes_rd_ge_0_03`, `reverse_timing_failure`, `documentation_failure`, `order_only_equivalence`, `ascertainment_explains`, `fewer_than_10_interruption_outcomes`, `ci_spans_zero_and_0_03`, `positivity_failure`, `unstable_hospital_support`, `high_seed_variation`, `discordant_ascertainment_bounds`, and `renal_interaction_ci_includes_zero`. Each diagnostic must also have a same-named entry under `diagnostic_evidence` containing `artifact` and `key`.

The verifier derives the overall label conservatively. Overall is `supportive` only if the baseline primary interval excludes zero in the positive direction and all seven support booleans (`no_pre_or_pseudo_association` through `renal_direction_larger`) are true, with no adverse or overall-claim inconclusive boolean true. Renal-interaction imprecision alone does not make the overall claim inconclusive. It is `inconclusive` if any overall-claim inconclusive boolean is true, even when a separately labeled component is adverse. Otherwise, if any prespecified adverse boolean is true or `narrow_excludes_rd_ge_0_03` is true, overall is `adverse`. Remaining patterns are `inconclusive`. Renal is `inconclusive` whenever `renal_interaction_ci_includes_zero` is true; otherwise it may be supportive only when its interaction direction is larger and its interval excludes zero, and is adverse only when a prespecified renal falsification is represented in `sensitivities.json`. This rule prevents a nonsignificant or imprecise estimate from being called adverse evidence. Component labels must still expose decisive timing, documentation, delivery-specificity, ascertainment, and generalizability failures.

`results/conclusion.json` must contain `schema: "eicu-nutrition-conclusion-v1"`, `overall.label`, `renal.label`, and `components` entries named `timing`, `delivery_specificity`, `documentation_robustness`, `ascertainment_robustness`, and `generalizability`; every claim object has `label`, `reason`, and a nonempty `evidence` list of objects with `artifact` and `key`. The conclusion must include `causal_claim: false`, `alert_ready: false`, and the stated adjudication/validation limitations.


Minimum tabular schemas not already enumerated are: `exclusion_flow.csv` has `stage,anchors,stays,people`; `counts.csv` has `hospitalid,exposure,interval,anchors,events,tested`; `overlap.csv` has `analysis,exposure,n,common_support_n`; and `model_metrics.csv` has `model,seed,split,metric,value`.
