# Residual instability before ICU-to-ward transfer: separable evidence contract

## Objective and evidence boundary

Determine whether final-24-hour physiologic value history adds held-out, decision-time information about 48-hour deterioration after ICU-to-general-ward transfer beyond a strong endpoint snapshot and observation-process context. Newly fit and evaluate S0, T1, O1, GRU-D L1, and two-stream TCN L2. No hypothesis result is supplied.

The strongest inspected evidence is bounded: a recent study found a longitudinal GRU-D++ model outperformed SWIFT for seven-day ICU readmission/death but did not isolate short-timescale trajectory information from operational factors or composite components [K1]; a systematic review found value in explicit outcomes, homogeneous cohorts, and longitudinal routine predictors while documenting heterogeneous definitions [K2]; and measurement timing/frequency can itself encode healthcare-process signal [K3]. The unresolved claim is whether prespecified value history adds 48-hour information in this fixed transfer cohort after enforcing prospective availability and separating value, order, observation-process, clinical-materiality, and endpoint-component evidence.

This is prognostic and measurement-discrimination research. Association, ablation, or model performance cannot establish biological instability, preventability, benefit from delaying transfer or adding monitoring, plannedness of ICU return, expected death, adequacy of ward resources, or transportability.

## Private input and exact bindings

The only runtime binding is read-only `/data/mimic-iv-3.1.zip`, SHA-256 `0dd448e341f489483194daafd884607d6f194648c6bf54eed56d1e2cd2af9e09`, size 10,551,747,784 bytes (MIMIC-IV core 3.1). Never modify it or copy it into the image. Use these exact members:

| Table | Archive member | Required columns / temporal use |
|---|---|---|
| `icu/icustays` | `mimic-iv-3.1/icu/icustays.csv.gz` | `[internal identifier],[internal identifier],[internal identifier],first_careunit,last_careunit,intime,outtime,los`; `[internal identifier]` and `[internal identifier],[internal identifier]`; `outtime=t0` |
| `hosp/transfers` | `mimic-iv-3.1/hosp/transfers.csv.gz` | `[internal identifier],[internal identifier],transfer_id,eventtype,careunit,intime,outtime`; exact successor and later path |
| `hosp/admissions` | `mimic-iv-3.1/hosp/admissions.csv.gz` | `[internal identifier],[internal identifier],admittime,dischtime,deathtime,admission_type,discharge_location,hospital_expire_flag` |
| `hosp/patients` | `mimic-iv-3.1/hosp/patients.csv.gz` | `[internal identifier],gender,anchor_age,anchor_year,anchor_year_group,dod`; `dod` is not primary death time |
| `hosp/services` | `mimic-iv-3.1/hosp/services.csv.gz` | `[internal identifier],[internal identifier],transfertime,prev_service,curr_service`; latest `transfertime <= t0` |
| `icu/chartevents` | `mimic-iv-3.1/icu/chartevents.csv.gz` | `[internal identifier],[internal identifier],[internal identifier],caregiver_id,charttime,storetime,itemid,value,valuenum,valueuom,warning`; join `[internal identifier]`; primary predictors require `charttime` in `[t0-24h,t0)` and `storetime<t0` |
| `icu/d_items` | `mimic-iv-3.1/icu/d_items.csv.gz` | `itemid,label,abbreviation,linksto,category,unitname,param_type`; exact assertions |
| `icu/inputevents` | `mimic-iv-3.1/icu/inputevents.csv.gz` | `[internal identifier],[internal identifier],[internal identifier],starttime,endtime,storetime,itemid,amount,amountuom,rate,rateuom,statusdescription`; interval overlap and `storetime<t0` |
| `icu/procedureevents` | `mimic-iv-3.1/icu/procedureevents.csv.gz` | `[internal identifier],[internal identifier],[internal identifier],starttime,endtime,storetime,itemid,statusdescription`; interval overlap and `storetime<t0` |

Frozen IDs: HR 220045; invasive/noninvasive SBP 220050/220179; invasive/noninvasive MAP 220052/220181; RR 220210; SpO2 220277; temperature F/C 223761/223762; O2 flow 223834; FiO2 223835; O2 device 226732; GCS 220739/223900/223901; code status 223758; invasive ventilation 225792; vasopressors 221289/229617, 221662, 221749/229630/229631/229632, 221906, 222315. Assert exact `d_items` metadata before fitting; never expand by fuzzy matching. Write observed metadata to `item_dictionary.csv`.

Discharge notes are not bound and are prohibited predictors. True plannedness, transfer intent, expected death, and goals of care require future blinded dual-clinician note adjudication.

## Frozen population, landmark, and outcome

The unit is each hospitalization's first eligible transfer. A subject may contribute multiple hospitalizations, but every admission for one subject remains in one split and bootstrap cluster.

For each ICU stay, set `t0=icustays.outtime` and require an exact successor row joined on `[internal identifier],[internal identifier]` with `transfers.intime=t0`. Require age `anchor_age + year(icustays.intime) - anchor_year >= 18`; `los >= 1.0` day; `deathtime` null or greater than `t0`; destination in the primary set; and earliest eligible row by `outtime,[internal identifier]` within `[internal identifier]`.

Primary destinations: `Medicine`, `Neurology`, `Med/Surg`, `Medicine/Cardiology`, `Transplant`, `Vascular`, `Med/Surg/GYN`, `Surgery/Trauma`, `Med/Surg/Trauma`, `Surgery`, `Cardiac Surgery`, `Medical/Surgical (Gynecology)`, `Surgery/Pancreatic/Biliary/Bariatric`, `Cardiology`, `Thoracic Surgery`, `Oncology`, `Hematology/Oncology`.

The step-down sensitivity adds separate strata: `Cardiology Surgery Intermediate`, `Hematology/Oncology Intermediate`, `Medicine/Cardiology Intermediate`, `Neuro Intermediate`, `Neuro Stepdown`, `Surgery/Vascular/Intermediate`, `Surgical Intermediate`. Exclude every other successor destination from the primary cohort.

The exposure is `[t0-24h,t0)`; the outcome window is `(t0,t0+48h]`. Determine the earliest post-`t0` transition among same-admission later ICU `intime`, `admissions.deathtime`, and live `admissions.dischtime`. States are deterioration (ICU return or death first), live discharge first, and alive/in-hospital no event. Preserve raw timestamps and chronology conflicts in `endpoint_chronology.csv`; never relabel after prediction inspection. Report ICU return/death separately with matched four-state S0c/T1c models and cumulative incidence.

Reproduce 49,157 index transfers and audit 2,607 raw unique ICU-return/death events within 48 hours before fitting. These are feasibility checks, not hypothesis results; report discrepancies rather than forcing counts.

## Frozen features

Use twelve left-closed two-hour bins; continuous bin values are medians. Prefer invasive BP and preserve source. Plausibility: HR 20–250, SBP 40–300, MAP 20–200, RR 4–80, SpO2 50–100, temperature 30–43 °C after Fahrenheit conversion, oxygen flow 0–100 L/min, FiO2 0.21–1.0 after converting values >1 and <=100 by 100. Report rejects; no data-dependent winsorization.

Abnormal states: HR <50 or >110; SBP <90 or MAP <65; RR <10 or >24; SpO2 <92%; temperature <36.0 or >38.3 °C; elevated oxygen support (FiO2 >0.30, flow >4 L/min, or exact device mapping to high-flow, reservoir/face-mask, noninvasive positive-pressure, or invasive-airway). Missing oxygen is unknown, never room air. Freeze `oxygen_device_dictionary.csv` before test opening with every normalized item-226732 value, count, exact mapping, and unmapped values; fuzzy expansion is forbidden.

For each channel construct abnormal observed-bin fraction; longest abnormal run (missing breaks run); normal↔abnormal transitions; 90th–10th percentile range; median absolute successive difference; Theil–Sen slope; early-12h minus late-12h median; worst and final-four-hour values; observed-bin/record counts; recency; and missing-bin fraction. Scale volatility on training only. Features needing <4 observed bins are missing plus indicator. Report persistence bounds treating missing as normal/abnormal only as uncertainty diagnostics.

Trajectory burden is the mean over six domains (HR, BP, RR, SpO2, temperature, oxygen support) of training-empirical percentile ranks for abnormal fraction, longest run/12, median absolute successive difference, and transitions/11, equally weighted. Require four covered domains; learn quartiles on training only.

Preserve masks, counts, distinct chart hours, recency, median/IQR store lag, and caregiver count. Primary chart predictors require both event time and decision availability before `t0`. Charttime-only is a labeled retrospective sensitivity; late-store counts are audits, never predictors.

Map last decision-time code status to full-code, DNR/DNI, comfort-measures-only, other, or undocumented; undocumented is not full code. Include no-treatment-limitation and full-code sensitivities. Ventilation/vasopressors require final-24h overlap and `storetime<t0`; exclude `Rewritten`, and require positive rate or amount for inputs. Also use destination, source ICU, latest service, ICU LOS, prior ICU count, admission type, transfer hour/night (19:00–06:59). Do not use day of week.

## Models on one question

Use subject-level 60/20/20 train/validation/test splitting, seed 20260923, stratified by any qualifying outcome and dominant destination group. Define rare-stratum handling before test opening, record it, and preserve approximate fractions. Train/validation alone fit preprocessing, imputation, splines, categories, hyperparameters, stopping, and calibration. Open test once.

- **S0:** ridge multinomial logistic regression with age, sex, admission type, source/last ICU, destination, latest service, ICU LOS, prior ICU count, transfer hour/night, last value and four-hour freshness per channel, last GCS, recent ventilation/vasopressor state, code status, and all density/process variables. Use training-fitted restricted cubic splines for prespecified nonlinear continuous terms and training medians plus indicators.
- **T1:** S0 plus only persistence, run, transition, volatility, slope, early/late, and worst-value features. Select penalty on validation log loss.
- **O1:** static transfer context plus decision-time masks/counts/recency/store-lag/caregiver counts, no measured values.
- **L1:** compact GRU-D on the same 12 bins plus identical static context; layers {1,2}, hidden {32,64}, dropout {0,0.2}, Adam LR {1e-3,3e-4}, validation early stopping and temperature scaling, five fixed seeds.
- **L2:** separate value and process causal TCNs plus S0 static context. Value stream has standardized observed/forward-filled values, no mask/gap. Process has masks, gaps, counts, decision-time lag summaries and caregiver counts, no values. Two causal layers, kernel 3, dilations 1/2, channels {32,64}, dropout {0,0.2}, Adam LR {1e-3,3e-4}, five fixed seeds, validation-only selection/calibration.

Mandatory L2 test contrasts: full vs process+static; full vs value+static; value+static vs S0; full vs T1. For order permutation keep final bin fixed and apply one shared permutation of preceding 11 bins across all value channels per person; average 20 frozen permutations. Also permute complete patient value sequences within destination, S0-risk decile, and density quintile. Record seeds. Repeat in dense core-vital, no-treatment-limitation, daytime, and charttime-only strata.

S0/T1 is the simple interpretable baseline. L1 may reveal nonlinear duration/lag. L2 separates value, process, and order information that T1 loses. A joint latent physiology/observation model is deferred because separation is not identifiable here; revisit with continuous-monitor, staffing/policy, adjudicated, or external data.

## Estimands, uncertainty, and interpretation

Primary: paired test binary deterioration-class Brier reduction `mean((y-pS0)^2)-mean((y-pT1)^2)`. Also estimate standardized top-vs-bottom burden risk difference and T1-vs-L1 Brier reduction. Report multinomial log loss, AUROC/AUPRC, calibration intercept/slope/plots, component Brier contrasts, cumulative incidence, and decision-curve net benefit at 2%, 5%, 10%. Report movements/counts for risk categories `<2%`, `2–<5%`, `5–<10%`, `>=10%`. Use exactly 2,000 subject-cluster percentile bootstrap replicates, seed 20260924, so uncertainty is replayable. Use Benjamini–Hochberg for secondary coefficient families; no univariate screening.

Report four axes:

1. **A—incremental information.** Supported iff Brier gain >0 with 95% CI entirely >0, T1 calibration slope 0.8–1.2, and no leakage/readiness failure. Falsified at material bound iff CI upper <0.002 with >=200 test deterioration events, <=30% inadequate core coverage, valid calibration, and no leakage. Otherwise inconclusive.
2. **B—clinical materiality.** Supported only when uncertainty does not straddle 0.002, gain >=0.002, T1 incremental net benefit is positive at >=2 thresholds, fixed category/count outputs exist, and calibration permits decision analysis. Not demonstrated when A is supported but a criterion fails with adequate precision. Inconclusive when uncertainty straddles a decision bound or calibration invalidates analysis. Burden contrast >=2 percentage points with CI >0 is corroborative, not required.
3. **C—source/order.** Flags may overlap. Value-history contribution requires T1>S0 and L2 full>process with CIs >0 and >50% attenuation under patient value permutation. Order contribution requires full L2 > mean order-permuted L2 with CI >0. Process-dominant requires process/static retain >=50% of static-to-full improvement while value additions include zero. Mixed requires independently positive process and value additions. None proves biology.
4. **D—endpoint validity.** Component-consistent requires favorable Brier direction/risk ordering for ICU return and death without PACU-proxy or treatment-limit reversal. Component-specific means one carries gain. Endpoint-ambiguous means conflicting direction or frozen sensitivity reversal. Otherwise inconclusive. Clinical adjudication is always required before planned/expected/preventable labels.

Overall supportive requires A supported and must qualify B/C/D. Overall adverse is allowed only when precision rules out 0.002 or value history adds nothing beyond S0/process. Overall inconclusive is required for insufficient precision, leakage, invalid calibration, inadequate events/coverage, or unresolved endpoint reversal. Negative/inconclusive results still complete the task.

## Required deliverables

Write derived files under `/workspace/results`; sources remain read-only. `analysis_manifest.json` maps these exact relative paths to SHA-256 hashes:

- `cohort_flow.csv`, `index_transfers.parquet`, `endpoint_chronology.csv`
- `item_dictionary.csv`, `oxygen_device_dictionary.csv`, `availability_audit.json`
- `subject_split.csv`, `preprocessing_manifest.json`, `model_manifest.json`
- `test_predictions.parquet`, `bootstrap_replicates.parquet`, `primary_metrics.json`
- `decision_curve.csv`, `component_metrics.json`, `sensitivity_metrics.json`
- `l2_ablation_metrics.json`, `interpretation_axes.json`, `conclusion.json`, `conclusion.md`
- executable analysis entrypoint and plan under `code/`; five L1 and five L2 checkpoints listed in `model_manifest.json`

`index_transfers.parquet` includes identifiers, `t0`, destination, age, raw event times, first transition, outcome state/component, and coverage. `subject_split.csv` has unique `[internal identifier],split`. `test_predictions.parquet` has one row/test transfer with identifiers, outcome, and calibrated three-state probabilities (deterioration/discharge/no-event) for S0, T1, O1, L1, L2; probabilities are finite, [0,1], and sum to one. Include row-level variant predictions sufficient for every paired contrast.

`bootstrap_replicates.parquet` has 2,000 replayable cluster-bootstrap estimates. JSON metrics contain points, CIs, denominators, event/coverage/calibration/leakage gates, seeds, and evidence paths. `interpretation_axes.json` states A–D and overall before narrative. `conclusion.json` lists each claim, scope (`prognostic`, `measurement`, `clinical_materiality`, or `endpoint_validity`), and evidence paths. `conclusion.md` is generated from those claims and explicitly states non-computable limitations.

The verifier checks source headers/item mappings; output hashes/schemas; cohort/split/probability/leakage invariants; metric recalculation; bootstrap interval construction; status-threshold consistency; and evidence-linked conclusions. It cannot certify model quality, novelty, mechanism, clinical benefit, endpoint intent, or external validity. Those require code review, clinical adjudication, another site, or a prospective study.

Estimated full-study budget (not measured): extraction 8 CPU/64 GiB, 2–4 h; S0/T1/O1/bootstrap 8 CPU/64 GiB, 1–3 h; L1/L2 five seeds one allocated A100 + 8 CPU/64 GiB, 3–6 h. This fits 16 CPU, 262,144 MiB, 8 GPU, 28,800 s. Use `cuda:0` only inside an allocated GPU job. Readiness does not run the study.

## Key bibliography

[K1] Heo Y, Kim M, Han SS, et al. “AI-Driven Predictions of Readmission and Mortality for Improved Discharge Decisions in Critical Care: A Retrospective Study.” *Diagnostics*. 2026;16(6):874. https://doi.org/10.3390/diagnostics16060874

[K2] Ruppert MM, Loftus TJ, Small C, et al. “Predictive Modeling for Readmission to Intensive Care: A Systematic Review.” *Critical Care Explorations*. 2023;5(1):e0848. https://doi.org/10.1097/CCE.0000000000000848

[K3] Agniel D, Kohane IS, Weber GM. “Biases in electronic health record data due to processes within the healthcare system: retrospective observational study.” *BMJ*. 2018;361:k1479. https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj.k1479

# Residual instability before ICU-to-ward transfer: separable evidence contract

Status: proposed substantive child of `candidate-4abe5d75e5aff52a84f62151`; no outcome model has been fit and no hypothesis result is claimed. The fixed population, index transfer, 24-hour exposure window, 48-hour outcome horizon, exact MIMIC-IV 3.1 bindings, S0/T1 comparison, and subject-level split are unchanged.

## Why a child is scientifically necessary

The parent is valid, but its single conjunctive “supportive” label entangles four different questions:

1. Does final-24-hour value history add held-out prognostic information beyond the endpoint snapshot?
2. Is the increment large enough to matter at prespecified clinical decisions?
3. Is the increment attributable to measured-value content and temporal order rather than observation or discharge processes?
4. Is the composite endpoint sufficiently valid for the intended interpretation?

A statistically real but subthreshold increment is neither supportive of clinical materiality nor adverse to incremental information. Likewise, masks-only performance does not erase a separately present value contribution, and a composite gain can conceal opposing ICU-return and death behavior. The parent’s patient-level value permutation tests whether patients’ values matter, but destroys value levels, trajectories, and cross-channel relations simultaneously; it cannot isolate temporal order. GRU-D also learns directly from masks and time gaps, so a GRU-D gain does not distinguish physiology from care process.

A second computability problem is prospective availability. `icu/chartevents` has both `charttime` and `storetime`. Requiring only `charttime < t0` can admit a retrospectively entered record that was unavailable at the transfer decision. The repaired primary analysis therefore requires both `charttime in [t0-24h,t0)` and `storetime < t0` for every chart-derived predictor. The charttime-only analysis remains a clearly labeled retrospective sensitivity. This does not change the biological exposure window; it makes the decision-time information set honest.

## Evidence boundary and unresolved claim

The strongest inspected evidence supports three bounded claims. A 2026 MIMIC-IV/external-hospital study found GRU-D++ discriminated seven-day ICU readmission/death better than SWIFT, while using daily averages and acknowledging unresolved operational factors, DNR status, and composite-component differences [K1]. A systematic review found that higher-performing ICU-readmission models often used homogeneous populations, explicit outcomes, and longitudinal routinely collected predictors, but outcome windows and composite definitions varied [K2]. A large EHR study showed that whether and when measurements occur can predict outcomes independently of values, because records encode healthcare processes as well as physiology [K3].

These works do not establish that short-timescale residual instability in the final 24 hours before a fixed ICU-to-general-ward transfer adds decision-time 48-hour information beyond endpoint state; that any increment is clinically material; that temporal order rather than value distribution or observation policy carries it; or that ICU return and death support the same interpretation.

**Primary falsifiable hypothesis.** In the parent’s fixed cohort, T1’s prespecified value-trajectory features improve held-out 48-hour three-state prediction over S0 after enforcing decision-time availability, and measured-value content adds information beyond the observation process. Clinical materiality and temporal-order dependence are distinct secondary claims and are not required to conclude that incremental prognostic information exists.

This remains a prognostic and measurement-discrimination study. No available automatic analysis can identify a biological mechanism or show that delaying transfer or increasing monitoring helps.

## Frozen population, times, and outcomes

Retain the parent exactly:

- unit: each hospitalization’s first eligible adult ICU-to-frozen-general-ward transfer after ICU LOS >=24 hours;
- `t0 = icu/icustays.outtime`, with exact successor `hosp/transfers.intime = t0` on `[internal identifier],[internal identifier]`;
- frozen general-ward and step-down sensitivity sets unchanged;
- exposure: exactly `[t0-24h,t0)`;
- outcome horizon: `(t0,t0+48h]`;
- outcome: first same-admission later ICU-stay `intime` or `admissions.deathtime`, with live discharge as a competing three-state outcome;
- one split and one bootstrap cluster per `[internal identifier]`.

Retain the parent’s verified feasibility evidence: 49,157 index transfers, 2,607 composite events, and dense core-vital support. These counts establish feasibility, not hypothesis results.\n\nA completed full-`chartevents` availability audit in the 49,157-transfer cohort scanned 7,235,465 selected chart rows. Of these, 2,145 (0.030%) had `storetime >= t0`, including 605 entered at least one hour and 309 at least four hours after transfer. Late entries affected 238–261 stays per core vital channel (counts overlap across channels). The magnitude is too small to presume it explains the trajectory signal, but it proves that charttime-only extraction is not a strictly real-time information set. These are leakage-feasibility counts, not outcome results.

### Endpoint audit and misclassification strata

Do not redefine the primary outcome after examining predictions. Precompute an endpoint chronology table for every positive event:

- ICU-return component, death component, or both; exact first-event time;
- first post-`t0` `hosp/transfers` path and whether the exact `careunit='PACU'` precedes ICU return; `hosp/transfers` contains no operating-room/procedural careunit label, so broader planned/procedural classification is unavailable;
- live discharge time;
- last pre-`t0` code-status class;
- source ICU, destination ward, service, transfer hour/night.

Report four frozen analyses:

1. primary composite;
2. ICU return and death separately, with paired uncertainty from secondary S0c/T1c models using the identical features/split but a four-state first-event target (ICU return, death, live discharge, alive/in-hospital without event);
3. “no observed PACU precursor” ICU return sensitivity;
4. no-treatment-limitation and explicitly-full-code sensitivities.

PACU-predecessor exclusion is an imperfect proxy, not a label of “unplanned.” True plannedness, transfer intent, expected death, and goals of care require blinded clinician note adjudication. Discharge notes are available at `note/discharge.csv.gz` with `[internal identifier],[internal identifier],charttime,storetime,text`, but are prohibited as model inputs; they may support a future stratified validation sample because they are written after the decision and can contain outcomes.

## Decision-time inputs and exact bindings

Read-only archive:
`[private path]`
(SHA-256 `0dd448e341f489483194daafd884607d6f194648c6bf54eed56d1e2cd2af9e09`).

Retain these exact archive members, columns, joins, and item IDs from the parent:

Retain verified mappings: HR 220045; invasive/noninvasive SBP 220050/220179; invasive/noninvasive MAP 220052/220181; RR 220210; SpO2 220277; temperature F/C 223761/223762; O2 flow 223834; FiO2 223835; O2 device 226732; GCS 220739/223900/223901; code status 223758; invasive ventilation 225792; vasopressors 221289/229617, 221662, 221749/229630/229631/229632, 221906, 222315.

For input/procedure context, primary predictors require both interval overlap based on `starttime,endtime` and decision-time availability `storetime < t0`. The parent’s event-time-only definition is retained as a labeled retrospective sensitivity, with discordance reported rather than silently dropping rows.

## Models: same inputs and target, more diagnostic alternative

### S0 and T1

Retain the parent’s ridge multinomial S0 and nested T1 formulas, plausibility rules, two-hour bins, persistence/volatility summaries, training-fitted preprocessing, and identical three-state target. Both models use only decision-time-available records in the primary analysis. S0 already includes measurement density, recency, store lag, caregiver count, endpoint values, support state, transfer context, and code status. T1 adds only the frozen trajectory-value summaries.

The primary incremental estimand remains paired test `Brier(S0)-Brier(T1)`. To avoid confusing explanation with risk contrast, the parent’s adjusted high-versus-low trajectory-burden risk difference is retained as a descriptive standardized association, not evidence that the burden caused deterioration.

### O1 observation-process model

Fit the parent’s measurement-only model on static transfer context plus decision-time-known masks, counts, recency, store-lag distributions, and caregiver counts, with no measured values. Counts of records entered after `t0` are leakage-audit outputs only and are never predictors. Report O1 versus static context and versus S0. O1 performance quantifies usable process signal; it does not by itself prove that T1’s separate value increment is artifactual.

### L1 GRU-D benchmark

Retain compact GRU-D on the same 12 bins, static inputs, target, split, tuning grid, calibration, and five seeds. It is useful as a flexible benchmark but not as the main attribution model because it deliberately entangles values, masks, and gaps.

### L2 two-stream masked temporal convolutional alternative

Add a compact two-stream TCN on the identical twelve bins and target:

- value stream: standardized observed values plus forward-filled values, with no mask or gap channel;
- process stream: masks, time since last measurement, within-bin counts, store-lag summaries computed only from records available by `t0`, and caregiver counts, with no measured values;
- static stream: exactly S0 transfer context;
- fusion: separate two-layer causal 1-D convolution encoders (kernel 3, dilations 1 and 2, 32 or 64 channels, dropout 0 or 0.2), concatenated with static context before the three-class head.

Fit five fixed seeds with Adam (`1e-3` or `3e-4`), validation log-loss early stopping, and validation-only temperature scaling. L2 is scientifically preferable to replacing GRU-D because its stream-specific predictions and ablations directly estimate what value history adds over process history while retaining nonlinear cross-channel timing. It can represent late relapse and local order that T1 summaries lose; unlike a latent physiological-state model, it does not claim identifiable biology.

Mandatory L2 contrasts on the untouched test set:

- full L2 versus process+static stream;
- full L2 versus value+static stream;
- value+static stream versus S0;
- full L2 versus T1;
- **within-person pre-endpoint bin-order permutation** of the value stream: keep the final two-hour bin fixed and apply one shared permutation of the preceding 11 bins across all value channels, leaving that person’s pre-endpoint value multiset, masks/process stream, static inputs, and endpoint snapshot fixed; average predictions across 20 frozen permutations;
- **patient-level value-sequence permutation** within destination, S0-risk decile, and density quintile, as in the parent.

The within-person pre-endpoint permutation asks whether ordering before the frozen endpoint matters beyond value distribution. The patient-level permutation asks whether the person-specific value trajectory matters at all. Neither manipulation proves biology: value responses may reflect treatment, clinician reaction, or measurement error.

A joint latent physiological/observation model remains deferred. From one observational site, its latent-state separation would depend on unverifiable assumptions and would not identify biology. Revisit only with independent continuous-monitor data, staffing/monitoring metadata, or adjudicated observation-policy changes.

## Split, evaluation, and four-axis interpretation

Retain the frozen subject split seed 20260923 (60/20/20), validation-only model selection/calibration, one test opening, and 2,000 subject-cluster bootstrap replicates.

Report four axes separately; never collapse them into one supportive/adverse label.

### A. Incremental prognostic information

- **Supported:** paired `Brier(S0)-Brier(T1) > 0` with 95% CI entirely above zero, acceptable calibration after validation-only recalibration, and no leakage/readiness failure.
- **Falsified at the material bound:** the 95% upper bound is <0.002 with adequate events/coverage. This rules out the prespecified material Brier gain, not every nonzero gain.
- **Inconclusive:** CI crosses zero or calibration/event/coverage gates fail.

### B. Clinical materiality

- **Supported:** point Brier gain >=0.002, positive incremental net benefit of T1 over S0 at at least two of 2%, 5%, 10%, and prespecified risk-category reclassification/clinical counts are reported; the standardized burden contrast >=2 percentage points with CI above zero is corroborative, not required to prove model utility.
- **Not demonstrated:** information gain is statistically supported but any materiality criterion fails.
- **Inconclusive:** uncertainty spans thresholds or calibration invalidates decision analysis.

Thus a real gain below one threshold is reported as “incremental but not clinically material by this contract,” not adverse.

### C. Source and temporal structure of signal

Classify the evidence pattern, allowing mixed results:

- **value-history contribution:** T1>S0 and L2 full>process+static, with patient-level value permutation removing most of that increment;
- **order contribution:** L2 full exceeds the mean within-person order-permuted L2 with paired CI above zero; if not, value distribution/persistence may matter without fine order;
- **process-dominant:** O1/process-stream carries most performance and value additions have CIs including zero;
- **mixed value/process:** both streams add; this is expected and must not be forced into a biological/artifact dichotomy.

Repeat these contrasts in the dense core-vital stratum, no-treatment-limitation stratum, daytime transfer stratum, and charttime-only retrospective sensitivity. Attenuation is reported quantitatively. No ablation establishes biological residual instability.

### D. Endpoint/component validity

Fit secondary four-state multinomial S0c/T1c models on the same split to estimate component-specific Brier differences; retain first-event cumulative incidences as descriptive checks. With approximately 661 deaths overall, a test split may be underpowered for a clinically material death-specific gain, which yields component uncertainty rather than forced consistency.

- **Component-consistent:** T1-S0 Brier direction and clinically relevant risk ordering agree for ICU return and death, without a sensitivity reversal.
- **Component-specific:** one component carries the composite gain; state which.
- **Endpoint-ambiguous:** directions conflict, PACU-precursor proxy exclusion materially reverses ICU-return results, or treatment-limit strata reverse death results.
- **Adjudication-required:** a random stratified sample of predicted high-risk positives and controls is needed to estimate planned-return and expected-death misclassification with blinded dual clinician review.

A composite signal remains prognostically checkable even when endpoint interpretation is ambiguous, but it cannot be called evidence of preventable deterioration.

## Supportive, adverse, and inconclusive overall reports

The solver must output the four-axis vector before a narrative:

- A supportive overall report requires A supported; it must qualify whether B is material, C is value/order/process/mixed, and D is consistent/component-specific/ambiguous.
- An adverse report is appropriate only when adequate precision rules out the 0.002 material increment or value history adds nothing beyond S0/process; it does not prove biological stability.
- An inconclusive report is required for insufficient precision, leakage failure, poor calibration, inadequate events/coverage, or unresolved endpoint reversal.

Examples the verifier must reject include: claiming biological instability from T1 or L2 gain; claiming no information because the 2-point burden threshold fails while Brier gain is supported; calling masks-only performance proof that values do not matter despite a positive full-versus-process contrast; or calling the composite preventable when only death or procedurally preceded returns drive it.

## What is computable and what is not

Computationally checkable: source hashes/headers, joins, population, windows, `charttime/storetime` availability, item dictionaries, event chronology, component labels, exact PACU-predecessor path, split integrity, all model inputs/ablations, calibration, paired metrics, bootstrap intervals, decision curves, and whether conclusion text matches the four-axis thresholds.

Not automatically establishable: true discharge intent, planned versus unplanned return, treatment preferences, expected death, adequacy of ward staffing/monitoring, biological mechanism, benefit of delaying transfer or extra monitoring, and external transportability. These require clinician adjudication, operational data, a prospective impact study, or external validation.

## Deliverable and resources

The new scientific deliverable is fitted decision-time S0, T1, O1, GRU-D L1, and two-stream L2 models plus a four-axis evidence report. Completion requires the parent outputs plus:

- `availability_audit.json` and real-time versus charttime-only predictions;
- `endpoint_chronology.csv` and component/sensitivity metrics;
- `l2_ablation_metrics.json` with full/value/process/order- and patient-permutation contrasts across five seeds;
- `interpretation_axes.json` containing A-D status, estimates, CIs, threshold comparisons, and exact supporting output paths;
- `conclusion.md` generated from, and consistent with, those axes.

Measured feasibility: parent cohort/event/coverage audits and the completed decision-time delay audit (7,235,465 selected chart rows; 2,145 or 0.030% entered at/after transfer) attached to this child. Estimated future solver budget: extraction with 8 CPUs/64 GiB for 2–4 hours; S0/T1/O1 and bootstrap with 8 CPUs/64 GiB for 1–3 hours; L1/L2 five-seed training with one allocated A100 plus 8 CPUs/64 GiB for 3–6 hours. This is within the configured 16 CPU, 262,144 MiB, 8 GPU, 28,800-second planning envelope. GPU availability is deployment-verified; no discovery GPU probe was needed.

## Exactly three key references

[K1] Heo Y, Kim M, Han SS, et al. *AI-Driven Predictions of Readmission and Mortality for Improved Discharge Decisions in Critical Care: A Retrospective Study.* Diagnostics. 2026;16(6):874. doi:10.3390/diagnostics16060874.

[K2] Ruppert MM, Loftus TJ, Small C, et al. *Predictive Modeling for Readmission to Intensive Care: A Systematic Review.* Crit Care Explor. 2023;5(1):e0848. doi:10.1097/CCE.0000000000000848.

[K3] Agniel D, Kohane IS, Weber GM. *Biases in electronic health record data due to processes within the healthcare system: retrospective observational study.* BMJ. 2018;361:k1479. doi:10.1136/bmj.k1479.

# Postoperative HCC marker-history positivity and interpretation audit

## Objective and evidence boundary

Reproduce the frozen prerequisite audit that determines whether this HCC snapshot can test this unresolved hypothesis:

> Among adults at a day-60 landmark after first recorded HCC resection, do preoperative marker level and postoperative marker change predict subsequent HCC-targeted laboratory measurement more strongly than continued local contact, generic laboratory testing, liver-injury monitoring, and same-workflow oncology-panel measurement?

This is a scoped numerical prerequisite audit with one deliberately minimal exploratory fit. It is not a recurrence study or a confirmatory estimate. Newly construct the cohort and marker-history support from the read-only CSVs, fit the specified diagnostic model, provide rerunnable code, and report the interpretation supported by the computed results.

The strongest existing clinical evidence is that incomplete AFP response measured 4–6 weeks after surgery was associated with worse recurrence-free and overall survival in a selected high-AFP resection cohort [K1]. It does not show that persistent AFP is residual tumor, follow-up measurement is ignorable, or changing surveillance improves outcomes. EHR order presence and timing can carry information generated by care processes [K2]. Informative-presence methods distinguish contact from repeated observation and do not give latent recording states a unique mechanism [K3]. This audit asks whether the snapshot has enough exposure and target-versus-workflow-comparator support to test the unresolved claim.

Confirmation is never rewarded. If the frozen support and gates are reproduced, the binary confirmatory experiment is infeasible and target-specific surveillance remains scientifically inconclusive, not refuted.

## Exact data bindings

Inputs are UTF-8 CSV files mounted read-only under `/data/hcc/`. Join within encounter on (`患者主索引`, `就诊号`) and across encounters on `患者主索引`. Use native event time. Write no identifiers, rows, or notes; only aggregate results under `/workspace`.

- `encounters`, `/data/hcc/encounters.csv`: `患者主索引, 就诊号, 年龄, 性别, 就诊时间, 入院时间, 出院时间, 就诊科室`. Age, service, stay, and sole source of contact A/A0. Start is admission else visit else discharge; end is valid discharge >= start else start.
- `procedures`, `/data/hcc/procedures.csv`: `患者主索引, 就诊号, 手术, 开始时间, 结束时间, 手术来源`. Index resection and recorded locoregional treatment; event time `开始时间`.
- `diagnoses`, `/data/hcc/diagnoses.csv`: `患者主索引, 就诊号, 诊断名称, 诊断类型`. Same-encounter HCC support; no native time.
- `pathology`, `/data/hcc/pathology.csv`: `患者主索引, 就诊号, 病理, 检查所见, 检查诊断, 机器型号`. Baseline severity proxies only; no native time.
- `labs`, `/data/hcc/labs.csv`: `患者主索引, 就诊号, 检验, 定性结果, 定量结果, 标本类型, 检验时间`. H and weekly L-M/N-L/L-I/O-TM; event time `检验时间`.
- `examinations`, `/data/hcc/examinations.csv`: `患者主索引, 就诊号, 检查, 检查所见, 检查诊断, 开始时间, 机器型号, 检查号`. Secondary context only, never a rescue outcome.
- `medications`, `/data/hcc/medications.csv`: `患者主索引, 就诊号, 用药, 单次用药计量, 单次用药计量单位, 频次, 开始时间, 结束时间, 用药方式, 药品类型`. Treatment/interference flags; time is start else end else encounter start.
- `clinical_documents`, `/data/hcc/clinical_documents.csv`: keys plus `主诉, 现病史, 既往史, 入院诊断, 入院情况, 诊疗经过, 出院情况, 出院诊断, 手术名称, 手术经过`. Optional blinded dictionary review only; handle duplicated `入院诊断` explicitly.

No lab unit, assay platform/range, order purpose, scheduled appointment, mortality, enrollment end, complete outside care, clinician intent, or true recurrence exists. Report text is not recurrence truth; images are unavailable.

## Frozen population, split, and time

Include adults age >=18 with earliest dated qualifying liver resection in 2012–2023. A procedure must contain both `肝` and `切除`; exclude `移植|供肝|修整|活检|穿刺|囊肿|脓肿|再植|复发|再次`. It must occur in the same encounter as non-uncertain HCC (`肝细胞癌|原发性肝癌`, excluding `疑|待排|可能|倾向`) and within 30 days of encounter start. Deduplicate to earliest qualifying resection per patient.

Exclude recorded directed treatment strictly after index through day 60: TACE/embolization, ablation, transplant, separate repeat resection, or strict HCC systemic therapy. Procedure expression: `栓塞|化疗栓塞|消融|移植|肝动脉.*灌注|肝局部灌注|肝病损.*射频|肝病损.*微波|肝肿瘤.*射频|肝肿瘤.*微波`. A qualifying liver-resection row in another encounter >=7 days after index is repeat resection. Systemic names: `索拉非尼|仑伐替尼|乐伐替尼|瑞戈非尼|多纳非尼|阿帕替尼|卡博替尼|雷莫芦单抗|阿替利珠单抗|信迪利单抗|卡瑞利珠单抗|替雷利珠单抗|帕博利珠单抗|纳武利尤单抗|度伐利尤单抗|德瓦鲁单抗|替西木单抗|贝伐珠单抗`. Prior treatment in days -180:-1 is a covariate, not exclusion. Later marks never affect eligibility.

Expected cohort: 15,575. Split by `int(SHA256(str(患者主索引))[:8],16) mod 100`: 0–59 train, 60–69 validation, 70–79 locked test, 80–99 reserve.

Keep every patient on 44 outcome-independent bins covering days 61–365; week is `min(43,floor((day-61)/7))`. A is encounter interval overlap only; A0 is encounter start only. No local mark means only “not present in these files.”

## Marker history H and outcomes

Exact HCC-marker priority is AFP `甲胎蛋白`, PIVKA-II `异常凝血酶原`, AFP-L3 `甲胎蛋白异质体`.

For each label, select the latest plain numeric result from day -90 to strictly before surgery and the latest plain numeric result during days 15–60. Strings with `< > <= >= ≤ ≥`, no number, or multiple numbers are availability evidence but not numeric. Exclude same-timestamp conflicts. Require pre >0 and post >=0. If multiple labels pair, select by priority without outcomes.

Keep two separate axes: training ECDF rank of pre value within exact label and era (2012–16, 2017–19, 2020–21, 2022–23), frozen outside train; and `log(max(post,1e-12)/pre)`. Never pool raw values across labels/eras. Keep sparse/unranked states explicit.

For positivity only:

- HP: pre-rank >=0.75 and post/pre >=0.5.
- LC: pre-rank <0.75 and post/pre <0.5.
- Other ranked pairs: discordant.

These states are not recurrence definitions.

Weekly multilabel marks, deduplicated within patient-week:

- L-M: the three HCC markers.
- N-L: `钠, 肌酐, 血红蛋白`.
- L-I: `丙氨酸氨基转移酶, 门冬氨酸氨基转移酶, 总胆红素, 白蛋白, 国际标准化比值, 血小板计数`.
- O-TM: `癌胚抗原, 糖类抗原19-9`.
- A: encounter interval overlap.

## Required files and JSON

Write `/workspace/analysis.py`, rerunnable as `python /workspace/analysis.py`, and aggregate-only `/workspace/results.json`.

Required top-level JSON fields:

- `schema="hcc-marker-history-positivity-v1"`;
- `source_snapshot="3f97e661e1884c34c1e2cdbf74ba0cf6d6c8995853e85f1857c3d72b82ccf521"`;
- `task_scope="prerequisite_audit_with_exploratory_diagnostic"`;
- `input_manifest` for all eight runtime paths and SHA-256 values;
- `population_flow, selected_summary, by_split, by_era, by_label, train_group_sizes, weekly_support`;
- `positivity_assessment` with booleans for every gate and reasons;
- `diagnostic_model, conclusion, limitations, provenance`.

Derive, do not copy, these verifier anchors: selected H n=328; HP/LC/discordant/unranked=5/165/157/1; label multiplicities 201/87/40 for one/two/three; split n=199/31/37/61; HP=4/0/0/1; test any LM/NL/LI/O-TM=9/10/10/9. Training LM-only/OTM-only weeks are 12/1; validation adds 3/0, so train+validation is 15/1.

## Minimal exploratory diagnostic

Use ranked H patients in train+validation (expected 230), all 44 weeks, and five stacked marks A/LM/NL/LI/OTM (50,600 rows). Standardize each H axis with train mean and population SD. Fit binomial logit with intercept; normalized week and square; mark intercepts (A reference); era indicators (2012–16 reference); PIVKA-II indicator (AFP reference); both H axes; and each H-axis by non-A-mark interaction. Use patient-cluster-robust covariance.

Report convergence, iterations, warnings, events (A/LM/NL/LI/OTM expected 184/110/128/128/96), Brier/log loss by mark, per-SD mark slopes with 95% CIs, and LM-minus-A/NL/LI/OTM interaction contrasts with CIs for each axis.

This checks numerical estimability only. It omits the final severity/service/history basis, bootstrap, standardized 365-day risks, Holm control, and locked test. Do not call it the final baseline or hypothesis support. Do not fit/report a binary HP effect after positivity fails.

## Gates and interpretation

Before a confirmatory effect model require: >=100 effective patients per H contrast; >=20 H-exposed LM and O-TM patients separately in validation and test; viable label-era scaling; and adequate discordant LM/OTM weeks. Evaluate gates first.

For the frozen data, `conclusion` must state:

- `binary_confirmatory_feasibility="infeasible"`;
- `target_specific_surveillance="inconclusive"`;
- `hypothesis_status="not_tested_adequately"`;
- `exploratory_diagnostic_supports_hypothesis=false`;
- `action="defer_until_new_data_meet_support_gates"`.

Explain that positivity failure is adverse to feasibility, not evidence that surveillance specificity is absent. Broad intervals, sparse discordance, unstable ranks, calibration failure, era/service reversal, or latent-state non-recovery are inconclusive. An imprecise null does not refute the claim. Do not revise thresholds after outcomes, pool assays, drop O-TM, or repeatedly peek at test.

In future adequate data, supportive evidence requires LM specificity over A/N-L/L-I/O-TM for both axes under Holm-adjusted 95% intervals, standardized specificity risk difference >=0.02, ratio-of-risk-ratios >=1.25, locked-test directional replication, no era/service sign reversal, calibration, and target-specific permutation evidence. Adverse evidence requires precise exclusion of material specificity, especially LM no greater than O-TM/L-I, plus U+Q+B matching U+Q+B+V within 1% held-out deviance. The deferred semi-Markov alternative can be revisited only after gates pass; do not fit it here.

The verifier can check bindings, computation evidence, counts, positivity, diagnostic extraction, and conclusion consistency. It cannot establish assay equivalence, complete retention, outside care/death, intent, recurrence, latent-state meaning, surveillance benefit, or causality. These need clinical adjudication, linkage, prospective data, expert review, or another study.

[K1] Liang L, Wang MD, Zhang YM, et al. “Association of Postoperative Biomarker Response with Recurrence and Survival in Patients with Hepatocellular Carcinoma and High Alpha-Fetoprotein Expressions (>400 ng/ml).” *J Hepatocell Carcinoma*. 2021;8:103–118. https://doi.org/10.2147/JHC.S289840

[K3] Sisk R, Lin L, Sperrin M, et al. “Informative presence and observation in routine health data.” *JAMIA*. 2021;28(1):155–166. https://doi.org/10.1093/jamia/ocaa242

# Positivity-resolved deferral of marker-history–specific postoperative HCC surveillance inference

Status: substantive feasibility child of candidate-e0e5a6138d6b64662869b5ca. The fixed N=15,575 day-60 cohort, full 44-week day-61:365 grid, source bindings, and prohibition on biological recurrence claims are unchanged. Two aggregate audits and one deliberately minimal fit were executed. They establish that a transparent continuous-H model is numerically fit-able, but the parent's prespecified high/persistent-versus-low/clearing estimand is not identified with usable split/era positivity. No target-specific surveillance conclusion is supported.

## Scientific opening, supported claim, and unresolved claim

The strongest clinical claim supported by inspected evidence remains that incomplete AFP response measured at a 4–6-week postoperative visit was associated with worse recurrence-free and overall survival among 549 selected resected HCC patients whose preoperative AFP exceeded 400 ng/mL [K1]. It does not establish that persistent AFP is residual tumor, that follow-up measurement availability is ignorable, or that measuring more often improves outcomes.

Routine EHR observation is generated by care: order presence and timing can carry strong prognostic information independent of values [K2], and informative presence/observation methods distinguish care contact from the process producing repeated measurements while warning against mechanistic interpretation of latent recording states [K3]. These findings support explicit modeling of the recording process; they do not show why a particular postoperative HCC patient was measured.

The parent's unresolved claim was that pre-landmark marker history H predicts subsequent HCC-targeted laboratory measurement more strongly than continued local contact A, generic laboratory testing N-L, liver-injury monitoring L-I, or oncology-panel measurement O-TM. The strongest rival is a recording process in which prior measurement propensity, liver severity, service/era workflow, and same-encounter panel bundling jointly produce both H availability and later L-M, with apparent “persistence” amplified by regression to the mean and mathematical coupling of the preoperative value to the post/pre ratio.

The present advance is negative but consequential: it resolves whether the parent’s H contrast can support that discrimination. It cannot. The binary contrast has five high/persistent patients in the entire cohort, none in validation or locked test. A continuous bivariate H fit is computationally possible, but only 328 patients have a valid same-label numeric pre/post pair and only 75 later receive L-M. Thus this snapshot can describe the measurement-selection opening and audit models, but cannot provide a confirmatory target-specific conclusion. Running the larger latent model would add precision-looking structure without resolving positivity.

## Exact H construction and executed support audit

The parent left several operational choices implicit. This child freezes them for audit:

- A preoperative result is the latest plain numeric result for an exact marker label from 90 days before surgery to strictly before the surgery timestamp. A sensitivity that ends at day −1 excludes same-day preoperative measurements.
- The postoperative result is the latest plain numeric same-label result from day 15 through day 60.
- Exact labels are AFP (`甲胎蛋白`), PIVKA-II (`异常凝血酶原`), and AFP-L3 (`甲胎蛋白异质体`). When several labels qualify, the deterministic anchor is AFP, then PIVKA-II, then AFP-L3. Label choice may not depend on outcomes.
- Inequality-qualified, missing, multi-number, and nonnumeric results are availability evidence but are not converted to numeric limits. A pair requires preoperative value >0 and postoperative value ≥0.
- The two primary continuous axes are training-frozen preoperative empirical rank within exact label and index era, and the log(post/pre) ratio. Raw values are never pooled across labels or eras because units, reference ranges, and platforms are absent.
- For the audited dichotomy only, “high/persistent” means preoperative rank ≥0.75 and post/pre ≥0.5; “low/clearing” means rank <0.75 and post/pre <0.5. Other pairs are discordant. These thresholds are operational recording-history states, not recurrence definitions.

On the frozen snapshot, the stricter day −90:−1 construction yielded 298 valid pairs; allowing a same-day result only when it precedes the surgery timestamp yielded 328/15,575 (2.1%). The timestamp construction is preferred because it preserves temporal order. Among 328: 201 have one eligible label, 87 have two, and 40 have three; the priority rule selected 292 AFP, 35 PIVKA-II, and one AFP-L3 pair. The selected H states were five high/persistent, 165 low/clearing, 157 discordant, and one unranked. High/persistent support was four train, zero validation, zero test, one reserve.

The continuous observed-pair sample was 199 train, 31 validation, 37 locked test, and 61 reserve. Any day-61:365 mark among those patients was sparse: A 86, L-M 75, N-L 79, L-I 79, and exact CEA/CA19-9 O-TM 74. Locked test contained only 9 L-M, 10 N-L, 10 L-I, and 9 O-TM patients. Training exact-label/era ECDF groups were adequate only for AFP (68, 55, 37, and 20 across four eras); PIVKA-II groups were 1, 10, 4, and 4, and AFP-L3 had no training member. Therefore pooled “within-label/era” scaling is not valid for all labels, and PIVKA-II/AFP-L3 can be descriptive only.

Panel overlap is even more consequential within H-observed patients. In train plus validation, there were 110 L-M, 128 N-L, 128 L-I, and 96 O-TM marked weeks across 230 patients. L-M-versus-O-TM discordance was only 12 L-M-only versus one O-TM-only week; validation contributed three versus zero. This leaves little information for distinguishing target selection from oncology-panel bundling.

These are aggregate feasibility results, not an association estimate or evidence against clinical surveillance.

## Fixed population, temporal boundaries, and variables

Population and exclusions remain exactly those of the parent: adults; earliest dated qualifying liver resection in 2012–2023 within 30 days of the linked encounter and in the same encounter as non-uncertain HCC; exclusion of transplant/donor/biopsy/cyst/abscess/repeat/recurrent wording and duplicate index-encounter procedure rows; exclusion of recorded directed HCC treatment during index+1 through day 60 under the strict dictionary, with broader cytotoxic sensitivity. Prior recorded treatment in days −180:−1 is a covariate. No later mark affects eligibility.

Every patient remains on the outcome-independent 44-week grid from day 61 through 365. A comes only from encounter interval overlap; A0 uses encounter start. “No mark” means no mark in these institutional files, not alive, retained, disease-free, or untreated outside the system. Numeric H is defined only in the 328 observed-pair patients; marker absent, pre-only, post-only, invalid-numeric, and unmatched-label states remain separate ascertainment categories in the full cohort and receive no imputed values.

The full cohort still supports descriptive comparison of ascertainment states: the inherited audit found 312 patients with any pre- and post-landmark marker observation, versus 10,753 pre-only, 64 post-only, and 4,446 neither; any A was 26.6% in the both-observed state versus 11.5% in neither. This is compatible with informative observation but does not identify an H effect.

## Exact source bindings

All source CSVs are read-only ordinary files. Join within encounter on `(患者主索引, 就诊号)`, link across encounters on `患者主索引`, use event time rather than inherited encounter time whenever available, and write only aggregate or derived artifacts to the workspace.

- `encounters`: `[private path]`; required columns `患者主索引, 就诊号, 年龄, 性别, 就诊时间, 入院时间, 出院时间, 就诊科室`. Sole source of A/A0; supplies service and length of stay.
- `procedures`: `[private path]`; `患者主索引, 就诊号, 手术, 开始时间, 结束时间, 手术来源`. Supplies index resection and recorded locoregional treatment.
- `diagnoses`: `[private path]`; `患者主索引, 就诊号, 诊断名称, 诊断类型`. No native time; baseline HCC support only.
- `pathology`: `[private path]`; `患者主索引, 就诊号, 病理, 检查所见, 检查诊断, 机器型号`. No native time; reviewed baseline severity proxies only.
- `labs`: `[private path]`; `患者主索引, 就诊号, 检验, 定性结果, 定量结果, 标本类型, 检验时间`. Supplies H and weekly L-M/N-L/L-I/O-TM. Exact L-M labels are above; N-L is sodium/creatinine/hemoglobin; L-I is ALT/AST/total bilirubin/albumin/INR/platelets; O-TM is exact CEA and CA19-9. No units/platform/reference ranges exist.
- `examinations`: `[private path]`; `患者主索引, 就诊号, 检查, 检查所见, 检查诊断, 开始时间, 机器型号, 检查号`. Imaging remains secondary and is not used to rescue the failed laboratory positivity.
- `medications`: `[private path]`; `患者主索引, 就诊号, 用药, 单次用药剂量, 单次用药剂量单位, 频次, 开始时间, 结束时间, 用药方式, 药品类型`. Supplies recorded systemic-treatment and PIVKA-interference flags; indication is unavailable.
- `clinical_documents`: `[private path]`; required fields are the two keys plus complaint, present/past history, admission diagnosis/condition, course, discharge status/diagnosis, procedure name/course. It may support blinded dictionary review, never automatic recurrence truth.

Mortality, enrollment end, outside care, scheduled appointments, assay platform/units, order purpose, clinician intent, and true recurrence are unavailable.

## Transparent full-grid baseline: what was and was not fit

The mandatory scientific baseline remains a stacked recurrent-mark model on a common patient-week grid. Its final design uses exactly the continuous H-observed subset, outcomes A/L-M/N-L/L-I/O-TM, week spline, separate pre-rank and log-ratio terms, H×mark interactions, baseline severity/pathology, service, index era, length of stay, prior treatment, pre-landmark injury/observation history, and only t− lagged A/mark history. It must report standardized 365-day component risks and LM-minus-A/N-L/L-I/O-TM specificity, patient-cluster bootstrap uncertainty, calibration by mark/era/service, and leave-one-era-out estimates. Pre-rank and log ratio must be reported separately; a single composite is prohibited because baseline value appears in the ratio denominator and can induce regression-to-the-mean structure.

A bounded diagnostic fit used the same 44-week grid but only train plus validation (230 patients, 50,600 stacked mark rows), with mark intercepts, quadratic week, era, label, and both H axes by mark. It converged in eight iterations without warnings. This answers a narrow compute question: ordinary logistic fitting is numerically possible on CPU. It is not the final baseline: it omits the full severity/service/history basis, standardization, bootstrap, multiplicity control, and locked test.

The diagnostic’s broad intervals and strongest workflow comparator are cautionary. Per 1-SD pre-rank, the LM-versus-O-TM interaction odds ratio was 1.10 (95% CI 0.97–1.24); for log ratio it was 1.08 (0.94–1.24). LM-versus-N-L/L-I pre-rank interactions were about 1.19 with lower limits barely above one, while log-ratio contrasts included one. These exploratory coefficients are neither adjusted materiality estimates nor confirmatory findings; repeated fitting or threshold revision to make them favorable is prohibited. They show why O-TM is essential and why panel bundling remains the strongest rival.

The binary high/persistent-versus-low/clearing baseline must not be fit: its positivity gate failed before model fitting. The continuous final baseline may be retained only as explicitly exploratory method development; it cannot satisfy locked-test replication or the inherited ≥100-effective-patient contrast gate.

Measured compute was about 116 seconds for the timestamp H audit and 115 seconds for audit plus minimal fit on ordinary CPU. A final exploratory baseline is estimated at 8 CPUs, ≤64 GiB, ≤2 hours. No GPU is scientifically needed.

## Matched substantive recording-process alternative

The scientifically matched alternative is retained as a future-data design, not fit on this snapshot. On the identical H-observed patients, weeks, split, features, and five marks, fit a joint semi-Markov recording-process model:

- U is local-record activity anchored positively by A and allowed to load on all marks.
- Q is liver-severity monitoring anchored by L-I and allowed to load on N-L and L-M.
- B is oncology-panel propensity anchored by O-TM and allowed to load on L-M.
- V is target enrichment allowed to load on L-M but constrained to zero on A/N-L/L-I/O-TM.
- A measurement-error component represents latent preoperative and postoperative marker state within exact label; it estimates shrinkage from repeated values where available and keeps pre-state and change distinct. It is a model of noisy recorded marker history, not tumor biology.
- Transitions use baseline and t− history only; era/service enter U/Q/B. Weekly emissions are multilabel, preserving co-bundled and discordant weeks.

Compare U+Q+B against U+Q+B+V on held-out marked-process deviance and posterior predictive LM/O-TM, LM/L-I, and LM/N-L cross-cells. The alternative could reveal persistent target-only covariance after representing return, liver monitoring, panel bundling, and measurement-error regression—information the transparent independent-logit basis loses. It still cannot identify retention, intent, recurrence, or a biological mechanism.

Match the baseline’s exact inputs, split, outcome definitions, era exclusions, and uncertainty target. Require null/shared-contact/panel-only/regression-to-mean/target-specific simulation recovery, three seeds, no state switching, 90–98% interval coverage, and posterior predictive reproduction of comparator cross-cells. Select V only if it improves validation LM deviance by ≥1% without ≥1% improvement or deterioration being misattributed to comparator marks, directionally replicates in locked test, and the baseline specificity gates also pass.

This alternative is deferred because current locked-test support is nine LM and nine O-TM patients and there are no high/persistent test patients. One A100, 16 CPUs, ≤128 GiB, and 4–6 hours is an unverified future estimate; no GPU job is warranted now. Revisit only after a new snapshot or linked cohort supplies at least 100 effective patients per H contrast, ≥20 H-exposed LM and O-TM patients in validation and test, viable label-era scaling, and sufficient discordant LM/O-TM weeks. These are scientific support gates, not hardware limits.

## Falsification and interpretation

The strongest claim supported now is computational: exact H can be constructed for only 328 patients; the nominal dichotomy violates positivity; and a reduced continuous stacked model converges. The unresolved scientific claim—whether marker history predicts target-specific surveillance beyond recording processes—was not tested adequately.

For a future adequately supported analysis:

- Supportive evidence requires LM specificity over A, N-L, L-I, and O-TM for both continuous H axes under Holm-adjusted 95% intervals, absolute standardized specificity risk difference ≥0.02, ratio-of-risk-ratios ≥1.25, locked-test directional replication, no era/service sign reversal, acceptable calibration, and a target-specific permutation result. U+Q+B+V is corroborative only after recovery and held-out gates.
- Adverse evidence is a precise result excluding material specificity, especially LM no greater than O-TM or L-I, together with U+Q+B matching U+Q+B+V within the 1% held-out threshold. This favors contact, liver monitoring, panel bundling, and regression-to-the-mean as adequate observed explanations.
- Inconclusive evidence includes the current positivity failure, broad intervals, sparse discordant LM/O-TM cells, unstable label-era ranks, calibration failure, era/service reversal, or latent-state non-recovery. An imprecise null does not refute target-specific surveillance.

Current conclusion: adverse to feasibility of the parent’s confirmatory binary experiment, inconclusive about target-specific surveillance. The branch should be deferred rather than compiled as a solved or confirmatory experiment. A new dataset/snapshot, linked claims, or prospectively scheduled follow-up is required to reopen it; changing the threshold, pooling assays, inspecting the test repeatedly, or dropping O-TM would not be a valid repair.

## Deliverable and verifier boundary

Delivered here: exact H rules; flow/support/positivity by split, era, and label; full-grid mark overlap; a bounded continuous fit diagnostic; matched baseline and recording-process alternative; resource estimates; and threshold-linked deferral.

An automatic verifier can check source hashes, cohort reproduction, timestamp order, parsing, label priority, split isolation, event counts, positivity gates, model convergence, use of common denominators, coefficient extraction, and that the conclusion is “inconclusive scientifically / infeasible confirmatorily.” It must reject a solver that labels the exploratory coefficients supportive, reports binary H effects, changes thresholds after seeing outcomes, pools sparse assays, or calls V recurrence/intent. It cannot adjudicate assay equivalence, outside care/death, clinical purpose, biological recurrence, or latent-state meaning; those require expert review or additional data.

## Alternatives and revisit triggers

- Binary H: abandoned in this snapshot because only 5/328 are high/persistent and none occur in validation/test.
- Continuous bivariate H: computationally feasible but exploratory only; retain separate pre-rank and log-ratio axes to expose regression-to-the-mean.
- Marker-availability state on all 15,575: useful descriptive ascertainment analysis, but it answers a different question and cannot substitute for marker-history specificity.
- Transparent stacked baseline: retained as the only justified current fit.
- U+Q+B+V model: scientifically substantive but deferred for support, not hardware, reasons.
- Imaging: remains secondary and cannot rescue the laboratory claim.
- Biological recurrence: remains frozen pending adjudicated/linked/prospective truth.

## Compact bibliography

[K1] Liang L, Wang MD, Zhang YM, et al. Association of Postoperative Biomarker Response with Recurrence and Survival in Patients with Hepatocellular Carcinoma and High Alpha-Fetoprotein Expressions (>400 ng/ml). *Journal of Hepatocellular Carcinoma*. 2021;8:103–118. doi:10.2147/JHC.S289840.

[K2] Agniel D, Kohane IS, Weber GM. Biases in electronic health record data due to processes within the healthcare system: retrospective observational study. *BMJ*. 2018;361:k1479. doi:10.1136/bmj.k1479.

[K3] Sisk R, Lin L, Sperrin M, et al. Informative presence and observation in routine health data: A review of methodology for clinical risk prediction. *Journal of the American Medical Informatics Association*. 2021;28(1):155–166. doi:10.1093/jamia/ocaa242.

# Residual instability before ICU-to-ward transfer

## Objective and evidence boundary

Conduct the frozen MIMIC-IV 3.1 investigation of whether decision-time-available final-24-hour trajectories add held-out information beyond endpoint state for 48-hour deterioration after an adult patient's first eligible ICU-to-general-ward transfer, and whether any gain concerns the timing of ICU return or in-hospital death rather than chiefly the operational process of live hospital discharge.

This is an open-ended retrospective prognostic and measurement-discrimination study. No model result is supplied. You must newly construct the cohort and predictors, fit and calibrate the models, estimate uncertainty, and link the conclusion to computed outputs. The known cohort/event counts below are feasibility and endpoint-audit findings, not evidence for the hypothesis.

The strongest inspected evidence supports only these premises. A longitudinal MIMIC-IV/external-hospital model predicted seven-day ICU readmission/death better than SWIFT while leaving operational factors, DNR status, and component trajectories unresolved [K1]. A systematic review found heterogeneous readmission windows and composites and advantages from explicit populations/outcomes and longitudinal predictors [K2]. Measurement timing and frequency can encode healthcare process as well as patient state [K3]. None establishes this task's unresolved trajectory, event-time, mechanism, or intervention claims.

Primary hypothesis: in the frozen cohort and information set, T1's prespecified value-trajectory features improve held-out 48-hour prediction over S0 after decision-time availability is enforced, and measured-value content adds information beyond observation process. The primary paired estimand is `Brier(S0)-Brier(T1)`.

Event-time stress-test hypothesis: if T1 captures information about observed post-transfer deterioration rather than mainly operational selection, M1 should improve calibrated cumulative-incidence prediction for first ICU return or in-hospital death over M0 across 48 hours, and that gain should not be explained solely by better live-discharge prediction.

The strongest rival is operational selection: transfer context, destination, service, treatment limitation, charting, and discharge workflow can determine continued observation and whether instability appears as return, death, or discharge. Association after adjustment is not a mechanism.

## Read-only input

The runtime binding is `/data/mimic-iv-3.1.zip`, SHA-256 `0dd448e341f489483194daafd884607d6f194648c6bf54eed56d1e2cd2af9e09`. Do not modify it. Required archive members, fields, keys, and times are:

- `mimic-iv-3.1/hosp/admissions.csv.gz`: `[internal identifier],[internal identifier],admittime,dischtime,deathtime,admission_type,discharge_location,hospital_expire_flag`; `dischtime` defines the recorded discharge transition and `deathtime` in-hospital death.
- `mimic-iv-3.1/hosp/patients.csv.gz`: `[internal identifier],gender,anchor_age,anchor_year,anchor_year_group,dod`; derive age by subject; never substitute `dod` for `deathtime`.
- `mimic-iv-3.1/hosp/services.csv.gz`: `[internal identifier],[internal identifier],transfertime,prev_service,curr_service`; use latest `transfertime <= t0`.

- `mimic-iv-3.1/icu/procedureevents.csv.gz`: `[internal identifier],[internal identifier],[internal identifier],starttime,endtime,storetime,itemid,statusdescription`.

## Frozen cohort and times

Create one row per hospitalization's first eligible transfer:

1. Adult age at ICU admission is at least 18.
2. ICU LOS is at least 24 hours.
3. The patient is alive at `t0=icustays.outtime`.
4. An exact `transfers.intime=t0` successor on the same nonmissing `[internal identifier],[internal identifier]` has a primary general-ward `careunit` in this exact set: `Medicine`, `Neurology`, `Med/Surg`, `Medicine/Cardiology`, `Transplant`, `Vascular`, `Med/Surg/GYN`, `Surgery/Trauma`, `Med/Surg/Trauma`, `Surgery`, `Cardiac Surgery`, `Medical/Surgical (Gynecology)`, `Surgery/Pancreatic/Biliary/Bariatric`, `Cardiology`, `Thoracic Surgery`, `Oncology`, `Hematology/Oncology`.

The expected independently audited primary cohort is 49,157 transfers. Split once by `[internal identifier]`, seed 20260923, into 60% development, 20% validation, and 20% untouched test. All admissions/person-period rows for a subject stay in one split. Fit preprocessing on development only; choose hyperparameters and calibrate on validation only; open test once.

Predictors use only `[t0-24h,t0)`. No post-`t0` ward measurement, destination change, treatment, note, discharge summary, service, or endpoint timestamp may enter a predictor. Post-`t0` fields define outcomes only.

## Outcomes and chronology

Frozen fixed-horizon three-state target over `(t0,t0+48h]`:

- deterioration: any same-admission later ICU `intime` or `admissions.deathtime`;
- live recorded hospital discharge by 48 hours without that raw deterioration label;
- otherwise alive/in hospital without deterioration at 48 hours.

Preserve this raw target even when chronology conflicts are found.

For the time-resolved target, create eight six-hour at-risk intervals. Everyone starts W. The first exact transition is R (later same-admission ICU `intime`), D (`deathtime`), L (recorded `dischtime` that is treated as live under the frozen rules), or W. R, D, and L are absorbing for this first-transition analysis. Resolve exact ties R before D before L and report tie counts.

Flag `chronology_conflict=1` when recorded discharge precedes a later raw ICU-return/death endpoint in the 48-hour window. Use literal first timestamp for the primary multistate analysis and run both mandatory sensitivities: exclude conflicts; and classify them by raw deterioration while explicitly noting the absorbing-state violation. Do not treat a later D after R as a separate modeled transition; report its count/order descriptively.

The existing audit found 49,157 rows, 2,607 raw deterioration labels, literal first transitions of 1,999 R, 586 D, 9,950 L, and 36,622 W at 48 hours, 22 chronology conflicts, 56 people with both ICU return and death, and no exact R/D or L/deterioration ties. Reproduce these values from source or explain a genuine implementation discrepancy before fitting; these are not hypothesis results. A recorded discharge is end of observed in-hospital follow-up, not proof of safety. Post-discharge deterioration is unavailable.

## Frozen predictors and models

Use training-fitted imputation/standardization and the inherited plausibility/unit rules. Construct twelve two-hour bins for each mapped value channel. Keep missingness explicit. Record endpoint value, measurement count/density, time since last observation, store-lag summaries, caregiver count, and current support state.

S0 is ridge multinomial regression using decision-time static transfer context (age, sex, admission type, source ICU, destination, current service, ICU LOS, transfer hour/night, code-status class and recent support), endpoint values, and the observation summaries above. T1 is nested in S0 and adds only prespecified measured-value history summaries across the twelve bins: level/persistence, slope/change, variability/volatility, extrema/range and abnormal-bin persistence. Freeze formulas, units, plausibility bounds, and missingness handling in `study_manifest.json` before test evaluation; do not select summaries after test results.

O1 uses static transfer context plus masks, counts/density, recency, decision-time store-lag distributions, and caregiver counts, with no measured values. Records stored at/after t0 are leakage-audit outputs and never predictors.

Retain the inherited learned alternatives on the same bins, static inputs, target, split, calibration, and five fixed seeds:

- L1: compact GRU-D benchmark.
- L2: two-stream masked temporal convolutional model. Its value stream receives standardized observed/forward-filled values without masks/gaps. Its process stream receives masks, time-since-last, counts, pre-t0 store-lag summaries, and caregiver counts without measured values. Separate two-layer causal 1-D encoders use kernel 3, dilations 1 and 2, 32 or 64 channels, dropout 0 or 0.2; concatenate with the S0 static stream before the three-class head. Fit with Adam at 1e-3 or 3e-4, validation-log-loss early stopping, and validation-only temperature scaling.
- Required L2 comparisons: full versus process+static; full versus value+static; value+static versus S0; full versus T1; within-person pre-endpoint order permutation (keep final bin fixed, one shared permutation of preceding 11 bins over all value channels, process/static unchanged, average 20 frozen permutations); and patient-level value-sequence permutation within destination, S0-risk decile, and density quintile.

L1/L2 diagnose representation and information source, not biology. A one-GPU allocation is appropriate for them; ordinary shells do not expose CUDA. The ridge models are CPU work.

Fit M0/M1 as ridge-penalized pooled multinomial logistic transition models on up to eight person-period rows with categorical interval baseline hazards and outcomes R/D/L/W. M0 uses exactly S0 inputs; M1 uses exactly T1 inputs. Use no post-t0 time-varying predictors. Choose penalty on validation multinomial log loss and calibrate cause-specific CIFs on validation only. Produce coherent transition hazards and CIFs at 6, 12, 18, 24, 30, 36, 42, and 48 hours.

## Required estimation and uncertainty

On untouched test subjects report:

- multiclass Brier, log loss, calibration and discrimination for S0/T1/O1 and L1/L2, plus paired `Brier(S0)-Brier(T1)`;
- L2 ablations/permutations across five seeds;
- R, D, L, and R+D CIF calibration at 6, 12, 24, 36, and 48 hours;
- time-dependent component and R+D Brier scores and integrated Brier scores over all eight intervals;
- paired `IBS(M0)-IBS(M1)` for R+D, R, D, and L;

Use 2,000 subject-cluster bootstrap replicates, preserving every admission and person-period row for a sampled subject. Report paired 95% intervals. Do not interpret an imprecise death-specific null as no death signal.
