- ZIP: `[private path]`; runtime target `/data/75850054cd-kit-corrected-eis.zip`; 17,307,136 bytes; SHA-256 `21f7942224c99bbcadb6c1ba3d229d5591a034c2d8785bfaf659fc8281078d34`.
- Members: all 228 semicolon-delimited files enumerated in `datasets/KIT_EIS/README.md`, named `cell_eisv2_P###_<replicate>_S##_C##.csv`.
- Example table/member: `kit_corrected_eis/cell_eisv2_P001_1_S01_C10.csv`; descriptor `datasets/KIT_EIS/table-d325c26bd9ee241e.json`.
- Catalog: `[private path]`; runtime target `/data/a90f68c3f0-catalog-v06.json`; SHA-256 `02afcb6c55ac8d6d1801f4d4ed51adaa45743e5a3461f9c468a1ecf85cf4d8b5`.

Required columns, present in the descriptor and raw archive, are filename-derived condition `P###`, replicate and specimen `P###_<replicate>`; audit-only hardware `S##,C##`; clocks/keys `timestamp_s,timestamp_origin,sd_block_id,uptime_ticks,seq_nr`; state/quality `cyc_charged,is_rt,soc_nom,valid,ocv_est_avg_V,t_avg_degC,eis_duration_s`; index `z_ref_init_mOhm,z_ref_now_mOhm,soh_imp`; and EIS `freq_Hz,z_amp_mOhm,z_ph_deg,z_amp_comp_mOhm,z_ph_comp_deg,z_re_comp_mOhm,z_im_comp_mOhm`. The spectrum key is `(specimen,timestamp_s,sd_block_id)`; the row key appends `seq_nr`. Units are seconds, Hz, mOhm, degrees, volts, and degrees Celsius as named in source headers.

The exact grid is `0:14705.8818, 1:10000, 2:6756.7568, 3:5000, 4:3125, 5:2083.3333, 6:1470.5883, 7:1000, 8:675.6757, 9:500, 10:312.5, 11:208.3333, 12:147.0588, 13:100, 14:67.5676, 15:50, 16:31.25, 17:20.8333, 18:14.7059, 19:10, 20:6.7568, 21:5, 22:3.125, 23:2.0833, 24:1, 25:0.5, 26:0.2083, 27:0.1, 28:0.05`. The fixed non-index panel is `seq_nr={7,15,24}`. The source-index panel is `{19,23,25,26}`. The quality-qualified corrected non-index set for eligibility is `{3,4,5,6,7,8,9,10,12,14,15,16,17,18,20,21,22,24}`.

Readiness verifies hashes, all schemas and filename identities, unique keys, within-spectrum metadata constancy, the common grid, and index reconstruction within 0.001 mOhm. Raw inspection found 35,275 rows at every sequence; raw amplitude/phase is finite for 35,232 spectra at most frequencies but only 30,701 at 100 Hz, so the full representation preserves missingness instead of requiring a complete raw grid.

## Frozen population, chronology, and future-safe endpoint

1. Within specimen, order spectrum keys by `timestamp_s`; start a visit after an adjacent gap greater than 48 h. Report 24 h and 72 h sensitivities and maximum chain-grouped duration.
2. For duplicate `(specimen,visit,is_rt,soc_nom)`, select among `valid=1` by `timestamp_origin=1`, then greatest count of finite corrected pairs on the 18-frequency eligibility grid, then earliest `timestamp_s,sd_block_id`. Never select by temperature proximity.
3. A room or operating state is complete when all five `soc_nom in {10,30,50,70,90}` are selected with at least 17/18 finite eligibility-grid pairs. One missing pair gets a mask; larger deficits are ineligible.
4. A unit at visit t requires immediately previous raw visit t-1 room-complete, current t room-and-operating-complete, and immediately next raw visit t+1 room-complete, without skipping a visit. Require an 18–24 day current-to-next room-anchor interval and `|median_SOC(T_op-T_rt)|>=8 °C`.
5. Define room anchor `A_v` as the median timestamp of five selected room spectra and `I_v=median_{SOC 30,50,70} z_ref_now_mOhm(v,SOC)`. The information cutoff is the maximum timestamp of all current predictors.
6. Fit future level `F_t=I_(t+1)`. Convert each OOF prediction to `Yhat_t=21*(Fhat_t-I_t)/h_t`, where `h_t=(A_(t+1)-A_t)/86400`, and score against `Y_t=21*(I_(t+1)-I_t)/h_t`. Future interval and completeness are never predictors or tuning features.
7. Assert every feature timestamp is at or before cutoff and every endpoint component is later. Inference is conditional on complete current room/operating measurements and a complete next check-up; report exclusions.

The audited primary population is 2,071 transitions, 167 specimens, and 57 conditions (approximately 573/697/801 transitions in 0/10/40 °C strata). Every primary model uses exactly these units. Package-specific availability populations are secondary selection diagnostics only.

## Same-population acquisition ladder

No model may use condition, specimen, hardware identity, absolute timestamp, future interval, or `eis_duration_s`. **`eis_duration_s` is prohibited from every predictive feature set, shadow, imputer, residualizer, interaction, and tuning rule.** It records the observed full sweep and may appear only in descriptive burden tables and outcome-free stratified sensitivity reports.

All representations use outer-training preprocessing and package-specific masks. For each impedance package, regress its impedance block on B-room plus its metadata shadow in outer training, apply unchanged to validation/test, and separately penalize the residual block. This yields an explicit shadow contrast without causal interpretation.

### B-scalar and B-room

`B-scalar` contains `I_t`, prior normalized index slope, log age, previous interval, current room temperature median/range, five room OCV values, origin/valid/finite/duplicate indicators, and `cyc_charged`; also report no-change, prior-slope persistence, and outer-training equal-condition mean-rate predictions.

`B-room`, the room-only decision baseline, adds the complete current five-SOC room acquisition: reconstruct signed complex values at all 29 frequencies as `z_amp_mOhm*(cos(z_ph_deg),sin(z_ph_deg))`, preserve coordinate masks, project each SOC/channel onto 10 fixed cubic B-splines over log10 frequency with masked ridge projection, standardize on outer training, and use outer-training SVD rank `q in {4,8,12,16,24,32}`. This strong baseline makes each operating package incremental to all recorded room information.

### Package-specific metadata shadows

`M90` adds only SOC90 operating temperature, temperature and reciprocal-temperature differences, OCV and OCV difference, room-to-operating lag, source-counter difference, timestamp-origin, valid/finite/missing indicators, and temperature stratum. `M50/90` adds the same fields for SOC50 and SOC90. `M5` adds them for all five SOCs. None includes operating impedance, duration, identity, or absolute time. Each package is compared with its exact shadow and B-room.

### Fixed sparse non-index packages

`S90-3 = M90 +` operating raw signed-complex impedance reconstructed from `z_amp_mOhm,z_ph_deg` at SOC90 and 1000/50/1 Hz (six values plus masks).

`S50/90-3 = M50/90 +` the same raw signed-complex coordinates at SOC50 and SOC90 (12 values plus masks).

These frequencies were fixed without endpoint outcomes, span three decades, exclude all four endpoint constituents, and have archive-wide corrected-complex finiteness of 99.878%, 99.830%, and 99.702% at 1000, 50, and 1 Hz. The inherited outcome-free held-condition audit found that the SOC90 and SOC50/90 panels reconstruct 84.7% and 88.5% of omitted standardized response variance. This makes 1/50/1000 Hz defensible as a prespecified sentinel panel, not as a unique optimum, a mechanistic decomposition, or a physically minimal scan. Use direct operating complex values; B-room already contains room counterparts. Corrected complex values, paired differences, and reciprocal-temperature secants are sensitivity representations, not separate packages. A fixed adjacent-grid panel at 3.125/67.5676/1470.5883 Hz and leave-one-frequency-out fits test frequency fragility without selecting a new package from forecast outcomes.

### Repeated source-index-frequency panel

`I5-4 = M5 +` the 20 operating raw amplitudes at 10, 2.0833, 0.5, and 0.2083 Hz across five SOCs, with masks. Recompute each four-frequency mean for audit but do not add the collinear mean. Phase is excluded so interpretation is specifically repeated access to the source index assay. Support confined here is repeat-assay persistence, not independent degradation diagnosis.

### Complete full-spectrum operating acquisition

`F5-29 = M5 +` the complete observed operating raw amplitude/phase grid at all 29 frequencies and five SOCs, reconstructed to signed complex values with masks. Apply the same masked spline projection and SVD ranks as B-room. It includes the four index frequencies and seven rows outside the 18-frequency corrected eligibility set. Report nested localization with I5-4 and the corrected 18-frequency non-index five-SOC surface, but F5-29 is the sole complete-acquisition reference for noninferiority.

This ladder estimates recorded information sufficiency under the historical room-first full-sweep procedure. Sparse panels were not physically collected alone. Their timestamps, thermal/rest trajectory, excitation history, and errors may depend on omitted scan portions. No contrast may be worded as protocol equivalence or time saving.

## Baseline and substantive learned alternative

The primary model is weighted ridge with block-specific penalties `10^-4,...,10^4`; rank and penalties are selected only in inner condition-held-out folds, with ties within 1% choosing lower rank and stronger regularization. It is selected because nested linear contrasts are auditable with only 57 independent conditions.

A substantive learned sensitivity fits shallow histogram gradient boosting separately to B-room, every shadow, and every package on the same future-level target, folds, weights, spline scores/masks, and forbidden-feature rules. Tune learning rate `{0.03,0.06}`, max leaf nodes `{7,15}`, minimum leaf size `{40,80}`, L2 `{1,10}`, at most 500 iterations with training-fold early stopping. It can reveal threshold or interaction-dependent package value that additive ridge loses. Primary decisions use ridge; a gain found only by boosting is inconclusive until stable across salts, strata, and pairing controls. Incremental cost is approximately 1–2 CPU-hours and <16 GiB. Neural sequences are deferred because only 57 independent conditions and no within-sweep timing are available. DRT/equivalent-circuit attribution is deferred because opaque conditions, fixed order, two non-simultaneous states, and absent equilibration/current logs make mechanism inversion nonunique.

## Held-condition inference, uncertainty, and controls

Assign conditions to five outer folds by sorting SHA-256 of `"KIT_EIS_package_v1:"+condition` within each approximately 0/10/40 °C stratum, then round-robin. Keep every specimen and visit of a condition together. Inner tuning repeats stratified condition-grouped folds. Save the fold map and repeat five prespecified salts as partition sensitivity.

For C conditions, m_c specimens and n_ci units, weight each unit `1/(C*m_c*n_ci)`. Pool every OOF prediction once. Report condition-balanced RMSE/MAE, calibration, per-condition/specimen losses, strata, age, lead, and first-transition cold start.

For package p and shadow M_p define `G_total,p=1-RMSE_p/RMSE_B-room`, `G_imp,p=1-RMSE_p/RMSE_Mp`, and only when F5-29 is supportive, `P_p=RMSE_p/RMSE_F5-29-1`. Bootstrap whole conditions 10,000 times within temperature stratum; report paired percentile/BCa intervals and leave-one-condition-out jackknife. This is sensitivity across 57 designed conditions, not a random protocol superpopulation or full training uncertainty.

Use the parent's auditable whole-specimen trajectory permutation in each of the 54 conditions retaining three specimens: enumerate five non-identity mappings; substitute the donor complete operating package at the same ordinal visit (nearest room-anchor age within 10.5 days only if absent); keep recipient shadow and label fixed; require >=90% coverage; form 10,000 stratum-balanced null draws. Other conditions remain in primary scoring but cannot adjudicate pairing.

Controls: near-isothermal pairs; strict SOC50/90 `|ΔOCV|<=20 mV` jointly with lag <=24 h (audited 1,545 units/158 specimens/55 conditions); cold/hot and leave-one-stratum-out; raw-versus-corrected/sign reconstruction; omission of SOC10 from the full package because its OCV mismatch is severe; the adjacent-grid and leave-one-frequency-out sparse diagnostics; 24/72 h visits; 18/18 eligibility; first transition; sparse-condition removal; complete-panel coordinates; package-availability cohort as selection diagnostic; fold salts; trajectory permutation; deliberate future-feature rejection; permuted labels. Report room-first lag and uniform source-counter offset without interpreting a completed cycle. Full-package support confined to SOC10 or to a high-missingness frequency is historical sequence/missingness information and is inconclusive for a state-matched package.

## Falsification and interpretation

The practical benefit threshold is 10% RMSE gain; 5% is the impedance-increment and package-noninferiority margin. These require expert review and are not proven economic optima.

- **Supportive reduced information package:** the first ordered package S90-3, S50/90-3, I5-4 with `G_total>=10%` and lower 95% bound >0, `G_imp>=5%` and lower bound >0, MAE not worse, gain above permutation 95th percentile, and upper 95% `P_p<5%`; controls do not reverse direction. Conclude only retrospective information sufficiency and recommend a prospective physical-package trial. If multiple packages pass, report the indistinguishable set and retained coordinate counts; do not rank by unobserved time or cost.
- **Complete acquisition warranted:** F5-29 total gain >=10% and impedance increment >=5%, both lower bounds >0, while every reduced package has lower 95% `P_p>5%`. The archive does not support discarding omitted information.
- **Metadata without EIS:** a shadow improves over B-room but matched impedance `G_imp` upper bound <5%. Attribute value only to state/timing metadata.
- **Repeated-assay localization:** I5-4 is sufficient but non-index packages are not. Conclude repeated endpoint-frequency persistence, not broad-spectrum or independent health value.
- **No useful operating package:** upper bounds for F5-29 and every total gain are below 5%, or all are worse with valid baseline/controls. Conclude no useful increment for this endpoint/horizon beyond complete room information.
- **Inconclusive:** F5-29 is not supportive; intervals cross 5–10%; pairing null is comparable; <45 conditions survive; methods/folds disagree; or OCV/lag/sign/visit/stratum controls reverse. If F5-29 is not useful, noninferiority cannot justify a package.

Near-isothermal support means repeated-measurement information, not temperature necessity. No result identifies causal thermal susceptibility, ageing mechanism, capacity, safety, or economic value. Preserve every adverse and inconclusive result.

## Deliverable, compute, and verifier boundary

The solver must newly construct the cohort and fit B-scalar, B-room, M90, S90-3, M50/90, S50/90-3, M5, I5-4, and F5-29 with ridge, plus boosting sensitivity. Completion requires:

- `audit.json, member_manifest.csv, frequency_map.csv, duplicate_resolution.csv, pairing_flow.csv, transitions.parquet`;
- `folds.json, room_features.parquet, metadata_shadows.parquet, sparse_features.parquet, index_panel_features.parquet, full29_features.parquet` and basis/SVD diagnostics;
- `predictions.parquet` with one OOF prediction per unit/model, `metrics.json, acquisition_frontier.json, uncertainty.json, trajectory_permutations.parquet, sensitivities.csv, conclusions.json` linking every conclusion to outputs and a decision rule.

Inherited audits used 4 CPUs/32 GiB and 85–141 s. The fit is estimated at 12–16 CPUs, 64 GiB, no GPU, and 5–8 h including nested folds, five salts, boosting, bootstraps, and permutations, within 16 CPUs/262,144 MiB/28,800 s. GPU use is unnecessary for these matrices; this is not a merit claim.

A verifier can recompute hashes, schemas, corrected sequence mapping, index identity, eligibility, chronology, cutoff, folds, weights, forbidden-feature absence (especially `eis_duration_s`), train-only transforms, predictions, metrics, uncertainty, permutations, and rule consistency. It must accept adverse/inconclusive conclusions and reject sparse claims based on reconstruction variance, outcome-selected frequencies, unmatched populations, a narrow “full” comparator, or asserted physical/time equivalence.

Scientific adjudication is required for whether 5%/10% is operationally valuable and whether a physical sparse device reproduces these masks. Stronger claims require a prospective trial acquiring packages independently with per-frequency timing, counterbalanced order, matched SOC/OCV/rest, current/equilibration logs, cost/energy accounting, an independent capacity or pulse endpoint, condition semantics, and external validation.

## Literature provenance

Luh and Blank, *Scientific Data* (2024), DOI `10.1038/s41597-024-03831-x`, was inspected through full public XML (PMCID `PMC11405776`; frozen source id `5c3de8fa937542c503c49aa0d7832107792c4f28fc8e9ad7cdadfe7403cbeabd`; SHA-256 `e55315f55e0b3ac2ce10deb1bcbe58a9babcac5e00a252ac058d27ee975ea115`). It supports cohort/check-up context; exact rows, grids, timing, package availability, and index identity come from archive inspection. Zhang et al. (2020), DOI `10.1038/s41467-020-15235-7`, is conceptual precedent only; full methods/supplements were not inspected here, and this is an adaptation, not a reproduction.

Required columns, present in the descriptor and raw archive, are filename-derived condition `P###`, replicate and specimen `P###_<replicate>`; audit-only hardware `S##,C##`; clocks/keys `timestamp_s,timestamp_origin,sd_block_id,uptime_ticks,seq_nr`; state/quality `cyc_charged,is_rt,soc_nom,valid,ocv_est_avg_V,t_avg_degC,eis_duration_s`; index `z_ref_init_mOhm,z_ref_now_mOhm,soh_imp`; and EIS `freq_Hz,z_amp_mOhm,z_ph_deg,z_amp_comp_mOhm,z_ph_comp_deg,z_re_comp_mOhm,z_im_comp_mOhm`. The spectrum key is `(specimen,timestamp_s,sd_block_id)`; the row key appends `seq_nr`. Units are seconds, Hz, mOhm, degrees, volts, and degrees Celsius as named in source headers.

The exact grid is `0:14705.8818, 1:10000, 2:6756.7568, 3:5000, 4:3125, 5:2083.3333, 6:1470.5883, 7:1000, 8:675.6757, 9:500, 10:312.5, 11:208.3333, 12:147.0588, 13:100, 14:67.5676, 15:50, 16:31.25, 17:20.8333, 18:14.7059, 19:10, 20:6.7568, 21:5, 22:3.125, 23:2.0833, 24:1, 25:0.5, 26:0.2083, 27:0.1, 28:0.05`. The fixed non-index panel is `seq_nr={7,15,24}`. The source-index panel is `{19,23,25,26}`. The quality-qualified corrected non-index set for eligibility is `{3,4,5,6,7,8,9,10,12,14,15,16,17,18,20,21,22,24}`.

Readiness verifies hashes, all schemas and filename identities, unique keys, within-spectrum metadata constancy, the common grid, and index reconstruction within 0.001 mOhm. Raw inspection found 35,275 rows at every sequence; raw amplitude/phase is finite for 35,232 spectra at most frequencies but only 30,701 at 100 Hz, so the full representation preserves missingness instead of requiring a complete raw grid.

## Frozen population, chronology, and future-safe endpoint

1. Within specimen, order spectrum keys by `timestamp_s`; start a visit after an adjacent gap greater than 48 h. Report 24 h and 72 h sensitivities and maximum chain-grouped duration.
2. For duplicate `(specimen,visit,is_rt,soc_nom)`, select among `valid=1` by `timestamp_origin=1`, then greatest count of finite corrected pairs on the 18-frequency eligibility grid, then earliest `timestamp_s,sd_block_id`. Never select by temperature proximity.
3. A room or operating state is complete when all five `soc_nom in {10,30,50,70,90}` are selected with at least 17/18 finite eligibility-grid pairs. One missing pair gets a mask; larger deficits are ineligible.
4. A unit at visit t requires immediately previous raw visit t-1 room-complete, current t room-and-operating-complete, and immediately next raw visit t+1 room-complete, without skipping a visit. Require an 18–24 day current-to-next room-anchor interval and `|median_SOC(T_op-T_rt)|>=8 °C`.
5. Define room anchor `A_v` as the median timestamp of five selected room spectra and `I_v=median_{SOC 30,50,70} z_ref_now_mOhm(v,SOC)`. The information cutoff is the maximum timestamp of all current predictors.
6. Fit future level `F_t=I_(t+1)`. Convert each OOF prediction to `Yhat_t=21*(Fhat_t-I_t)/h_t`, where `h_t=(A_(t+1)-A_t)/86400`, and score against `Y_t=21*(I_(t+1)-I_t)/h_t`. Future interval and completeness are never predictors or tuning features.
7. Assert every feature timestamp is at or before cutoff and every endpoint component is later. Inference is conditional on complete current room/operating measurements and a complete next check-up; report exclusions.

The audited primary population is 2,071 transitions, 167 specimens, and 57 conditions (approximately 573/697/801 transitions in 0/10/40 °C strata). Every primary model uses exactly these units. Package-specific availability populations are secondary selection diagnostics only.

## Same-population acquisition ladder

No model may use condition, specimen, hardware identity, absolute timestamp, future interval, or `eis_duration_s`. **`eis_duration_s` is prohibited from every predictive feature set, shadow, imputer, residualizer, interaction, and tuning rule.** It records the observed full sweep and may appear only in descriptive burden tables and outcome-free stratified sensitivity reports.

All representations use outer-training preprocessing and package-specific masks. For each impedance package, regress its impedance block on B-room plus its metadata shadow in outer training, apply unchanged to validation/test, and separately penalize the residual block. This yields an explicit shadow contrast without causal interpretation.

### B-scalar and B-room

`B-scalar` contains `I_t`, prior normalized index slope, log age, previous interval, current room temperature median/range, five room OCV values, origin/valid/finite/duplicate indicators, and `cyc_charged`; also report no-change, prior-slope persistence, and outer-training equal-condition mean-rate predictions.

`B-room`, the room-only decision baseline, adds the complete current five-SOC room acquisition: reconstruct signed complex values at all 29 frequencies as `z_amp_mOhm*(cos(z_ph_deg),sin(z_ph_deg))`, preserve coordinate masks, project each SOC/channel onto 10 fixed cubic B-splines over log10 frequency with masked ridge projection, standardize on outer training, and use outer-training SVD rank `q in {4,8,12,16,24,32}`. This strong baseline makes each operating package incremental to all recorded room information.

### Package-specific metadata shadows

`M90` adds only SOC90 operating temperature, temperature and reciprocal-temperature differences, OCV and OCV difference, room-to-operating lag, source-counter difference, timestamp-origin, valid/finite/missing indicators, and temperature stratum. `M50/90` adds the same fields for SOC50 and SOC90. `M5` adds them for all five SOCs. None includes operating impedance, duration, identity, or absolute time. Each package is compared with its exact shadow and B-room.

### Fixed sparse non-index packages

`S90-3 = M90 +` operating raw signed-complex impedance reconstructed from `z_amp_mOhm,z_ph_deg` at SOC90 and 1000/50/1 Hz (six values plus masks).

`S50/90-3 = M50/90 +` the same raw signed-complex coordinates at SOC50 and SOC90 (12 values plus masks).

These frequencies were fixed without endpoint outcomes, span three decades, exclude all four endpoint constituents, and have archive-wide corrected-complex finiteness of 99.878%, 99.830%, and 99.702% at 1000, 50, and 1 Hz. The inherited outcome-free held-condition audit found that the SOC90 and SOC50/90 panels reconstruct 84.7% and 88.5% of omitted standardized response variance. This makes 1/50/1000 Hz defensible as a prespecified sentinel panel, not as a unique optimum, a mechanistic decomposition, or a physically minimal scan. Use direct operating complex values; B-room already contains room counterparts. Corrected complex values, paired differences, and reciprocal-temperature secants are sensitivity representations, not separate packages. A fixed adjacent-grid panel at 3.125/67.5676/1470.5883 Hz and leave-one-frequency-out fits test frequency fragility without selecting a new package from forecast outcomes.

### Repeated source-index-frequency panel

`I5-4 = M5 +` the 20 operating raw amplitudes at 10, 2.0833, 0.5, and 0.2083 Hz across five SOCs, with masks. Recompute each four-frequency mean for audit but do not add the collinear mean. Phase is excluded so interpretation is specifically repeated access to the source index assay. Support confined here is repeat-assay persistence, not independent degradation diagnosis.

### Complete full-spectrum operating acquisition

`F5-29 = M5 +` the complete observed operating raw amplitude/phase grid at all 29 frequencies and five SOCs, reconstructed to signed complex values with masks. Apply the same masked spline projection and SVD ranks as B-room. It includes the four index frequencies and seven rows outside the 18-frequency corrected eligibility set. Report nested localization with I5-4 and the corrected 18-frequency non-index five-SOC surface, but F5-29 is the sole complete-acquisition reference for noninferiority.

This ladder estimates recorded information sufficiency under the historical room-first full-sweep procedure. Sparse panels were not physically collected alone. Their timestamps, thermal/rest trajectory, excitation history, and errors may depend on omitted scan portions. No contrast may be worded as protocol equivalence or time saving.

## Baseline and substantive learned alternative

The primary model is weighted ridge with block-specific penalties `10^-4,...,10^4`; rank and penalties are selected only in inner condition-held-out folds, with ties within 1% choosing lower rank and stronger regularization. It is selected because nested linear contrasts are auditable with only 57 independent conditions.

A substantive learned sensitivity fits shallow histogram gradient boosting separately to B-room, every shadow, and every package on the same future-level target, folds, weights, spline scores/masks, and forbidden-feature rules. Tune learning rate `{0.03,0.06}`, max leaf nodes `{7,15}`, minimum leaf size `{40,80}`, L2 `{1,10}`, at most 500 iterations with training-fold early stopping. It can reveal threshold or interaction-dependent package value that additive ridge loses. Primary decisions use ridge; a gain found only by boosting is inconclusive until stable across salts, strata, and pairing controls. Incremental cost is approximately 1–2 CPU-hours and <16 GiB. Neural sequences are deferred because only 57 independent conditions and no within-sweep timing are available. DRT/equivalent-circuit attribution is deferred because opaque conditions, fixed order, two non-simultaneous states, and absent equilibration/current logs make mechanism inversion nonunique.

## Held-condition inference, uncertainty, and controls

Assign conditions to five outer folds by sorting SHA-256 of `"KIT_EIS_package_v1:"+condition` within each approximately 0/10/40 °C stratum, then round-robin. Keep every specimen and visit of a condition together. Inner tuning repeats stratified condition-grouped folds. Save the fold map and repeat five prespecified salts as partition sensitivity.

For C conditions, m_c specimens and n_ci units, weight each unit `1/(C*m_c*n_ci)`. Pool every OOF prediction once. Report condition-balanced RMSE/MAE, calibration, per-condition/specimen losses, strata, age, lead, and first-transition cold start.

For package p and shadow M_p define `G_total,p=1-RMSE_p/RMSE_B-room`, `G_imp,p=1-RMSE_p/RMSE_Mp`, and only when F5-29 is supportive, `P_p=RMSE_p/RMSE_F5-29-1`. Bootstrap whole conditions 10,000 times within temperature stratum; report paired percentile/BCa intervals and leave-one-condition-out jackknife. This is sensitivity across 57 designed conditions, not a random protocol superpopulation or full training uncertainty.

Use the parent's auditable whole-specimen trajectory permutation in each of the 54 conditions retaining three specimens: enumerate five non-identity mappings; substitute the donor complete operating package at the same ordinal visit (nearest room-anchor age within 10.5 days only if absent); keep recipient shadow and label fixed; require >=90% coverage; form 10,000 stratum-balanced null draws. Other conditions remain in primary scoring but cannot adjudicate pairing.

Controls: near-isothermal pairs; strict SOC50/90 `|ΔOCV|<=20 mV` jointly with lag <=24 h (audited 1,545 units/158 specimens/55 conditions); cold/hot and leave-one-stratum-out; raw-versus-corrected/sign reconstruction; omission of SOC10 from the full package because its OCV mismatch is severe; the adjacent-grid and leave-one-frequency-out sparse diagnostics; 24/72 h visits; 18/18 eligibility; first transition; sparse-condition removal; complete-panel coordinates; package-availability cohort as selection diagnostic; fold salts; trajectory permutation; deliberate future-feature rejection; permuted labels. Report room-first lag and uniform source-counter offset without interpreting a completed cycle. Full-package support confined to SOC10 or to a high-missingness frequency is historical sequence/missingness information and is inconclusive for a state-matched package.

## Falsification and interpretation

The practical benefit threshold is 10% RMSE gain; 5% is the impedance-increment and package-noninferiority margin. These require expert review and are not proven economic optima.

- **Supportive reduced information package:** the first ordered package S90-3, S50/90-3, I5-4 with `G_total>=10%` and lower 95% bound >0, `G_imp>=5%` and lower bound >0, MAE not worse, gain above permutation 95th percentile, and upper 95% `P_p<5%`; controls do not reverse direction. Conclude only retrospective information sufficiency and recommend a prospective physical-package trial. If multiple packages pass, report the indistinguishable set and retained coordinate counts; do not rank by unobserved time or cost.
- **Complete acquisition warranted:** F5-29 total gain >=10% and impedance increment >=5%, both lower bounds >0, while every reduced package has lower 95% `P_p>5%`. The archive does not support discarding omitted information.
- **Metadata without EIS:** a shadow improves over B-room but matched impedance `G_imp` upper bound <5%. Attribute value only to state/timing metadata.
- **Repeated-assay localization:** I5-4 is sufficient but non-index packages are not. Conclude repeated endpoint-frequency persistence, not broad-spectrum or independent health value.
- **No useful operating package:** upper bounds for F5-29 and every total gain are below 5%, or all are worse with valid baseline/controls. Conclude no useful increment for this endpoint/horizon beyond complete room information.
- **Inconclusive:** F5-29 is not supportive; intervals cross 5–10%; pairing null is comparable; <45 conditions survive; methods/folds disagree; or OCV/lag/sign/visit/stratum controls reverse. If F5-29 is not useful, noninferiority cannot justify a package.

Near-isothermal support means repeated-measurement information, not temperature necessity. No result identifies causal thermal susceptibility, ageing mechanism, capacity, safety, or economic value. Preserve every adverse and inconclusive result.

## Deliverable, compute, and verifier boundary

The solver must newly construct the cohort and fit B-scalar, B-room, M90, S90-3, M50/90, S50/90-3, M5, I5-4, and F5-29 with ridge, plus boosting sensitivity. Completion requires:

- `audit.json, member_manifest.csv, frequency_map.csv, duplicate_resolution.csv, pairing_flow.csv, transitions.parquet`;
- `folds.json, room_features.parquet, metadata_shadows.parquet, sparse_features.parquet, index_panel_features.parquet, full29_features.parquet` and basis/SVD diagnostics;
- `predictions.parquet` with one OOF prediction per unit/model, `metrics.json, acquisition_frontier.json, uncertainty.json, trajectory_permutations.parquet, sensitivities.csv, conclusions.json` linking every conclusion to outputs and a decision rule.

Inherited audits used 4 CPUs/32 GiB and 85–141 s. The fit is estimated at 12–16 CPUs, 64 GiB, no GPU, and 5–8 h including nested folds, five salts, boosting, bootstraps, and permutations, within 16 CPUs/262,144 MiB/28,800 s. GPU use is unnecessary for these matrices; this is not a merit claim.

A verifier can recompute hashes, schemas, corrected sequence mapping, index identity, eligibility, chronology, cutoff, folds, weights, forbidden-feature absence (especially `eis_duration_s`), train-only transforms, predictions, metrics, uncertainty, permutations, and rule consistency. It must accept adverse/inconclusive conclusions and reject sparse claims based on reconstruction variance, outcome-selected frequencies, unmatched populations, a narrow “full” comparator, or asserted physical/time equivalence.

Scientific adjudication is required for whether 5%/10% is operationally valuable and whether a physical sparse device reproduces these masks. Stronger claims require a prospective trial acquiring packages independently with per-frequency timing, counterbalanced order, matched SOC/OCV/rest, current/equilibration logs, cost/energy accounting, an independent capacity or pulse endpoint, condition semantics, and external validation.

## Literature provenance

Luh and Blank, *Scientific Data* (2024), DOI `10.1038/s41597-024-03831-x`, was inspected through full public XML (PMCID `PMC11405776`; frozen source id `5c3de8fa937542c503c49aa0d7832107792c4f28fc8e9ad7cdadfe7403cbeabd`; SHA-256 `e55315f55e0b3ac2ce10deb1bcbe58a9babcac5e00a252ac058d27ee975ea115`). It supports cohort/check-up context; exact rows, grids, timing, package availability, and index identity come from archive inspection. Zhang et al. (2020), DOI `10.1038/s41467-020-15235-7`, is conceptual precedent only; full methods/supplements were not inspected here, and this is an adaptation, not a reproduction.

# Li2025 paired-path two-RPT forecast experiment

## Objective and evidence boundary

Determine whether the evolution of same-RPT low-rate charge–discharge path separation adds forecast information for directly measured capacity and scheduled resistance two RPTs later beyond scalar history, acquisition conditions, and the evolving discharge curve alone.

This is an open-ended estimation task. No fitted answer is supplied. Existing evidence establishes feasibility only: the archive contains 17 longitudinally paired specimens in E1 and E5, with 212 eligible capacity responses and 110 eligible resistance responses before chronological scoring. The hypothesis is unresolved.

A complete submission must newly extract the bound measurements, construct the frozen cohort and chronology, fit all specified models, make out-of-specimen predictions, quantify uncertainty and controls, and issue rule-coded endpoint conclusions. Replotting curves, reproducing the availability counts, or calculating same-RPT capacity is not completion.

The result is an electrical prognostic association under the represented E1/E5 schedules. It cannot identify a degradation reaction or mode, establish causality, treat E1/E5 as independent cohorts, claim that future dose was known at time t, or establish transfer to another chemistry or protocol. Those stronger claims need electrochemical expert adjudication, phase-specific thermodynamic/kinetic measurements, controlled future-dose interventions, and an independent paired-curve cohort.

## Immutable inputs and population

Read only:

- `/data/d740a0fd11-li-full.zip`, SHA-256 `51e37532a759e1a3bed1f05dd17b682eca0eb38c132c37481c534baf4526e42c`
- `/data/a90f68c3f0-catalog-v06.json`, SHA-256 `02afcb6c55ac8d6d1801f4d4ed51adaa45743e5a3461f9c468a1ecf85cf4d8b5`

The complete frozen 509-member analysis list is available at `/opt/task/li2025-required-members.txt`; use exactly those members and reproduce the list in `source_audit.json`.

Use only these exact experiment directories:

- E1: `SimSave/InputData/Expt 1 - Si-based Degradation`; cells A, B, D, E, F, J, K, L, M.
- E5: `SimSave/InputData/Expt 5 - Standard Cycle Aging (Control)`; cells A–H.

Treat E1 and E5 as opaque family labels, not mechanisms. A specimen identifier is the exact experiment directory joined with `|` and the cell letter.

Curve archive-member pattern:

`SimSave/InputData/{experiment}/0.1C Voltage Curves/cell {cell}/{short} - cell {cell} - RPT{rpt} - 0.1C {charge|discharge} data.csv`

Required curve columns after stripping header whitespace are `Time (s)`, `Voltage (V)`, `Current (mA)`, `Charge (mA.h)`, and `Temperature (degC)`.

Summary-member pattern:

`SimSave/InputData/{experiment}/{short} - cell {cell} ({10|25|40}degC) - Extracted Data.csv`

Required summary columns are `Unnamed: 0` (the CSV's unnamed RPT index), `Ageing Sets`, `Ageing Cycles`, `Age set start date`, `Age set end date`, `RPT start date`, `Days of degradation`, `Age set average temperature (degC)`, `Charge Throughput (A.h)`, `Energy Throughput (W.h)`, `C/10 Capacity (mA.h)`, `C/2 Capacity (mA.h)`, `0.1s Resistance (Ohms)`, `Mean_R (Ohms)`, `R_80to48_SOC (Ohms)`, and `R_100SOC (Ohms)`.

Join by exact experiment directory, cell, and integer RPT parsed from the member/index. Parse `RPT start date` day-first. Within each specimen require one-to-one charge/discharge/summary keys, strictly increasing dates, and sequential RPT 0…n−1. Abort on a source hash, schema, key, phase, or chronology failure. E3 has only three RPT0 charge curves and is excluded; E2/E4 have no charge curves.

## Endpoints and temporal boundary

For specimen i and index RPT t:

- capacity: `y_capacity = (C[t+2] - C[t]) / C[0]`, where C is `C/10 Capacity (mA.h)`;
- resistance: `y_resistance = log(R[t+2] / R[t])`, where positive R is `Mean_R (Ohms)`.

Never impute an outcome. Resistance is scored only when both scheduled measurements exist. Expected pre-scoring eligibility is E1 100/E5 112 capacity rows and E1 54/E5 56 resistance rows.

Every predictor must be available by the end of RPT t. Do not use any t+1/t+2 capacity, resistance, curve, date, throughput, ageing temperature, achieved exposure, or future dose. Do not use DMA, fitted capacity/parameters, simulations, or family-folder text as a predictor. The naturally scheduled two-interval future dose is hidden; within-family performance is protocol-conditional.

## Curve representation and acquisition controls

Filter nominal 0.1C records to +450…+550 mA for charge and −550…−450 mA for discharge. Require monotone active time and phase-local `Charge (mA.h)`. The charge counter is not SOC ground truth.

For each phase independently define:

- `s_D = 1 - (Q-Qmin)/(Qmax-Qmin)`
- `s_C = (Q-Qmin)/(Qmax-Qmin)`

Interpolate voltage at 97 coordinates `s=0.02,0.03,…,0.98` within each phase's own span. Do not extrapolate one phase to the other's endpoint and do not describe equal normalized coordinates as identical SOC. Retain discharge span, charge span, ratio, median current, median temperature, and measured phase gap before normalization.

Relative to the same specimen's RPT0 pair construct `delta_D(t,s)`, `delta_C(t,s)`, and `A(t,s)=[V_C(t,s)-V_D(t,s)]-[V_C(0,s)-V_D(0,s)]`. Remove each curve's least-squares affine component in s before it enters a morphology channel. Residualize paired morphology against both phase temperatures/currents and span measures using training data only. Keep RPT0 paired shape only for S0.

Required representation sensitivities are the empirically common voltage interval and the interior grid `s=0.10,…,0.90`. A direction-swap control must exchange charge/discharge blocks and algebraically reverse separation.

## Frozen validation and models

Primary evaluation is chronological within-family leave-one-specimen-out. For each held row, training may include only other specimens in the same family whose target date is strictly earlier than the held row's index date. Require at least 20 training rows and four training specimens. Expected scored rows are E1 61/E5 73 capacity and E1 30/E5 33 resistance. All imputers, scalers, residualizers, feature transforms, RPT0 references, model selection, target scaling, and conformal residuals are training-only. Inner selection repeats the specimen/date discipline. Random row splits are forbidden.

Reciprocal-family stress tests use the same date rule and no family token. Report train-E5/test-E1 and train-E1/test-E5 separately. They are hidden-action extrapolations, not evidence of family transport or independent replication.

Fit each endpoint separately on identical eligible outer rows:

- P0: training median response within family and nominal-temperature stratum, falling back to family median.
- B0: standardized ridge over `10^-4,…,10^4`, selected by inner chronological specimen folds. Inputs are current C/C0, backward capacity differences and Theil–Sen slope; latest observed R/R0, staleness, missing-history indicators and backward even-RPT resistance changes; RPT index; cumulative cycles, days, Ah and Wh through t; nominal ageing temperature; phase spans/ratio, median currents/temperatures and phase gap.
- D1: B0 plus signed area, absolute area and RMS of detrended delta_D in five fixed s windows, and fixed-rule derivative-extrema locations/prominences after Savitzky–Golay order 3/window 11.
- D2: B0 plus all 97 detrended, acquisition-adjusted delta_D coordinates. Fit a PLS residual correction with 1–8 rank-bounded components selected by inner folds. Its target is cross-fitted B0 residual, never an in-sample residual.
- S0: replace evolving blocks with RPT0 discharge, charge and static separation; use P2 preprocessing/component grids and the same scalar acquisition variables.
- P1: D1 plus the same fixed summaries of delta_C and A.
- P2: D2 plus all 97 adjusted delta_C and A coordinates. Fit training-only PCA separately for delta_D, delta_C and A (1–6 components per block), then ridge on cross-fitted D2 residuals; tune block counts and alpha in the same inner folds.

The primary contrast is P2−D2; also report P2−S0, P1−D1 and D2−B0. P1 sign agreement is interpretive and cannot rescue P2.

## Metrics, uncertainty, and controls

For each endpoint/model, average absolute error first over scored RPTs within specimen, then over specimens within family, then give E1 and E5 equal weight. Define `I = 1 - MAE(P2)/MAE(D2)`. Also report RMSE, reconstructed absolute-state error, family and specimen effects, and E1/E5 effect signs. Score capacity again on resistance-complete rows; never pool endpoints into an unscaled loss.

Use 10,000 paired hierarchical bootstrap replicates. Resample specimens with replacement within each fixed family and retain complete trajectories. Use NumPy `Generator(PCG64(20250923))`, sorted specimen IDs, and draw E1 then E5 for each replicate. The interval describes these specimens and families, not a family superpopulation. Compute descriptive training-only group-conformal 90% intervals and report coverage/width by endpoint/family.

Run and retain numeric outputs for:

1. capacity-span ablation with span, ratio and C(t) in both D2 and P2;
2. P2 versus S0 overall and in each family;
3. 1,000 within-specimen time permutations of delta_C/A, separately in training and held data;
4. same-family/same-temperature static RPT0 charge-pair permutation;
5. direction swap, which must be invariant after refitting within `max_abs_prediction_difference <= 1e-8`;
6. t−2 paired-evolution lag;
7. complete target-trajectory shuffle within training family/temperature;
8. acquisition residualization remove/retain comparison;
9. common-voltage and s=0.10…0.90 support sensitivities;
10. resistance repeats using `0.1s Resistance`, `R_80to48_SOC`, and `R_100SOC`, with median absolute error, Huber fit, and leave-one-specimen-out influence. Do not discard the E5|A excursion.

Protocol/family classifiers using RPT0, discharge evolution and paired evolution are diagnostics only; their predictability does not prove confounding or mechanism.

## Frozen conclusions

For each endpoint label the result exactly one of `supportive`, `adverse`, `inconclusive`, or `invalid`.

Support requires all of: point improvement at least 0.10 and 95% bootstrap lower bound above zero; positive E1 and E5 effects with neither worse than −0.05; P2 beats S0 overall and in both families; P1−D1 agrees in sign; time permutation removes the advantage; target shuffle removes it; capacity-span, acquisition, common-voltage, interior-support and lag controls do not reverse sign; no single specimen removes the sign; and, for resistance, at least two alternative resistance definitions agree.

Provided computation is valid and controls do not force inconclusive status, a bootstrap upper bound below 0.10 is adverse at the planned effect size; an upper bound at or below zero supports no detectable benefit or harm. If D2 matches P2 after span/acquisition controls, paired morphology adds no detectable information beyond discharge. If S0 matches P2, narrow apparent value to static identity/protocol.

Inconclusive includes an interval crossing zero or 0.10, conflicting E1/E5 effects, P1/P2 conflict, dependence on one specimen or resistance definition, sign reversal under common-voltage/acquisition adjustment, equal lag performance, failed calibration, or retained time-permutation advantage. A retained target-shuffle advantage is invalid. Other invalid conditions are source/schema/join/chronology or phase-coordinate failures, leakage, target imputation, row-random splitting, training on held specimens, or treating post-index dose as known at t.

The joint hypothesis is supportive only if both endpoints are supportive. Preserve endpoint-specific results. Reciprocal-family success alone is inconclusive for transport, and failure does not refute within-family information.

## Required outputs and auditability

Write all outputs under `/workspace`:

- `source_audit.json`: `mode="real"`; source hashes; `archive_members` containing exactly the 509 analysis members (246 charge, 246 discharge, 17 summary); `join_keys=["experiment_directory","cell","rpt"]`; `time_field="RPT start date"`; `date_parse_dayfirst=true`; required columns; counts; signs; spans; phase gaps; join/chronology checks; and named boolean `invalidity_flags`.
- `eligible_rows.parquet`: one row per endpoint/specimen/t with source values and computed target.
- `folds.csv`: one row per scored endpoint/specimen/t with held fold, index/target dates, training row/specimen counts, and latest training target date.
- `features_schema.json`: every feature, source time, units, channel/model membership, and leakage status.
- `curve_cache.parquet`: specimen/RPT/s coordinates and raw, normalized, detrended and adjusted phase channels plus spans/acquisition variables.
- `predictions.parquet`: columns `endpoint,family,specimen_id,rpt_t,index_date,target_date,outer_fold_id,model,y_true,y_pred,lower90,upper90` for P0/B0/D1/D2/S0/P1/P2 on identical rows.
- `metrics.json`: specimen-balanced metrics, contrasts, bootstrap bounds, rule-coded endpoint/joint conclusions, and `claim_scope` exactly recording prognostic-association-only true and mechanism, causal-effect, independent-external-validation, cross-protocol-transfer, and future-dose-known claims false.
- `bootstrap.parquet`: all 10,000 replicates per endpoint with D2/P2 MAE and improvement.
- `calibration.json`: 90% group-conformal coverage/width by endpoint and family.

The private verifier recomputes outcome arithmetic, split invariants, prediction coverage, specimen-balanced metrics, deterministic bootstrap values, and decision-rule consistency. It validates adverse and inconclusive outcomes as well as supportive ones and rejects unsupported conclusions. It does not establish scientific truth or microscopic interpretation. Readiness checks only imports, mounts, representative headers, and a tiny synthetic contract; they do not solve this experiment.

# Time-t paired low-rate path information for measured two-RPT response in Li2025

## Decision, unresolved question, and scientific advance

This child makes the deferred paired charge-discharge question primary:

**Does the evolution of low-rate charge-discharge path separation at RPT t add forecast information for directly measured capacity and scheduled resistance response at t+2 beyond scalar history, acquisition conditions, and the evolving discharge curve alone?**

The operational distinction is consequential. A second low-rate direction adds diagnostic time and energy. If paired-path information does not improve a strict time-t forecast, discharge alone is the better-supported diagnostic for this archive. If it does improve, paired acquisition is worth retaining for future validation—but the result remains an electrical prognostic association, not identification of a reaction or degradation mode.

The strongest evidence now supported is feasibility: E1 and E5 contain longitudinal paired curves for 17 specimens and provide 212 directly measured C/10-capacity responses and 110 scheduled Mean_R responses at the two-RPT horizon. Charge follows discharge by about 6.008 hours; it is therefore available by the end of the same RPT, not before the RPT begins. The unresolved claim is incremental future information. No forecast model has been fit, and no positive result is claimed.

This is a bounded adaptation of the parent, not a reproduction of Li et al. Li/Kirkaldy share one experimental lineage. Family folder descriptions are opaque E1/E5 labels in analysis and are not mechanisms or independent cohorts.

## Hypotheses, endpoints, and deliverable

For specimen i, let C be summary `C/10 Capacity (mA.h)` and R be positive summary `Mean_R (Ohms)`. For index RPT t:

- capacity response: Y-C(i,t) = [C(i,t+2)-C(i,t)] / C(i,0);
- resistance response: Y-R(i,t) = log[R(i,t+2)/R(i,t)], only where both scheduled measurements exist.

The horizon is fixed at t+2 because resistance is measured at every even RPT and absent at every odd RPT. No outcome is imputed.

Primary hypothesis H-C: on the same rows and frozen chronological specimen splits, the learned paired-curve model P2 reduces specimen-balanced capacity-response MAE by at least 10% versus the full discharge model D2.

Key secondary H-R applies the same contrast and threshold to scheduled resistance response. A joint paired-diagnostic claim requires both endpoints to satisfy the rules. Capacity-only or resistance-only support is endpoint-specific.

The actual deliverable is newly fitted, out-of-specimen predictions from B0 scalar history, D1 structured discharge, D2 learned discharge, P1 structured paired asymmetry, and P2 learned paired curves; uncertainty, support diagnostics, controls, calibration, and one rule-coded conclusion per endpoint. Replotting curves or computing same-RPT capacity is not completion.

## Population, temporal boundaries, and exact audit

A specimen is `experiment directory|cell letter`, never cell letter alone. E1 has 9 specimens and 118 paired states; E5 has 8 specimens and 128 paired states. After requiring t+2:

| family | specimens | capacity rows | resistance rows | index t |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| E1 | 9 | 100 | 54 | 0-12 |
| E5 | 8 | 112 | 56 | 0-13 |
| total | 17 | 212 | 110 | |

E3 has only three charge curves, all at RPT0 for three specimens, yielding three t=0 forecasts. These are insufficient for a longitudinal asymmetry model and are excluded before analysis; they may be listed as availability evidence only. E2/E4 have no charge curves.

Primary validation is chronological within-family leave-one-specimen-out (LOSO). For each held row, training contains only other specimens in the same family whose **target date is strictly earlier than the held index date**. Require at least 20 training rows and four training specimens. The audit yields:

- E1: 61 capacity and 30 resistance scored rows across all 9 specimens, index dates 2020-11-24 to 2021-04-28;
- E5: 73 capacity and 33 resistance scored rows across all 8 specimens, index dates 2020-10-15 to 2021-05-10.

This is a deliberately strict hindcast of deployment after an initial labeled history exists. It does not score early RPTs for which no prior target history exists.

Reciprocal-family validation is a prespecified stress test using the same date rule and no family token=[redacted] E5/test E1 gives 75 capacity and 39 resistance rows; train E1/test E5 gives 72 and 32. It cannot establish family transport because E1's two-RPT ageing dose is always 514 cycles and E5's is always 156. The held family is perfectly aligned with future dose and protocol. Report the two directions separately; never pool them as independent replication.

## Immutable source and table bindings

Read-only source `li_full`:

- source: `[private path]`
- runtime: `/data/d740a0fd11-li-full.zip`
- SHA-256: `51e37532a759e1a3bed1f05dd17b682eca0eb38c132c37481c534baf4526e42c`

Catalog:

- source: `[private path]`
- runtime: `/data/a90f68c3f0-catalog-v06.json`
- SHA-256: `02afcb6c55ac8d6d1801f4d4ed51adaa45743e5a3461f9c468a1ecf85cf4d8b5`

The supporting `li2025_paired_binding_manifest.csv` enumerates 800 catalog tables: 249 charge curves, 511 discharge curves, and 40 summaries. All required catalog columns were found. The 509 analysis-required E1/E5 bindings are 246 charge, 246 discharge, and 17 summary tables.

Curve table pattern:
`li_full/SimSave/InputData/{experiment}/0.1C Voltage Curves/cell {cell}/{experiment-short} - cell {cell} - RPT{rpt} - 0.1C {charge|discharge} data.csv`

Required curve columns: `Time (s)`, `Voltage (V)`, `Current (mA)`, `Charge (mA.h)`, `Temperature (degC)`.

Summary pattern:
`li_full/SimSave/InputData/{experiment}/{experiment-short} - cell {cell} ({10|25|40}degC) - Extracted Data.csv`

Required summary columns: unnamed RPT index (catalog `""`, pandas `Unnamed: 0`), `Ageing Sets`, `Ageing Cycles`, `Age set start date`, `Age set end date`, `RPT start date`, `Days of degradation`, `Age set average temperature (degC)`, `Charge Throughput (A.h)`, `Energy Throughput (W.h)`, `C/10 Capacity (mA.h)`, `C/2 Capacity (mA.h)`, `0.1s Resistance (Ohms)`, `Mean_R (Ohms)`, `R_80to48_SOC (Ohms)`, and `R_100SOC (Ohms)`.

Join by exact experiment directory, cell, and integer RPT parsed from each member. Parse `RPT start date` day-first, sort within specimen, and require sequential RPT 0..n-1 and one-to-one phase/summary keys. Abort on hash, schema, key, or chronology failure.

## Measurement conventions and paired representation

At nominal 0.1C, retain +450 to +550 mA on charge and -550 to -450 mA on discharge. The audit found all 760 curves share the five-column schema and have monotone active time and `Charge (mA.h)`. Charge medians are +499.777 to +500.388 mA, discharge -500.199 to -499.573 mA. Median curve temperatures span 24.695-29.798 C for charge and 21.492-29.625 C for discharge.

`Charge (mA.h)` is a phase-local coulomb counter, not SOC ground truth. Define:

- discharge coordinate s-D = 1-(Q-Qmin)/(Qmax-Qmin);
- charge coordinate s-C = (Q-Qmin)/(Qmax-Qmin).

Both run from low to high state of charge. Interpolate voltage on s=0.02,...,0.98 only. Terminal voltages are finite-rate cutoff observations, not equilibrium OCV anchors.

Charge and discharge do not span identical capacity: across all 249 paired states the charge/discharge span ratio has median 0.969, 5th-95th percentile 0.893-0.984, and minimum 0.618. Therefore **do not extrapolate one phase to the other's endpoints and do not call equal normalized coordinates identical SOC**. Primary pairing uses only the 2-98% interior of each phase's own span and supplies both span ratio and absolute spans to every paired model. Sensitivities restrict each state to its empirically common voltage interval and to s=0.10,...,0.90. A sign-reversing direction-swap control is required.

Before normalization, retain discharge span, charge span, their ratio, median current, temperature, and the 6.008-hour phase gap as scalar acquisition controls. Curve temperature difference has median 0.205 C but ranges -0.512 to 1.804 C; paired features must be residualized against both phase temperatures/currents and span measures using training data only.

Represent evolution relative to that specimen's RPT0 pair:

- delta-D(t,s) = V-D(t,s)-V-D(0,s);
- delta-C(t,s) = V-C(t,s)-V-C(0,s);
- evolving asymmetry A(t,s) = [V-C(t,s)-V-D(t,s)] - [V-C(0,s)-V-D(0,s)].

Remove each curve's least-squares affine component in s before the morphology channel. This prevents bulk offset/tilt, endpoint span, and current capacity from masquerading as paired morphology. RPT0 paired shape is retained only as a static-identity control.

## Time-t inputs and future-action boundary

Every predictor is available by the end of RPT t. B0 uses:

- current C(t)/C(0), backward capacity differences and Theil-Sen slope;
- latest observed R/R(0), staleness, missing-history indicators, and backward even-RPT resistance changes;
- RPT index; cumulative ageing cycles, days, charge Ah and energy Wh through t;
- nominal ageing temperature;
- discharge and charge spans, their ratio, phase median currents/temperatures, and phase gap.

No t+1 or t+2 capacity, resistance, curve, date, throughput, ageing temperature, or achieved exposure enters a predictor. No DMA, fitted capacity, fitted parameter, simulation, family-folder text, or future dose is used.

The unknown-use boundary is explicit: the model forecasts the response under the naturally scheduled next two ageing intervals without being told their realized dose. Because scheduled future cycle dose is family-fixed and different (514 E1; 156 E5), primary within-family performance is protocol-conditional. Reciprocal-family performance is extrapolation under a hidden action shift, not a common-support causal comparison.

## Comparable alternatives and retained information

All models use identical endpoint rows, outer predictions, target scaling, and training-only preprocessing.

**P0 trivial:** training median response within family and nominal-temperature strata, falling back to family median.

**B0 scalar/history:** separate standardized ridge fits per endpoint, alpha in 10^-4,...,10^4 selected by inner chronological specimen folds. It retains measured state, history, capacity spans, acquisition conditions, and protocol-conditional time, but loses voltage morphology.

**D1 structured discharge:** add fixed signed/absolute areas and RMS of detrended delta-D in five s windows plus fixed-rule derivative-extrema locations/prominences after Savitzky-Golay order 3/window 11. It can localize predictive discharge regions but cannot identify electrode reactions.

**D2 learned discharge:** add all 97 detrended, condition-adjusted delta-D coordinates to B0. Fit a PLS residual correction with 1-8 components, rank-bounded and selected by inner chronological specimen validation. The target is cross-fitted B0 residual, never an in-sample residual. It preserves distributed discharge deformation that D1 summaries lose.

**S0 static paired identity:** replace every evolving block with the RPT0 discharge curve, RPT0 charge curve, and their static separation, using P2 preprocessing and component grids. It tests whether batch/specimen/protocol identity in the baseline pair, rather than evolving path information, carries the gain.

**P1 structured asymmetry:** augment D1 with fixed window summaries of delta-C and A, plus charge/discharge span ratio and temperature difference already in B0. This tests interpretable phase-specific and path-separation changes.

**P2 learned paired curves (primary):** augment D2 with all 97 condition-adjusted delta-C and A coordinates. Fit a group-regularized residual model: training-only PCA separately for delta-D, delta-C, and A (1-6 components per block), followed by ridge on cross-fitted D2 residuals; tune components and alpha in the same inner splits. P2 retains where charge and discharge evolve together versus oppositely and distributed asymmetry that P1 summaries lose. It does not infer why.

Primary contrasts are P2-D2 and P2-S0. P1 must agree in sign for interpretability but cannot rescue failed P2. D2-B0 is reported to establish whether discharge itself adds information on this reduced population. A neural sequence model is deferred: 17 specimens do not justify higher capacity before stable P2 residual signal. Revisit with at least 30 additional paired specimens or reproducible underfit patterns. A mechanistic electrode model is deferred because independent half-cell states, phase-specific thermodynamic anchors, and mechanism truth are unavailable.

Approximate future solver budget: 8 CPU, 32 GiB, zero GPU, 7200 s. Extraction of 509 required members and nested low-rank/ridge fits should be comfortably CPU-bound; the full audit read 800 bindings in about 28 s with 4 CPU/8 GiB. GPU use would not add scientific value here.

## Splits, metrics, uncertainty, and controls

Primary outer evaluation is the chronological within-family LOSO rule above. All transforms, RPT0 references, imputers, residualizers, PCA/PLS bases, penalties, component counts, target scales, and conformal residuals exclude the held specimen and all rows failing the target-date cutoff. Inner selection uses the same specimen/date discipline. No random row split is allowed.

For each endpoint/model, average absolute error over scored RPTs within specimen, then specimens within family, then give E1 and E5 equal weight. Define I=1-MAE(P2)/MAE(D2). Report MAE in response units, RMSE, reconstructed absolute-state error, family effects, specimen effects, and the E1/E5 sign count. Capacity is also scored on the resistance-complete rows; endpoints are never pooled into one unscaled loss.

Use 10,000 paired hierarchical bootstrap replicates: resample specimens within each fixed family and retain complete scored trajectories. This interval describes these 17 specimens/two families, not a family superpopulation. Training-only group-conformal 90% intervals are descriptive; report coverage and width per endpoint/family.

Required controls:

1. **Capacity-span ablation:** P2 must beat D2 when both include charge span, discharge span, ratio, and measured C(t). Otherwise the result is charge return/capacity, not morphology.
2. **Static identity:** compare P2 with S0 plus the same scalar acquisition variables.
3. **Within-specimen time permutation:** permute delta-C and A among eligible times inside each specimen, separately in training and held data, for 1000 seeds; refit.
4. **Static pair permutation:** permute RPT0 charge curves among same-family/same-temperature training specimens; a gain that persists only with identity pairing is narrowed to static identity.
5. **Direction swap:** exchange the charge/discharge blocks and recompute separation with its algebraic sign reversed. Because P2 uses symmetric block component grids and ridge penalties, refitted predictions should be invariant within numerical tolerance; failure indicates a sign, coordinate, or implementation error.
6. **Lag control:** replace current paired evolution with t-2 paired evolution; equal performance narrows the information to persistent history.
7. **Target-trajectory shuffle:** shuffle complete response trajectories among training specimens within family/temperature. Any retained gain invalidates computation.
8. **Acquisition residualization:** remove versus retain current, temperature, span, and phase-gap adjustment; sign reversal is inconclusive.
9. **Support sensitivity:** common-voltage interval and s=0.10-0.90 representations must retain the gain sign.
10. **Resistance robustness:** repeat with `0.1s Resistance`, `R_80to48_SOC`, and `R_100SOC`; report median absolute error, Huber fit, and leave-one-specimen-out influence. Retain the known E5|A excursion in primary analysis.

Protocol/family classifiers from RPT0, discharge evolution, and paired evolution under LOSO are diagnostics only. Predictability shows encoding, not confounding proof or mechanism.

## Frozen supportive, adverse, inconclusive, and invalid outcomes

Support H-C or H-R only if all hold for that endpoint:

1. P2 improves on D2 by at least 10%, with 95% specimen-within-family bootstrap interval above zero;
2. both E1 and E5 within-family effects are positive and neither worsens by more than 5%;
3. P2 improves on S0 overall and in both families;
4. P1-D1 has the same sign;
5. time permutation and target shuffle remove the advantage;
6. capacity-span, acquisition, common-voltage, interior-support, and lag controls do not reverse the sign;
7. no single specimen removes the sign; for resistance, at least two alternative supplied definitions agree.

The joint paired-diagnostic hypothesis requires both endpoints. Support means only that same-RPT paired finite-rate paths add two-RPT forecast information under represented E1/E5 schedules.

Adverse at the planned effect size: the upper 95% bound below 0.10 rejects a 10% paired benefit. An upper bound at or below zero supports no detectable benefit or harm. If D2 matches P2 after span/acquisition controls, conclude paired morphology adds no detectable information beyond discharge. If S0 matches P2, narrow the apparent value to static identity/protocol.

Inconclusive: interval crosses zero or 0.10; E1/E5 effects conflict; P1 and P2 conflict; gain depends on one specimen/resistance definition; common-voltage or acquisition adjustment reverses it; lag performs equally; calibration fails; or a negative control retains gain. Reciprocal-family success alone is inconclusive for transport because dose is non-overlapping; reciprocal-family failure does not refute within-family information.

Invalid: hash/schema/join/chronology failure, phase sign or coordinate error, use of t+1/t+2 information, target imputation, row-random splits, training on held specimens, post-index dose presented as known at t, or gain surviving target shuffle.

## Claims, verifier boundary, and stronger evidence

A verifier can recompute hashes/members/columns, phase signs, charge coordinates, phase gaps/spans, exact joins, chronological cutoffs, complete specimen separation, nested transformations, predictions, weighting, bootstrap, controls, and rule-to-conclusion mapping. It must accept correct adverse and inconclusive interpretations and reject mechanism claims from positive metrics.

It cannot establish that voltage hysteresis/asymmetry has a unique microscopic cause, that family labels denote mechanisms, that E1/E5 are independent cohorts, that the hidden future protocol was known, or that performance transfers to another chemistry/protocol. Those require expert electrochemical review, phase-specific thermodynamic/kinetic measurements, controlled future-dose interventions, and an independent paired-curve cohort.

Required outputs: `source_audit.json`, `eligible_rows.parquet`, `folds.csv`, `features_schema.json`, `curve_cache.parquet`, `predictions.parquet`, `metrics.json`, `bootstrap.parquet`, `calibration.json`, `controls.json`, `family_classifier.json`, `model_artifacts/`, `environment.json`, and `report.md`. Every numerical claim and verdict in the report must cite a computed output field.

## Literature boundary and alternatives record

Li et al. (2025), DOI `10.1038/s41467-025-57968-3`, is retained only as motivation that capacity/resistance agreement need not establish unique internal degradation modes. In the parent episode, only abstract/opening material was accessible; complete paper and supplement were not claimed read. Crossref search source `31a7f2b48ec4ca7cf82e54a68b7a1a7b70d54665ee700bcebaac8b2ddea1b0cc` identified discharge-curve forecasting literature, including Xiong et al. (2023), DOI `10.1016/j.est.2023.106790`, by bibliographic metadata only. It does not establish paired-path incremental value.

Alternatives not selected: discharge-only D2 is the essential comparator, not a discarded branch. Higher-capacity neural paired models are deferred for specimen scarcity. Mechanistic fitting is deferred for missing adjudicating measurements. Five-family discharge analysis remains the stronger general-population study; this child answers the narrower operational question of whether acquiring the second direction has incremental value.

# Proposal: Which reduced KIT_EIS package preserves prospective information under a nested full-information benchmark?

## Scientific decision and substantive advance

The configured KIT_EIS snapshot contains 1,022,975 rows, 35,275 spectrum keys, and 228 filename-defined specimens, exactly three under each of 76 opaque condition codes. It records repeated source-labelled room (`is_rt=1`) and operating (`is_rt=0`) EIS at five nominal SOCs, with timestamps, measured temperature, estimated OCV, validity, raw amplitude/phase, corrected complex impedance, and a source-defined reference-impedance index.

The frozen prospective cohort has 2,071 transitions from 167 specimens and 57 conditions. No package forecast has been fitted.

The unresolved hypothesis is unchanged: on that same historical complete-pair population, at least one fixed operating-state impedance package retains practically useful prospective information for next-check-up room-EIS-index change and is no more than 5% worse in condition-balanced RMSE than the best usable predictor allowed the complete five-SOC, 29-frequency operating acquisition.

The substantive advance is an inferential repair. In the parent, reduced packages enter as exact direct coordinates, while the full acquisition is compressed through splines and an SVD of rank at most 32. The fitted full model therefore does not contain the reduced models, so sparse noninferiority could be caused by representation loss. This child makes the primary full-information model-selection library contain every reduced model exactly and requires uncertainty bounds—not only point estimates—to clear the stated 10%, 5%, and 5% practical margins.

A supportive result establishes only retrospective recorded-information sufficiency and motivates a prospective independently acquired sparse-package trial. It does not establish physical sparse-scan equivalence, time savings, hardware equivalence, causal temperature response, capacity prognosis, or mechanism.

## Frozen population, chronology and endpoint

The following is frozen exactly from the parent.

1. Within specimen, order spectrum keys by `timestamp_s`; start a visit after an adjacent gap greater than 48 h. Report 24 h and 72 h sensitivities and maximum chain-grouped duration.
2. For duplicate `(specimen,visit,is_rt,soc_nom)`, select among `valid=1` by `timestamp_origin=1`, then greatest finite corrected-pair count on the 18-frequency eligibility grid, then earliest `timestamp_s,sd_block_id`; never select by temperature proximity.

4. A transition at visit t requires immediately previous raw visit t-1 room-complete, current t room-and-operating-complete, and immediately next raw visit t+1 room-complete, without skipping; current-to-next room-anchor interval is 18–24 days and `|median_SOC(T_op-T_rt)|>=8 °C`.

6. Fit future level `F_t=I_(t+1)`. For scoring only, `Yhat_t=21*(Fhat_t-I_t)/h_t` and `Y_t=21*(I_(t+1)-I_t)/h_t`, where `h_t=(A_(t+1)-A_t)/86400`. Future interval and completeness are never predictors or tuning features.
7. Assert every feature timestamp is at or before cutoff and every endpoint component is later.

The primary population remains exactly 2,071 transitions, 167 specimens and 57 conditions, approximately 573/697/801 transitions in the 0/10/40 °C strata. Every primary model uses these same units. Inference is conditional on complete current and future check-ups; exclusions and package-availability populations are descriptive only.

The finite-study estimand is equal-condition, then equal-specimen, then equal-transition out-of-condition cross-fitted prediction loss over these 57 designed conditions. It is not a random-condition superpopulation effect, cell-transfer estimate within a known condition, or independent-transition effect.

## Information boundaries and package ladder

No predictive path may use condition, specimen, hardware identity, absolute timestamp, future interval, or `eis_duration_s`. The duration field describes the historical full sweep and is allowed only in burden tables and outcome-free stratification. No omitted package coordinate, full-package imputation, future completeness flag, or outcome-derived frequency selection may enter a reduced model.

All real/imaginary coordinates are reconstructed as `z_amp_mOhm*(cos(z_ph_deg),sin(z_ph_deg))`. - `S50/90-3`: M50/90 plus the same exact coordinates at SOC50 and SOC90.
- `I5-4`: M5 plus the 20 exact operating raw amplitudes and masks at 10, 2.0833, 0.5 and 0.2083 Hz across five SOCs; phase is excluded to preserve the repeated-index-assay interpretation.
- Complete acquisition: all M5 fields plus all five-SOC, 29-frequency operating raw amplitude/phase measurements, represented by 290 signed-complex coordinates and 145 masks. The 20 exact raw amplitudes from `I5-4` are retained explicitly because a linear real/imaginary model does not contain their nonlinear amplitude transform.

The 1/50/1000-Hz panel remains fixed without endpoint outcomes. It spans three decades, excludes all four endpoint constituents, and had 99.878%/99.830%/99.702% corrected-complex finiteness in the inherited archive audit. The 84.7%/88.5% omitted-spectrum reconstruction results support redundancy only, not forecast value, optimality, mechanism or physical minimality. The adjacent 3.125/67.5676/1470.5883-Hz panel and leave-one-frequency-out fits remain prespecified fragility sensitivities.

## Primary nested model and substantive alternative

The primary estimator is weighted block ridge on direct coordinates. Penalties are selected from `10^-4,...,10^4`, with an explicit `infinity` option that drops each added block. Inner condition-held-out validation selects penalties, with ties within 1% choosing fewer blocks and stronger penalties.

For the complete acquisition, define an inner-selected library `U-full` containing:

1. every exact reduced model `S90-3`, `S50/90-3` and `I5-4`;
2. each reduced model augmented by the additional M5 metadata and all remaining direct full-acquisition coordinates/masks as separately penalized blocks; and
3. the omnibus direct full model.

Selection occurs only in inner training. Because every reduced algorithm and its penalty grid appears unchanged in this library, the full-information algorithm can ignore extra coordinates and cannot be structurally handicapped by spline/SVD compression. OOF degradation can still occur through finite-sample model selection and is reported rather than overwritten. `U-full` is the sole primary noninferiority reference.

Two specificity-matched alternatives are retained. First, repeat the nested library with the parent's masked spline/SVD remainder, but preserve each exact reduced block before compression. Second, fit shallow histogram gradient boosting to the same direct feature sets and grouped folds, with learning rate `{0.03,0.06}`, max leaves `{7,15}`, minimum leaf size `{40,80}`, L2 `{1,10}`, and at most 500 iterations with training-only early stopping. These alternatives test whether smooth spectral structure or nonlinear state interactions reveal full-only information that additive direct ridge loses. A decision supported only by one representation/model family is inconclusive.

Neural sequences remain deferred because there are only 57 independent conditions and no within-sweep timing. DRT/equivalent-circuit claims remain deferred because operating-condition meanings, equilibration/current logs and an independent endpoint are absent; fitted components could not uniquely adjudicate mechanism.

## Held-condition evaluation and uncertainty

Use the parent's deterministic, temperature-stratified five-fold condition assignment and four additional prespecified hash salts. All transitions and specimens from a condition stay together in outer and inner folds. Unit weight is `1/(C*m_c*n_ci)` for C conditions, `m_c` specimens in condition c, and `n_ci` transitions in specimen i. Pool each salt's OOF predictions once and report condition-balanced RMSE/MAE, calibration, per-condition/specimen losses, temperature stratum, age, lead and first-transition cold start.

For package p define:

- `G_imp,p = 1 - RMSE_p/RMSE_Mp`;
- `P_p = RMSE_p/RMSE_U-full - 1`.

- **Metadata without operating impedance:** a shadow improves over B-room-direct, while the matched package's adjusted upper bound for `G_imp,p` is below 5%. Attribute value only to recorded state/timing metadata.
- **Repeated-assay localization:** I5-4 passes but both non-index packages fail. Conclude persistence of the source-index assay across state/SOC, not independent degradation diagnosis.
- **No useful operating package:** adjusted upper bounds for `G_total,U` and every package total gain are below 5%, or all point estimates are adverse with valid controls. Conclude no useful increment beyond current complete room information at this horizon.

## Scientific question, importance, and evidence boundary

The unresolved decision is which standardized second EIS acquisition is more informative after a diagnostic program already supplies ten past measured discharge capacities and a rested, fully charged state-V spectrum: state I before charge, state IX after discharge and rest, or both. The associated scientific question is whether charge-side and discharge-side impedance responses carry distinct, cell-transferable information about the next 10 and 20 measured-capacity losses, rather than stable cell/contact offsets or protocol-age and elapsed-time proxies.

This matters because I and IX impose different acquisition timing. State I is available before charge and can support a prediction when V finishes; IX requires completing the intervening discharge/rest sequence. If one response is sufficient, the other spectrum may be avoidable. If both add conditional value, the result would establish an empirical asymmetry across standardized electrochemical states that a single rested-full spectrum loses. It would not identify a microscopic degradation mechanism.

Relevant passages of Zhang et al. (2020), DOI 10.1038/s41467-020-15235-7, were inspected through a focused public-page extraction; the frozen full-text source is PMCID PMC7136228, source ID 33086e0650f9774d98a2853f7973f0a88c4e8c045703abb09e08fa21aadabf79, SHA-256 ef60f78e673d5bc5c93aecf68520f4b018343f2d4465b56acb0ca6be71ac0144.
