## Variables and matched model ladder

At each canonical frequency j define:
dI_Re[j] = V_Re[j] - I_Re[j], dI_nIm[j] = V_nIm[j] - I_nIm[j];
dIX_Re[j] = IX_Re[j] - V_Re[j], dIX_nIm[j] = IX_nIm[j] - V_nIm[j].
These directional responses span charge/rest and discharge/rest respectively. They are not pure SOC effects or mechanism measurements. Do not form ratios because imaginary components may cross zero.

**P, simple baseline.** OLS on Q[c-10:c-1], predicting -H times the ten-cycle slope without clipping.

**B, strong history baseline.** Inputs: c, log(1+c), fixed temperature numeric and one-hot family, Q0, Q[c-1], Q[c-1]/Q0, ten Q/Q0 history values, nine first differences, five- and ten-cycle slopes, slope difference, ten-cycle quadratic coefficient, residual SD, P, and predeclared temperature interactions with age, level, and slopes. Fit cubic age splines with df in {3,5,7} and ridge alpha in {0.01,0.1,1,10,100}.

**Primary full-spectrum linear acquisition ladder.** Standardize on outer-training cells only and fit ridge with the same alpha grid:

- V: B plus all 120 state-V components.
- VI: V plus all 120 dI components.
- VX: V plus all 120 dIX components.
- VIX: V plus both 120-component response blocks.

These are feature-nested acquisition sets under one estimator and answer H-I, H-IX, selection, and H-both. Also fit direct-coordinate I/V, V/IX, and I/V/IX joint models. They contain the same raw information but expose different ridge geometry; disagreement with difference-coordinate models is representation sensitivity, not replication. Fit B+I and B+IX snapshots to test whether a second state is merely a better absolute snapshot than V.

**Sparse companion.** Repeat the complete V/VI/VX/VIX ladder using Re and stored -Im at exactly 17.79613 and 2.16054 Hz for each relevant block. This tests whether a predeclared four-value response panel retains the acquisition ranking. It cannot claim shorter acquisition time because the archive contains complete sweeps, not a timed sparse protocol.

**Scientifically substantive learned alternative.** For every 120-component V, dI, and dIX block, standardize and fit PCA separately within each training fold, taking the smallest dimension that reaches 99% variance capped at a tuned {10,20}. Concatenate the relevant scores with B, then fit an RBF Nystroem map plus ridge. ## Timing, stable-offset, and protocol-proxy controls

Run every control on the same origins, outer folds, and aggregation.

**Timing-only nuisance set T.** From prediction-time timestamps derive elapsed time from that cell's first archived time to I_start and IX_end, I/V/IX sweep durations, I_end-to-V_start, V_end-to-IX_start, and I_start-to-IX_end. Fit V+T, VI+T, VX+T, and VIX+T. Primary spectral support requires the unadjusted direction to persist and each claimed state model to improve over its matched timing-adjusted predecessor with a lower confidence bound above zero. If T alone matches a state gain or adjustment removes it, report elapsed-time/protocol-associated information, not unique EIS information. T is available by IX but may reflect unrecorded charge/discharge/rest behavior; it is not a randomized protocol variable.

**Stable offset controls.**

1. Replace current dI(c) and/or dIX(c) by each cell's cycle-1 response while retaining current V. Comparable performance is compatible with stable cell, fixture, contact, or instrument calibration.
2. Use centered responses dI(c)-dI(1) and dIX(c)-dIX(1), singly and jointly. Claimed evolving-state information must remain directionally positive.
3. Replace all current states by I(1), V(1), IX(1). If this stale triple matches VIX, narrow the result to stable specimen calibration.
4. Remove a per-spectrum complex translation by subtracting the highest-frequency Re and -Im values from every frequency; separately fit highest-frequency-only controls. Loss confined to the offset component is compatible with series/contact offset, not proof of it.
5. Compare common-mode blocks (I+V)/2 and (IX+V)/2 with dI and dIX. Gain confined to common mode does not support directional response.
6. On common-support windows, permute entire dI and dIX cell trajectories independently among cells within temperature family, preserving cycle alignment; also permute them jointly to preserve their mutual correlation. Use 1,000 fixed-seed permutations. Never permute origins individually.
7. Use lagged dI(c-1) and dIX(c-1) controls. If lagged and current responses are indistinguishable, narrow the claim to slowly varying age-associated information.
8. Fit training-cell family-by-age trends for each response feature and repeat with training-derived residual response blocks. This asks whether signal exceeds protocol age and family without using held-cell outcomes.
9. Hash complete spectra and reject any train/test fold containing an exact cross-specimen duplicate.
10. Repeat outcomes with ox/red=1, normalized L/Q0, common-support windows, and both disputed identity mappings.

These controls distinguish compatible information sources; none establishes causality. In particular, IX follows a diagnostic discharge, so its spectrum and its V-to-IX elapsed interval can encode a protocol response closely related to capacity. A useful IX predictor does not by itself establish electrochemical-state information distinct from that proxy.

## Splits, estimation, and uncertainty

Primary transfer evaluation is ten outer leave-one-confirmatory-cell-out folds. Every origin and spectrum from one physical-cell key remains together. The held cell supplies only Q through c-1, its current I/V/IX spectra, prediction-time timestamps, c, and fixed temperature; it supplies no labels, preprocessing, PCA, landmarks, tuning, calibration, or feature selection. Inner leave-one-training-cell-out selection minimizes the same family-balanced cell MAE. Random row, cycle, origin, or spectrum splits are prohibited.

Stress tests are:

- leave-one-temperature-family-out, labeled severe within-study protocol shift, not external validation;
- age-forward at tau={50,100,150}, fitting only training-cell origins with c+H-1<=tau and predicting held-cell c=tau+1…tau+20 without updates;
- the mandatory common-support windows;
- clock-resolved and literal 12-cell identity sensitivities, reported separately and never pooled.

For each model, cell, family, and horizon report MAE in mAh, RMSE, signed bias, R² when defined, MAE/Q0, and errors by early/middle/late within-cell age thirds. Primary aggregation is equal-origin-within-cell, equal-cell-within-family, equal-family. Equal-cell and cycle-weighted summaries are secondary.

Construct nominal 90% prediction intervals only from inner held-cell residuals. Reduce each calibration cell to its 90th-percentile absolute residual and use finite-sample rank ceil[0.90(m+1)], clipped at m, as a symmetric radius. Report family-balanced coverage, width, and interval score; no conditional or family-shift guarantee is claimed.

Generate 10,000 fixed-seed paired bootstraps by resampling cells within temperature family, never origins. Recompute all ΔI, ΔIX, S, NI|IX, and NIX|I contrasts jointly. Report percentile intervals. For the 95% simultaneous max-deviation band over the ten primary horizon-by-contrast estimands, compute in each bootstrap the maximum absolute deviation from the original ten-component estimate vector; use its 95th percentile q and report each estimate ±q. Also report all ten paired cell effects and exact 2^10 sign-flip sensitivities. With only two cells in each high-temperature family, uncertainty is coarse and bootstrap assumptions are limited.

## Decision and falsification rules

Support H-I or H-IX only when, at both horizons:

- point Δ is at least 10%;
- its simultaneous lower bound exceeds zero;
- improvement is positive in at least two temperature families and no family is worse than 10%;
- common-support improvement is positive;
- the state model also beats B (and P if B loses to P);
- nominal 90% coverage is 0.80–1.00; and
- timing-adjusted, centered-response, stale, offset-removal, and representation checks do not reverse the claimed direction.

The conjunctive 10% claim for a state is falsified if either horizon's simultaneous upper bound is below 10%. It is adverse to acquiring that state if both horizons' upper bounds are at or below zero and common-support does not reverse. Otherwise it is inconclusive.

Declare I or IX the preferred second state only under the selection rule above. If both states pass H-I/H-IX but neither has ≥5% uncertainty-resolved superiority at both horizons, conclude both are useful but preference is unresolved. If neither passes, do not select one by its point estimate.

Support H-both only if both NI|IX and NIX|I have point improvements ≥5% at both horizons, simultaneous lower bounds above zero, positive common-support effects, no family worse by >10%, adequate interval coverage, and both centered/timing-adjusted conditional increments remain positive. H-both is falsified if any one of its four horizon-by-conditional upper bounds is below 5%. It is adverse to acquiring both if VIX fails to improve over either single-state model at both horizons with upper bounds at or below zero. Other outcomes are inconclusive.

A sparse success with full failure is a fragile frequency-specific association; a full success with sparse failure means the two-bin panel is insufficient. A nonlinear-only success is model-dependent. A current-response gain matched by stale responses narrows to stable calibration. A gain absorbed by T narrows to elapsed-time/protocol association. A full-risk gain reversed on common support narrows to age/follow-up composition. Identity-map disagreement is inconclusive for 25C02/25C03.

A supportive result establishes only held-cell predictive information in ten unambiguously linked LCO/graphite coin cells under these fixed protocols. An adverse result means this study did not demonstrate the specified practical increment; it does not show multi-state EIS is universally useless. No branch may claim causality, LLI/LAM, SEI growth, lithium plating, charge-transfer resistance, active-material loss, safety, changed-use robustness, chemistry/form-factor transfer, or field economics.

## Computation, outputs, and verification boundaries

Use the configured Python 3.11 stack: numpy 1.26.4, pandas 2.2.3, scipy 1.14.1, scikit-learn 1.5.2, joblib 1.4.2. Budget 16 CPUs, 64 GiB RAM, zero GPUs, and 4–6 hours, within the 16-CPU/262,144-MiB/28,800-s solver envelope. Parallelize outer folds and cap BLAS threads. The new triple audit used 2 CPUs/4 GiB and completed in seconds; full model timing remains planned, not measured. GPU use offers no clear advantage for this table-scale experiment.

Required outputs:

- immutable source/catalog/software/seed manifest and exact member/table map;
- parser tests, row-layout/current-sign audit, canonical frequency array/hash, duplicate report, and exclusion/censoring ledger;
- I/V/IX triple table with source rows, token, cycle, sweep starts/ends, completeness, and order assertions;
- capacity-cycle table and explicit confirmatory/cross-map/literal identity maps;
- frozen H10/H20 analytic tables with every feature cutoff and target index;
- fold, transform, PCA, kernel, tuning, interval-calibration, and seed manifests;
- outer predictions and intervals for P, B, every full/sparse/learned V/VI/VX/VIX model, direct-coordinate snapshots/joints, and every timing/stale/centered/offset/common-mode/lag/permutation control;
- per-origin, cell, family, horizon, aggregate, bootstrap, simultaneous-band, and sign-flip outputs;
- age-forward, family-holdout, common-support, polarity, normalization, and identity sensitivities;
- plots retaining unfavorable cells and horizons;
- executable code/tests and reusable checkpoints; and
- `conclusion.json` mapping every support/falsification clause to exact computed fields and selecting only an allowed supportive, adverse, or inconclusive statement.

Readiness must verify hashes, all 48 bound members, table IDs, layouts, units/sign, integer cycles, 60-bin completeness, exact sparse frequencies, triple joins/order, capacity handoffs, identity exclusions, exact risk/common-support counts, imports, split isolation, and a two-cell end-to-end smoke fit. Readiness does not answer the hypotheses.

An automatic verifier can recompute parsing, hashes, joins, timing, identity-map application, risk sets, predictors, training cutoffs, folds, predictions, uncertainty, controls, thresholds, and whether `conclusion.json` follows the numbers. It must accept correctly computed supportive, adverse, and inconclusive outcomes and reject correct computations paired with unsupported causal, mechanistic, external-validation, independent-origin, or prospective-field conclusions.

Battery-expert or data-owner adjudication is required for the physical identity of 25C02/25C03, semantics of headerless 35/45 °C columns, whether timestamps adequately capture charge/discharge/rest protocol variation, physical interpretation of stable versus evolving spectral offsets, practical adequacy of 10%/5% margins, acquisition latency and cost, and informative stopping. Microscopic mechanisms, deployment safety/economics, other chemistries, changed-use transfer, and external validity require additional measurements, controlled interventions, independent cells, or another study.

## Selection and deferral record

The simple P/B and full V ridge baselines quantify persistence, capacity history, and the already-acquired rested-full spectrum. The full linear V/VI/VX/VIX ladder is selected as primary because it gives symmetric, explicit nested estimands with all observed frequencies and restrained complexity. Sparse models test a lower-information panel; the matched nonlinear ladder tests scientifically relevant nonlinear interaction that ridge loses. Direct-coordinate models test representation sensitivity.

Neural encoders and equivalent-circuit models are deferred, not prohibited. Revisit neural models only with substantially more independent specimens or reproducible held-cell residual structure. Revisit circuits only with a predeclared identifiable topology and physical validation. States II–IV and VI–VIII are deferred because they would expand the acquisition decision beyond the assigned I-versus-IX question. A new population, prediction boundary, estimand, outcome, analysis family, or falsification rule requires Lead approval as a scientific child, not compiler repair.

# Zhang2020 three-state acquisition experiment: pre-charge I, post-discharge IX, or both beyond rested-full V?

## Scientific question, importance, and evidence boundary

The unresolved decision is which standardized second EIS acquisition is more informative after a diagnostic program already supplies ten past measured discharge capacities and a rested, fully charged state-V spectrum: state I before charge, state IX after discharge and rest, or both. The associated scientific question is whether charge-side and discharge-side impedance responses carry distinct, cell-transferable information about the next 10 and 20 measured-capacity losses, rather than stable cell/contact offsets or protocol-age and elapsed-time proxies.

This matters because I and IX impose different acquisition timing. State I is available before charge and can support a prediction when V finishes; IX requires completing the intervening discharge/rest sequence. If one response is sufficient, the other spectrum may be avoidable. If both add conditional value, the result would establish an empirical asymmetry across standardized electrochemical states that a single rested-full spectrum loses. It would not identify a microscopic degradation mechanism.

Relevant passages of Zhang et al. (2020), DOI 10.1038/s41467-020-15235-7, were inspected through a focused public-page extraction; the frozen full-text source is PMCID PMC7136228, source ID 33086e0650f9774d98a2853f7973f0a88c4e8c045703abb09e08fa21aadabf79, SHA-256 ef60f78e673d5bc5c93aecf68520f4b018343f2d4465b56acb0ca6be71ac0144. The public extraction has frozen provenance source 0219300998276e5b4c41a9d59aa5c84e34084ace0a330c7e6b0e0c6a0c7cfd8c and supports that 12 commercial 45 mAh Eunicell LR2032 LCO/graphite coin cells generated more than 20,000 spectra at nine protocol states; V and IX are rested, electrochemically stable full-charge and full-discharge states; and EIS was used for capacity and remaining-life prediction with cell-held-out evaluation. A focused extraction from the acquired supplement (source ID 5db2e3100f5dcdae2ae19e33ff9c2c7d6c4f848df96afe8c206604f17fefe10a; SHA-256 e6b678e13ed22b5014cbdb8d92b448360d93030b3e4342d8d30603343afb358e) supports the I-before-charge, V-after-charge-plus-15-minute-rest sequence. The complete supplement was not successfully text-extracted, so no unobserved supplementary details are claimed.

**Strongest claim supported before modeling:** the configured archives contain 2,786 complete same-cell, same-cycle I/V/IX triples on one 60-frequency grid; every triple is ordered I before V before IX; on ten unambiguously linked cells every eligible IX sweep ends before capacity cycle c begins; and those cells provide 2,054 H10 and 1,974 H20 prospective origins. Existing evidence supports EIS association with capacity and the feasibility of the comparison, not the result.

**Unresolved claim:** conditional on future-safe capacity history and current V, current I and IX responses may differ in transferable prognostic information, and both may be nonredundant. The inspected article does not report the required common-risk-set ablation B+V versus B+V+I versus B+V+IX versus B+V+I+IX.

**Substantive advance:** this experiment changes the evidence from separate “does I help?” and “does IX help?” analyses into one paired acquisition-choice study. It holds specimens, origins, target, split, model class, tuning, uncertainty, and the latest prediction boundary fixed; directly estimates I-versus-IX superiority and both conditional increments; and uses controls aimed at the principal rival explanations. This is an adaptation, not a reproduction.

## Frozen hypotheses and deliverable

For horizon h in {10,20}, let E_h(M) be outer-test MAE aggregated by averaging origins within cell, cells within temperature family, then the three temperature families equally. Define the full-spectrum models below as V, VI, VX, and VIX and:

- ΔI_h = [E_h(V)-E_h(VI)]/E_h(V): incremental value of state I.
- ΔIX_h = [E_h(V)-E_h(VX)]/E_h(V): incremental value of state IX.
- S_h = [E_h(VI)-E_h(VX)]/E_h(V): positive values favor IX over I and negative values favor I, measured against their common V baseline.
- NI|IX_h = [E_h(VX)-E_h(VIX)]/E_h(VX): value of adding I when IX is present.
- NIX|I_h = [E_h(VI)-E_h(VIX)]/E_h(VI): value of adding IX when I is present.

The primary practical hypotheses are:

1. **H-I:** ΔI_h is at least 10% at both horizons.
2. **H-IX:** ΔIX_h is at least 10% at both horizons.
3. **H-both:** both NI|IX_h and NIX|I_h are at least 5% at both horizons. This deliberately requires each endpoint to add value conditional on the other; merely beating the weaker single-state model is not nonredundancy.
4. **Selection:** recommend IX over I only if H-IX is supported and S_h is at least +5% at both horizons with the simultaneous lower bound above zero. Recommend I only if H-I is supported and S_h is at most -5% at both horizons with the simultaneous upper bound below zero. Otherwise report no resolved winner. A tie is a result, not a failure.

All claims must also survive the timing-adjusted and stable-offset gates below. Thresholds are engineering relevance margins, not facts supplied by the paper.

The required scientific deliverable is newly fitted outer predictions for all four matched acquisitions at both horizons, all conditional and pairwise estimands with specimen-level uncertainty, sparse and nonlinear alternatives, chronology/timing/stable-offset controls, and one mechanically determined supportive, adverse, or inconclusive interpretation. No positive result is required.

## Common risk set, prediction time, and target

Pair all three states only by exact EIS token and integer cycle c. A state spectrum is complete only with exactly 60 finite rows, 60 unique canonical frequencies, and one Re/-Im pair per frequency. Never pair by row order, nearest timestamp, or capacity filename.

Every model issues its prediction at the end of IX(c), the latest candidate acquisition. This is the only temporally fair head-to-head comparison: I, V, and IX are then all available, and no model receives a shorter target horizon. VI models simply wait and use no post-V information. Report separately that an I+V deployment could act earlier; this experiment estimates information value at a common boundary, not latency-adjusted utility.

For each included token reproduce:
capacity(c-1) discharge end < I(c) start < V(c) end < IX(c) end < capacity(c) charge start < capacity(c) discharge end.
If this fails, exclude that specimen and report the failure; do not change the target.

Let Q[i,k] be primary measured discharge capacity. For H in {10,20}:
L[i,c,H] = Q[i,c-1] - Q[i,c+H-1].
Only Q[i,c-10] through Q[i,c-1] is available. The target spans future measured discharges c through c+H-1. Keep negative losses caused by recovery/noise. Eligibility requires ten consecutive positive finite past Q values, a complete ordered I/V/IX triple at c, both exact sparse bins, and positive finite Q[c+H-1]. Build separate H10/H20 tables, but all models within a horizon use exactly the same rows.

End-of-record absence is right censoring and may be informative; never impute zero or extrapolate. Family totals are 875/835 origins at 25 °C, 607/587 at 35 °C, and 572/552 at 45 °C for H10/H20. Mandatory common-support windows are c=10–25 for H10 (16 origins per cell, 160 total) and c=10–15 for H20 (6 per cell, 60 total). Report included/excluded origins and baseline distributions for observed versus censored tail anchors.

## Variables and matched model ladder

At each canonical frequency j define:
dI_Re[j] = V_Re[j] - I_Re[j], dI_nIm[j] = V_nIm[j] - I_nIm[j];
dIX_Re[j] = IX_Re[j] - V_Re[j], dIX_nIm[j] = IX_nIm[j] - V_nIm[j].
These directional responses span charge/rest and discharge/rest respectively. They are not pure SOC effects or mechanism measurements. Do not form ratios because imaginary components may cross zero.

**P, simple baseline.** OLS on Q[c-10:c-1], predicting -H times the ten-cycle slope without clipping.

**B, strong history baseline.** Inputs: c, log(1+c), fixed temperature numeric and one-hot family, Q0, Q[c-1], Q[c-1]/Q0, ten Q/Q0 history values, nine first differences, five- and ten-cycle slopes, slope difference, ten-cycle quadratic coefficient, residual SD, P, and predeclared temperature interactions with age, level, and slopes. Fit cubic age splines with df in {3,5,7} and ridge alpha in {0.01,0.1,1,10,100}.

**Primary full-spectrum linear acquisition ladder.** Standardize on outer-training cells only and fit ridge with the same alpha grid:

- V: B plus all 120 state-V components.
- VI: V plus all 120 dI components.
- VX: V plus all 120 dIX components.
- VIX: V plus both 120-component response blocks.

These are feature-nested acquisition sets under one estimator and answer H-I, H-IX, selection, and H-both. Also fit direct-coordinate I/V, V/IX, and I/V/IX joint models. They contain the same raw information but expose different ridge geometry; disagreement with difference-coordinate models is representation sensitivity, not replication. Fit B+I and B+IX snapshots to test whether a second state is merely a better absolute snapshot than V.

**Sparse companion.** Repeat the complete V/VI/VX/VIX ladder using Re and stored -Im at exactly 17.79613 and 2.16054 Hz for each relevant block. This tests whether a predeclared four-value response panel retains the acquisition ranking. It cannot claim shorter acquisition time because the archive contains complete sweeps, not a timed sparse protocol.

**Scientifically substantive learned alternative.** For every 120-component V, dI, and dIX block, standardize and fit PCA separately within each training fold, taking the smallest dimension that reaches 99% variance capped at a tuned {10,20}. Concatenate the relevant scores with B, then fit an RBF Nystroem map plus ridge. Tune gamma in {0.5,1,2} times inverse median squared training distance, landmarks in {128,256} capped by training rows, and alpha in {0.01,0.1,1,10,100}; seed 20260923. Apply this identical ladder to V, VI, VX, and VIX. It can reveal nonlinear interaction between charge-side and discharge-side responses that additive linear ridge loses. A nonlinear-only finding is model-dependent and cannot rescue the primary linear hypotheses.

All transformations, spline bases, PCA, distances, landmarks, hyperparameters, and interval calibration are training-only. Fit horizons separately. The full linear ladder is primary because it preserves all measured frequencies with limited capacity relative to ten independent specimens. Neural encoders are deferred because 2,054 repeated origins do not replace ten independent cells and a high-capacity model could learn identity. Revisit with a materially larger independent cohort or repeatable held-cell residual structure. Equivalent circuits are deferred because no topology or parameter-identifiability criterion is established and fitted parameters would not be microscopic ground truth.

## Timing, stable-offset, and protocol-proxy controls

Run every control on the same origins, outer folds, and aggregation.

**Timing-only nuisance set T.** From prediction-time timestamps derive elapsed time from that cell's first archived time to I_start and IX_end, I/V/IX sweep durations, I_end-to-V_start, V_end-to-IX_start, and I_start-to-IX_end. Fit V+T, VI+T, VX+T, and VIX+T. Primary spectral support requires the unadjusted direction to persist and each claimed state model to improve over its matched timing-adjusted predecessor with a lower confidence bound above zero. If T alone matches a state gain or adjustment removes it, report elapsed-time/protocol-associated information, not unique EIS information. T is available by IX but may reflect unrecorded charge/discharge/rest behavior; it is not a randomized protocol variable.

**Stable offset controls.**

1. Replace current dI(c) and/or dIX(c) by each cell's cycle-1 response while retaining current V. Comparable performance is compatible with stable cell, fixture, contact, or instrument calibration.
2. Use centered responses dI(c)-dI(1) and dIX(c)-dIX(1), singly and jointly. Claimed evolving-state information must remain directionally positive.
3. Replace all current states by I(1), V(1), IX(1). If this stale triple matches VIX, narrow the result to stable specimen calibration.
4. Remove a per-spectrum complex translation by subtracting the highest-frequency Re and -Im values from every frequency; separately fit highest-frequency-only controls. Loss confined to the offset component is compatible with series/contact offset, not proof of it.
5. Compare common-mode blocks (I+V)/2 and (IX+V)/2 with dI and dIX. Gain confined to common mode does not support directional response.
6. On common-support windows, permute entire dI and dIX cell trajectories independently among cells within temperature family, preserving cycle alignment; also permute them jointly to preserve their mutual correlation. Use 1,000 fixed-seed permutations. Never permute origins individually.
7. Use lagged dI(c-1) and dIX(c-1) controls. If lagged and current responses are indistinguishable, narrow the claim to slowly varying age-associated information.
8. Fit training-cell family-by-age trends for each response feature and repeat with training-derived residual response blocks. This asks whether signal exceeds protocol age and family without using held-cell outcomes.
9. Hash complete spectra and reject any train/test fold containing an exact cross-specimen duplicate.
10. Repeat outcomes with ox/red=1, normalized L/Q0, common-support windows, and both disputed identity mappings.

These controls distinguish compatible information sources; none establishes causality. In particular, IX follows a diagnostic discharge, so its spectrum and its V-to-IX elapsed interval can encode a protocol response closely related to capacity. A useful IX predictor does not by itself establish electrochemical-state information distinct from that proxy.

## Splits, estimation, and uncertainty

Primary transfer evaluation is ten outer leave-one-confirmatory-cell-out folds. Every origin and spectrum from one physical-cell key remains together. The held cell supplies only Q through c-1, its current I/V/IX spectra, prediction-time timestamps, c, and fixed temperature; it supplies no labels, preprocessing, PCA, landmarks, tuning, calibration, or feature selection. Inner leave-one-training-cell-out selection minimizes the same family-balanced cell MAE. Random row, cycle, origin, or spectrum splits are prohibited.

Stress tests are:

- leave-one-temperature-family-out, labeled severe within-study protocol shift, not external validation;
- age-forward at tau={50,100,150}, fitting only training-cell origins with c+H-1<=tau and predicting held-cell c=tau+1…tau+20 without updates;
- the mandatory common-support windows;
- clock-resolved and literal 12-cell identity sensitivities, reported separately and never pooled.

For each model, cell, family, and horizon report MAE in mAh, RMSE, signed bias, R² when defined, MAE/Q0, and errors by early/middle/late within-cell age thirds. Primary aggregation is equal-origin-within-cell, equal-cell-within-family, equal-family. Equal-cell and cycle-weighted summaries are secondary.

Construct nominal 90% prediction intervals only from inner held-cell residuals. Reduce each calibration cell to its 90th-percentile absolute residual and use finite-sample rank ceil[0.90(m+1)], clipped at m, as a symmetric radius. Report family-balanced coverage, width, and interval score; no conditional or family-shift guarantee is claimed.

Generate 10,000 fixed-seed paired bootstraps by resampling cells within temperature family, never origins. Recompute all ΔI, ΔIX, S, NI|IX, and NIX|I contrasts jointly. Report percentile intervals. For the 95% simultaneous max-deviation band over the ten primary horizon-by-contrast estimands, compute in each bootstrap the maximum absolute deviation from the original ten-component estimate vector; use its 95th percentile q and report each estimate ±q. Also report all ten paired cell effects and exact 2^10 sign-flip sensitivities. With only two cells in each high-temperature family, uncertainty is coarse and bootstrap assumptions are limited.

## Decision and falsification rules

Support H-I or H-IX only when, at both horizons:

- point Δ is at least 10%;
- its simultaneous lower bound exceeds zero;
- improvement is positive in at least two temperature families and no family is worse than 10%;
- common-support improvement is positive;
- the state model also beats B (and P if B loses to P);
- nominal 90% coverage is 0.80–1.00; and
- timing-adjusted, centered-response, stale, offset-removal, and representation checks do not reverse the claimed direction.

The conjunctive 10% claim for a state is falsified if either horizon's simultaneous upper bound is below 10%. It is adverse to acquiring that state if both horizons' upper bounds are at or below zero and common-support does not reverse. Otherwise it is inconclusive.

Declare I or IX the preferred second state only under the selection rule above. If both states pass H-I/H-IX but neither has ≥5% uncertainty-resolved superiority at both horizons, conclude both are useful but preference is unresolved. If neither passes, do not select one by its point estimate.

Support H-both only if both NI|IX and NIX|I have point improvements ≥5% at both horizons, simultaneous lower bounds above zero, positive common-support effects, no family worse by >10%, adequate interval coverage, and both centered/timing-adjusted conditional increments remain positive. H-both is falsified if any one of its four horizon-by-conditional upper bounds is below 5%. It is adverse to acquiring both if VIX fails to improve over either single-state model at both horizons with upper bounds at or below zero. Other outcomes are inconclusive.

A sparse success with full failure is a fragile frequency-specific association; a full success with sparse failure means the two-bin panel is insufficient. A nonlinear-only success is model-dependent. A current-response gain matched by stale responses narrows to stable calibration. A gain absorbed by T narrows to elapsed-time/protocol association. A full-risk gain reversed on common support narrows to age/follow-up composition. Identity-map disagreement is inconclusive for 25C02/25C03.

A supportive result establishes only held-cell predictive information in ten unambiguously linked LCO/graphite coin cells under these fixed protocols. An adverse result means this study did not demonstrate the specified practical increment; it does not show multi-state EIS is universally useless. No branch may claim causality, LLI/LAM, SEI growth, lithium plating, charge-transfer resistance, active-material loss, safety, changed-use robustness, chemistry/form-factor transfer, or field economics.

## Computation, outputs, and verification boundaries

Use the configured Python 3.11 stack: numpy 1.26.4, pandas 2.2.3, scipy 1.14.1, scikit-learn 1.5.2, joblib 1.4.2. Budget 16 CPUs, 64 GiB RAM, zero GPUs, and 4–6 hours, within the 16-CPU/262,144-MiB/28,800-s solver envelope. Parallelize outer folds and cap BLAS threads. The new triple audit used 2 CPUs/4 GiB and completed in seconds; full model timing remains planned, not measured. GPU use offers no clear advantage for this table-scale experiment.

Required outputs:

- immutable source/catalog/software/seed manifest and exact member/table map;
- parser tests, row-layout/current-sign audit, canonical frequency array/hash, duplicate report, and exclusion/censoring ledger;
- I/V/IX triple table with source rows, token, cycle, sweep starts/ends, completeness, and order assertions;
- capacity-cycle table and explicit confirmatory/cross-map/literal identity maps;
- frozen H10/H20 analytic tables with every feature cutoff and target index;
- fold, transform, PCA, kernel, tuning, interval-calibration, and seed manifests;
- outer predictions and intervals for P, B, every full/sparse/learned V/VI/VX/VIX model, direct-coordinate snapshots/joints, and every timing/stale/centered/offset/common-mode/lag/permutation control;
- per-origin, cell, family, horizon, aggregate, bootstrap, simultaneous-band, and sign-flip outputs;
- age-forward, family-holdout, common-support, polarity, normalization, and identity sensitivities;
- plots retaining unfavorable cells and horizons;
- executable code/tests and reusable checkpoints; and
- `conclusion.json` mapping every support/falsification clause to exact computed fields and selecting only an allowed supportive, adverse, or inconclusive statement.

Readiness must verify hashes, all 48 bound members, table IDs, layouts, units/sign, integer cycles, 60-bin completeness, exact sparse frequencies, triple joins/order, capacity handoffs, identity exclusions, exact risk/common-support counts, imports, split isolation, and a two-cell end-to-end smoke fit. Readiness does not answer the hypotheses.

An automatic verifier can recompute parsing, hashes, joins, timing, identity-map application, risk sets, predictors, training cutoffs, folds, predictions, uncertainty, controls, thresholds, and whether `conclusion.json` follows the numbers. It must accept correctly computed supportive, adverse, and inconclusive outcomes and reject correct computations paired with unsupported causal, mechanistic, external-validation, independent-origin, or prospective-field conclusions.

Battery-expert or data-owner adjudication is required for the physical identity of 25C02/25C03, semantics of headerless 35/45 °C columns, whether timestamps adequately capture charge/discharge/rest protocol variation, physical interpretation of stable versus evolving spectral offsets, practical adequacy of 10%/5% margins, acquisition latency and cost, and informative stopping. Microscopic mechanisms, deployment safety/economics, other chemistries, changed-use transfer, and external validity require additional measurements, controlled interventions, independent cells, or another study.

## Selection and deferral record

The simple P/B and full V ridge baselines quantify persistence, capacity history, and the already-acquired rested-full spectrum. The full linear V/VI/VX/VIX ladder is selected as primary because it gives symmetric, explicit nested estimands with all observed frequencies and restrained complexity. Sparse models test a lower-information panel; the matched nonlinear ladder tests scientifically relevant nonlinear interaction that ridge loses. Direct-coordinate models test representation sensitivity.

Neural encoders and equivalent-circuit models are deferred, not prohibited. Revisit neural models only with substantially more independent specimens or reproducible held-cell residual structure. Revisit circuits only with a predeclared identifiable topology and physical validation. States II–IV and VI–VIII are deferred because they would expand the acquisition decision beyond the assigned I-versus-IX question. A new population, prediction boundary, estimand, outcome, analysis family, or falsification rule requires Lead approval as a scientific child, not compiler repair.

Execute the frozen, open-ended experiment below. Determine whether the 11 admitted
Oxford NCR18650BD specimens have a useful specimen-common BoL-to-MoL real-impedance
change across nominal 20%, 50%, and 80% SOC, or whether at least one target requires a
reproducible rank-1 specimen-by-SOC interaction.

The strongest claim established before this task is only data/conversion and numerical

11 cells, with finite `ReZ_Ohm`. The separability hypothesis remains unresolved. Do not
copy the proposal's observed-only pilot numbers into the answer; that pilot omitted the
required calibration and stability analyses.

| group | specimens | cycling rate | cycle/calendar block | class |
|---|---|---:|---:|---|
| 1 | G1_C15, G1_C20 | C/2 | 1/5 days | short |
| 2 | G2_C3, G2_C4, G2_C8 | C/4 | 1/5 days | short |

| 4 | G4_C12, G4_C18, G4_C19 | C/4 | 2/10 days | long |

acquisition clock, equal-age/equal-health guarantee at MoL, capacity normalization,
current sign series, charge return, or independent SOC ground truth for this analysis.
The endpoint is contemporaneous checkpoint change, not a forecast.

Use nominal SOC labels 20, 50, and 80 and `ReZ_Ohm` only. Preserve `N_A` as
uninterpreted `channel2_raw`. Stored row position is `point_index=1..35`; it is not
frequency. The document-level 5 kHz-to-10 mHz statement does not map rows to frequencies.

## Inputs and exact source binding

Runtime inputs are read-only:

- `/data/e05ee114fa-oxford-eis.zip`, SHA-256
  `64d1fc94dcd3b2403d3f84b88666781a4f6153068e2ef4311d7cde97106a6d27`;

- `/data/a90f68c3f0-catalog-v06.json`, SHA-256
  `02afcb6c55ac8d6d1801f4d4ed51adaa45743e5a3461f9c468a1ecf85cf4d8b5`.

For every listed `(group, cell)`, stage in `{BoL,MoL}`, and SOC in
`{20,50,80}`, read archive member

`EIS/{stage}/Group{group}_{stage}_Cell{cell}_SOC{SOC}.mat`

and select internal table

`Group{group}_{stage}_Cell{cell}_SOC{SOC}`.

Each canonical table must have exactly 35 stored rows and exactly the columns
`ReZ_Ohm,N_A`. Reject missing or nonfinite `ReZ_Ohm`, an absent expected internal
name, or conflicting duplicates. Each G2_C3 MoL container exposes all three G2_C3 MoL
tables; the G3_C11 MoL SOC20 container also exposes SOC50 and SOC80. Select by internal
identity, prove repeated payloads equal, and retain one canonical copy. Never concatenate
all table objects blindly.

A public ingestion-only helper is installed at `/opt/task/oxford_loader.py`. Running

`python /opt/task/oxford_loader.py`

creates `source_manifest.csv`, `duplicate_audit.json`, and
`normalized_eis.parquet`. It does not fit a model or supply any scientific result.
You may inspect or replace it, but submitted normalized values must match the source.

Normalize columns to:

`group,cell_id,specimen_key,stage,SOC_label_pct,point_index,ReZ_Ohm,channel2_raw,cycling_rate_C,cycling_block_days,calendar_block_days,periodicity_class`.

Require 66 canonical tables, 2,310 stage rows, and 1,155 rows after joining BoL and MoL
on `(group,cell_id,SOC_label_pct,point_index)`. In `joined_change.parquet`, retain
both stage values as `ReZ_Ohm_BoL`, `ReZ_Ohm_MoL` and define
`dR_Ohm=ReZ_Ohm_MoL-ReZ_Ohm_BoL`.

## Frozen coordinate representation

Let `x=(point_index-1)/34` and `A=[1,x]`. Evaluate exactly:

`SplineTransformer(n_knots=5, degree=3, knots="uniform", include_bias=False, extrapolation="constant")`.

Residualize all spline columns against `col(A)`, take deterministic SVD, orient each
retained left singular vector so its largest-absolute element is positive, and retain
values above `1e-10` times the largest. Concatenate a deterministic QR
orthonormalization of `A` (orient columns by the same rule) with those vectors to make
`Q`. Require affine rank 2, non-affine rank 5, total rank 7, and
`max(abs(Q.T@Q-I)) <= 1e-10`. Store `Q`, singular values, ranks, tolerance and
orthogonality error in `basis_audit.json`.

In every fitting set, calculate SOC mean curves `bar_d[s]`, the grand mean
`bar_m=mean_s(bar_d[s])`, and

`delta[s] = Q @ Q.T @ (bar_d[s]-bar_m)`.

Numerically enforce `sum_s delta[s]=0`. Report retained and discarded population-offset
energy. This is a smooth basis over ordinal index, never a frequency basis.

## Models and held-specimen fitting

Each of 11 outer leave-one-specimen-out folds has three leave-one-SOC-out targets. The
held specimen's two non-target change curves are the only held outcomes exposed to a
predictor. No row, SOC, target scale, offset, loading, residual scale, or tuning decision
from the held specimen may enter fitting.

For target `t` and source SOCs `a,b`:

- **P (population/SOC only):** `pred=bar_m+delta[t]`.
- **A (additive/shared change):**
  `m_hat=((dR[c,a]-delta[a])+(dR[c,b]-delta[b]))/2`, then
  `pred=m_hat+delta[t]`.
- **L1 (rank-1 interaction):** on fitting cells, set
  `m_i=mean_s dR[i,s]`, `e[i,s]=dR[i,s]-m_i-delta[s]`, project each residual
  onto `Q`, concatenate the three seven-coordinate SOC blocks into one row per cell,
  and take an uncentered deterministic SVD. Let the first raw score be `U[:,0]*S[0]`;
  divide it by its sample standard deviation and multiply `Vt[0]` by that same
  standard deviation. Reshape the loading coefficients to SOC by coordinate, map them
  through `Q.T` to `L[s,j]`, and orient score/loading together so the
  largest-absolute loading entry is positive. Require `sum_s L[s,j]=0` to numerical
  tolerance.

For L1, infer the held scalar score only from the two source residuals. Define raw MAD as
`median(abs(v-median(v)))` and

`tau[a,b,j]=max(sqrt(MAD(e[:,a,j])^2+MAD(e[:,b,j])^2),1e-6)`.

With `r=(dR[c,a]-dR[c,b])-(delta[a]-delta[b])` and
`ell=L[a]-L[b]`, minimize
`sum_j ((r[j]-z*ell[j])/tau[j])^2 + lambda*z^2`, i.e.

`z=sum_j ell[j]*r[j]/tau[j]^2 / (sum_j ell[j]^2/tau[j]^2 + lambda)`.

Then average the two source estimates after subtracting `delta+zL`, and predict
`m_hat+delta[t]+zL[t]`. Record
`I/(I+lambda)`, where `I=sum_j ell[j]^2/tau[j]^2`.

Tune one outer-fold penalty over `{0.01,0.1,1,10,100}` by exhaustive inner
leave-one-specimen-out validation, refitting `delta,L,tau` and inner-training target
scales each time. Pool the 30 inner cell-target losses with equal cell/target weight.
Ties choose larger lambda. A selected 100 emits a boundary warning.

For outer fold `o`, target `s`, coordinate `j`, obtain from outer-training target
curves only:

`q[o,s,j]=max(raw_MAD({dR[i,s,j]}),1e-6)`.

Report

`Loss[M,c,s]=mean_j(((dR[c,s,j]-pred[M,c,s,j])/q[o,s,j])^2)`

and raw-ohm RMSE/MAE. Primary weighting is equal across 33 cell-target tasks. Also report
equal-group sensitivity. Define:

- `Gcommon[s]=1-E[A,s]/E[P,s]`;
- `Gint[s]=1-E[L1,s]/E[A,s]`;
- `Gtotal[s]=1-E[L1,s]/E[P,s]`.

Compute aggregate versions from losses averaged over all 33 tasks. The practical margin
is 0.10. Target-specific claims are primary.

## Linkage calibration and uncertainty

For each target separately, enumerate all 432 within-group specimen permutations
(`2!*3!*3!*3!`, identity included). Keep target curves, labels, folds, and target
scales fixed; jointly move the complete pair of non-target source curves from each donor
to a recipient within group. Rerun outer/inner fitting, tuning, offsets, loadings and
predictions for every allocation. Cache P only after equality checks. Compute upper-tail
exact p-values as `count(T_perm >= T_observed)/432` for each target and for both
`Gcommon` and `Gint`. Apply Holm correction over the three targets separately for
the two families. These are conditional linkage tests, not randomized-treatment or
population p-values.

With `numpy.random.Generator(PCG64(20260923))`, generate 10,000 resamples independently
within groups at sizes 2/3/3/3, using common multiplicities across models and targets.
From frozen outer losses calculate all gains. Form a 95% max-standardized simultaneous
band over the six target quantities `Gcommon[20/50/80]` and `Gint[20/50/80]`.
State that this only changes observed-cell weighting: it omits model refitting,
between-group uncertainty, and measurement repeatability.

Delete each specimen and rerun the complete nested observed analysis on ten cells.
Additionally run rank 2, penalty-grid extension to 1000, MAD floors 5e-7 and 2e-6 ohm,
and equal-group weighting. Any primary classification reversal is inconclusive.
Rank 2 cannot rescue failed rank-1 identification.

Repeat observed P/A/L1 fitting on BoL `ReZ_Ohm` surfaces, relearning every parameter
and using no MoL data. Similar BoL and change patterns prohibit an ageing-emergence claim;
differences remain descriptive.

## Required outputs

Write these exact paths under `/workspace`:

- `source_manifest.csv`
- `duplicate_audit.json`
- `normalized_eis.parquet`
- `joined_change.parquet`
- `basis_audit.json`
- `outer_predictions.parquet`
- `outer_losses.csv`
- `offsets_and_loadings.parquet`
- `interaction_diagnostics.json`
- `inner_tuning.csv`
- `linkage_permutations.parquet`
- `conditional_stability.parquet`
- `deletion_metrics.csv`
- `sensitivity_metrics.csv`
- `bol_comparator_metrics.csv`
- `metrics.json`
- `conclusion.json`

- `outer_predictions.parquet`: `specimen_key,target_SOC,point_index,model,observed_dR,predicted_dR,target_scale`; exactly one row for every 11 x 3 x 35 x 3 combination.
- `outer_losses.csv`: `specimen_key,target_SOC,model,scaled_loss,raw_rmse,raw_mae,outer_fold`; exactly 99 rows.
- `inner_tuning.csv`: `outer_fold,lambda,mean_inner_loss,selected`; exactly 55 rows, one selected penalty per fold.
- `linkage_permutations.parquet`: `target_SOC,allocation_id,is_identity,Gcommon,Gint`; exactly 1,296 rows and one identity per target.
- `conditional_stability.parquet`: `resample_id,target_SOC,Gcommon,Gint,Gtotal`; exactly 30,000 rows.
- `deletion_metrics.csv`: `deleted_specimen,target_SOC,Gcommon,Gint,Gtotal,selected_lambda,median_data_fraction,min_loading_cosine`; 33 rows.
- `sensitivity_metrics.csv`: `scenario,target_SOC,Gcommon,Gint,Gtotal,classification_preserved,direction_preserved`, with all five frozen scenarios for each target.
- `bol_comparator_metrics.csv`: one row per target with P/A/L1 losses and gains.
- `offsets_and_loadings.parquet`: include fold, target SOC, point index, `bar_m`, `delta`, L1 loading, retained energy and discarded energy.
- `interaction_diagnostics.json`: selected penalties, boundary warnings, per-target median score data fraction, 11 outer-loading cosines per target, singular values and rank-2 diagnostics.
- `metrics.json`: per-target and aggregate P/A/L1 losses and gains; raw and Holm linkage p-values; simultaneous band endpoints; bootstrap seed/count; practical threshold; and sensitivity/deletion summaries.
- `conclusion.json`: `branch`, target classifications, a concise summary, `asserted_claims`, and limitations/adjudication requirements.

All JSON must be finite strict JSON (no NaN/Infinity). Parquet and CSV numeric fields must
be finite. Include enough intermediate values to make the reported metrics auditable.

## Frozen decision rules

A target has **stringent common-specimen information** only if:

1. `Gcommon >= 0.10`;
2. common-family Holm p-value <= 0.05;
3. simultaneous lower band > 0;
4. all 11 deletion gains are positive and at least 8 are >= 0.10; and
5. floor and group-weight sensitivities preserve classification.

A target has a **required stable interaction** only if:

1. `Gint >= 0.10`, interaction-family Holm p-value <= 0.05, and its simultaneous lower band > 0;
2. all deletion gains are positive and at least 8 are >= 0.10;
3. `Gtotal >= 0.10` with positive uncertainty lower bound;
4. median score data fraction >= 0.20;
5. all 11 absolute loading cosines are >= 0.50; and
6. every frozen sensitivity preserves direction and classification.

Choose exactly one branch:

- `supportive_separability`: all targets have stringent common information; every
  interaction upper bound is below 0.10; no interaction Holm test is significant; every
  interaction lower bound exceeds -0.10; and sensitivities agree.
- `adverse_stable_interaction`: at least one target has a required stable interaction.
  Name all such targets and keep the claim target-specific if not all pass.
- `adverse_no_linkage`: no target identifies a >=10% total linked gain with linkage
  support, or all relevant total-gain uncertainty upper bounds are below 0.10. This is
  failure to identify useful linkage, not evidence for physical separability.
- `inconclusive`: every other valid outcome, including margin-spanning uncertainty,
  calibration disagreement, deletion dependence, weak observability, unstable loadings,
  boundary/rank sensitivity, or mixed common-information results.

Failure of L1 never proves separability. In-sample improvement never establishes an
interaction.

A supportive result permits only a bounded statement that these 11 cells, nominal SOCs,
and this smooth ordinal-index resolution support held-target reconstruction by a common
specimen change plus fixed SOC offsets without resolving a practically important rank-1
interaction. An adverse-interaction result permits only a target-specific predictive
low-rank interaction statement. A no-linkage result says the archive/model did not
identify useful cross-SOC specimen structure. Otherwise report inconclusive.

No output may claim a frequency region, time constant, DRT feature, circuit element,
SEI growth, lithium plating, LLI, LAM, physical latent mode, causal protocol effect,
population transfer, practical anchor optimality, or electrochemical SOC accuracy.
Those require authoritative frequency vectors, timestamps/exposure/capacity data,
SOC equilibration evidence, repeat spectra/noise estimates, matched MoL health,
electrochemical expert review, and an independent prospective cohort. Within-group
exchangeability is an unverified scientific assumption, not something this computation
can prove.

Use 8 CPU cores, 16 GiB RAM and no GPU. Fix BLAS thread counts and all RNG seeds. Record
software versions, wall time, and any checkpoint/restart in `metrics.json`.

# Proposal: is the Oxford checkpoint-change surface separable by specimen and SOC?

## Scientific question, hypothesis, and advance

For the 11 Oxford NCR18650BD cells with paired beginning-of-life (BoL) and middle-of-life (MoL) EIS at nominal 20%, 50%, and 80% SOC, can the three-SOC real-impedance change surface be represented adequately as one specimen-specific change curve shared across SOC plus a low-dimensional population SOC offset, or is a repeatable specimen-by-SOC interaction needed to reconstruct a held cell's third SOC from its other two?

The primary hypothesis is **adequate separability** within a prespecified smooth-coordinate resolution:

`dR[c,s,j] = m[c,j] + delta[s,j] + error[c,s,j]`,

where `dR=ReZ_Ohm(MoL)-ReZ_Ohm(BoL)`, `m[c,j]` is an unrestricted 35-point specimen-common change curve, and each population offset `delta[s,j]` lies in a fixed seven-dimensional basis over stored point index with `sum_s delta[s,j]=0`. Adequacy means that two observed SOC-change curves identify a held specimen's common curve and improve reconstruction of the third SOC by at least 10% over a population/SOC-only predictor, while a learned rank-1 smooth specimen-by-SOC interaction cannot improve the additive model by 10% at any target under simultaneous uncertainty.

The falsifying alternative is a reproducible rank-1 interaction

`dR[c,s,j] = m[c,j] + delta[s,j] + z[c] L[s,j] + error[c,s,j]`,

where the score `z[c]` is inferred only from the held cell's two observed SOCs. This alternative can reveal a recurring direction in which the SOC contrast changes from cell to cell; the additive model discards that information by forcing every cell to have the same SOC offsets.

This is scientifically distinct from the existing source-anchor candidates. Those ask which **one** MoL SOC best predicts the other two, or whether a BoL-informed policy can select that anchor. This experiment observes two SOCs and asks the prior structural question: is there a specimen-common cross-SOC change state at all, and is its residual SOC dependence reproducible enough to be identified in a held specimen? A resolved interaction would warn against further optimizing a single-anchor policy under a separability assumption; resolved separability would justify treating anchor optimization as a lower-dimensional acquisition question. It does not identify an ageing mechanism.

## Evidence supported now and unresolved claim

The strongest supported claim is availability and computational feasibility, not separability. The admitted archive supplies paired nominal-SOC `ReZ_Ohm` curves for 11 cells. A fresh registered MATLAB export on 2026-09-23 completed in 15.47 s: 66 requested containers yielded 74 table objects because of known repeated internal tables; selecting the expected internal variable produced exactly 66 unique canonical tables, each with 35 rows and columns `ReZ_Ohm,N_A`. All 2,310 canonical `ReZ_Ohm` values were finite, repeated variables had no conflicting hashes, native round-trip was verified, and semantic interpretation was not verified.

A bounded observed-linkage CPU diagnostic established numerical feasibility of the fixed seven-dimensional basis, 11 held-cell folds, additive predictor, and regularized rank-1 score inference. Its aggregate scaled losses were 5.391 (population/SOC), 3.107 (additive), and 2.530 (rank 1), corresponding to observed-only gains of 42.4% and 18.6%. Interaction gain was heterogeneous: -10.8% for target 20% and about +68.9% for targets 50% and 80%; all outer folds chose the largest pilot penalty. No linkage permutations, conditional resampling, deletion refits, rank-2 sensitivity, or BoL comparator was run. These numbers motivate the question and warn about regularization-boundary sensitivity; they are not evidence for either hypothesis branch and must not appear as a final result.

The unresolved claim is whether correctly linked, held-specimen source SOCs contain practically important information about a target through (i) a common specimen change and (ii) a stable low-rank SOC interaction, after conditional linkage calibration and uncertainty checks. The archive cannot establish electrochemical SOC accuracy, measurement repeatability, equal physical age or health at MoL, population transfer, or mechanism.

## Population, measurement state, and temporal boundary

Use exactly these 11 specimens:

- Group 1, C/2, short schedule (1 cycling + 5 calendar days): `G1_C15`, `G1_C20`;
- Group 2, C/4, short: `G2_C3`, `G2_C4`, `G2_C8`;
- Group 3, C/2, long schedule (2 cycling + 10 calendar days): `G3_C10`, `G3_C11`, `G3_C14`;
- Group 4, C/4, long: `G4_C12`, `G4_C18`, `G4_C19`.

The source README describes Panasonic NCR18650BD 3 Ah graphite/NCA cells, a 24 degC chamber setpoint, and 100 mA peak-to-peak EIS over a document-level 5 kHz-to-10 mHz range. The analysis uses only the supplied nominal SOC labels 20/50/80 and ordinal stages BoL/MoL. It has no acquisition timestamps, exposure clock, capacity normalization, current-sign series, charge-return calculation, or independent SOC ground truth. `dR[c,s,j]` is contemporaneous checkpoint change, not forecasting. G1_C9 is excluded because MoL is absent; Groups 5-10 are not part of the README-bound paired four-group population in this selected archive.

## Exact read-only binding

Use unchanged sources:

- catalog `[private path]`, SHA-256 `02afcb6c55ac8d6d1801f4d4ed51adaa45743e5a3461f9c468a1ecf85cf4d8b5`, runtime `/data/a90f68c3f0-catalog-v06.json`;
- documentation `[private path]`, SHA-256 `59489534eaa5cddd2cef74b057855d2074bbef802d3aa12db6e082f9886dc59c`, runtime `/data/4a245ba1d6-oxford-readme.txt`;
- EIS archive `[private path]`, SHA-256 `64d1fc94dcd3b2403d3f84b88666781a4f6153068e2ef4311d7cde97106a6d27`, runtime `/data/e05ee114fa-oxford-eis.zip`.

The exact 66 members are the Cartesian product of the 11 `(group,cell)` pairs above, `stage in {BoL,MoL}`, and `SOC in {20,50,80}`, with member name

`EIS/{stage}/Group{group}_{stage}_Cell{cell}_SOC{SOC}.mat`

and required internal MATLAB table

`Group{group}_{stage}_Cell{cell}_SOC{SOC}`.

Require exactly 35 stored rows and columns exactly `ReZ_Ohm,N_A`; fail on missing/nonfinite `ReZ_Ohm`, an unexpected variable name, or conflicting duplicates. The three G2_C3 MoL containers each expose all three G2_C3 MoL SOC tables; the G3_C11 MoL SOC20 container additionally exposes its SOC50 and SOC80 tables. Select by expected internal-variable identity, retain one canonical copy only after exact equality, and never concatenate every table object blindly.

Normalize to `group,cell_id,specimen_key,stage,SOC_label_pct,point_index,ReZ_Ohm,channel2_raw,cycling_rate_C,cycling_block_days,calendar_block_days,periodicity_class`. Set `specimen_key="G{group}_C{cell}"`, `point_index=1..35` in stored order, and retain `N_A` only as uninterpreted `channel2_raw`. Join BoL to MoL on `(group,cell_id,SOC_label_pct,point_index)`. Require 66 canonical tables, 2,310 stage rows, and 1,155 joined change rows.

No row-level frequency column is admitted. `point_index` is only an aligned stored coordinate. Do not label indices as frequencies or infer frequency bands, time constants, DRT peaks, circuit elements, or electrochemical processes. The source's document-level frequency range does not supply the row mapping.

## Fixed coordinate representation

Let `x=(point_index-1)/34`. Form `A=[1,x]`. Evaluate once, independent of outcomes, `SplineTransformer(n_knots=5,degree=3,knots="uniform",include_bias=False,extrapolation="constant")`; residualize its columns against `col(A)`, take deterministic SVD, orient each vector so its largest-absolute entry is positive, and retain singular vectors above `1e-10` times the largest. Concatenate orthonormalized `A` with the retained non-affine vectors to obtain `Q`. Require affine rank 2, non-affine rank 5, total rank 7, and numerical orthogonality. `Q` is a smooth basis over index, not a frequency basis.

In each fitting set, compute the mean curve by SOC `bar_d[s,j]`, grand mean `bar_m[j]=mean_s bar_d[s,j]`, and low-dimensional offsets

`delta[s,:] = Q Q' (bar_d[s,:]-bar_m[:])`,

then enforce `sum_s delta[s,:]=0` numerically. This restriction is part of the hypothesis; report the discarded population-offset energy rather than silently treating it as noise.

## Three matched models and prediction rule

Every outer held specimen contributes three leave-one-SOC-out tasks. For target `t`, only its other two `dR` curves are exposed to the predictor.

1. **P, population/SOC-only comparator.** Predict `bar_m + delta[t]`. It uses no held-cell change and tests whether specimen linkage adds information.
2. **A, additive/shared-change baseline.** For source SOCs `a,b`, estimate `m_hat=(dR[c,a]-delta[a]+dR[c,b]-delta[b])/2`, then predict `m_hat+delta[t]`. This is the simple separable model.
3. **L1, learned rank-1 interaction.** On fitting cells set `m_i=mean_s dR[i,s]` and `e[i,s]=dR[i,s]-m_i-delta[s]`. Project each `e[i,s]` onto `Q`, stack the three SOC coefficient blocks by cell, and take deterministic SVD. The first right singular vector, scaled so its training scores have unit sample variance, defines `L[s,j]`; orient its sign by its largest-absolute entry and require `sum_s L[s,j]=0`. For a held target, infer scalar `z` only from the difference of the two source residuals by weighted ridge, using fitting-only coordinate scales `tau[a,b,j]=sqrt(MAD(e[:,a,j])^2+MAD(e[:,b,j])^2)` floored at `1e-6 ohm`. Minimize the weighted source-difference residual plus `lambda*z^2`, estimate `m_hat` after subtracting `zL` from both sources, and predict `m_hat+delta[t]+zL[t]`.

Tune `lambda in {0.01,0.1,1,10,100}`. The maximum-grid choice is permitted but triggers a boundary warning; extending once to 1000 is a frozen sensitivity, not a post-hoc replacement. Report the data fraction `I/(I+lambda)`, where `I` is the weighted source-contrast loading energy. If its median is below 0.20 for a target, interaction scores are treated as weakly observable and no stable-mode interpretation is allowed.

The primary learned alternative is rank 1 because it asks whether one recurring specimen-specific SOC contrast exists with only 11 independent cells. Repeat with rank 2 as a frozen sensitivity. Rank 2 may refine a rank-1 result but cannot rescue a failed rank-1 primary claim; a reversal makes the interaction conclusion model-dependent/inconclusive.

## Held-cell fitting, outcomes, and estimands

Use 11 outer leave-one-specimen-out folds. No row, SOC, stage, target scale, offset, interaction loading, residual scale, or tuning decision from the held specimen may enter fitting. Within each outer training set, tune L1 with exhaustive leave-one-specimen-out inner folds, refitting `delta,L,tau` in every inner fit. Pool inner loss with equal weight per specimen and target; ties choose larger `lambda`. A group may become absent in an inner fit, but no group parameter is fitted.

For outer fold `o`, target `s`, and coordinate `j`, compute from outer-training target curves only

`q[o,s,j]=max(raw_MAD({dR[i,s,j]}),1e-6 ohm)`.

For model `M`, held cell `c`, target `s`, define

`Loss[M,c,s]=(1/35) sum_j ((dR[c,s,j]-pred[M,c,s,j])/q[o,s,j])^2`.

Each cell and SOC has equal primary weight. Report raw-ohm RMSE and MAE secondarily, plus group-balanced summaries as sensitivity. Define target-specific and aggregate gains:

- common specimen information: `Gcommon[s]=1-E[A,s]/E[P,s]`;
- learned interaction information: `Gint[s]=1-E[L1,s]/E[A,s]`;
- total linked information: `Gtotal[s]=1-E[L1,s]/E[P,s]`.

Aggregate gains use the ratio of losses averaged equally over all 33 held cell-target tasks. The frozen practical effect threshold is 0.10 (10% relative loss reduction). Target-specific claims are primary because an aggregate can hide opposing SOC behavior.

Also report per-cell/target paired losses, interaction scores, offset/interaction projection energy, discarded energy, loading contrasts, singular values, outer-fold loading cosine similarity after sign alignment, and residual plots against point index. Repeated coordinates are not independent observations; inference is at specimen level.

## Conditional linkage calibration and uncertainty

For each target SOC separately, enumerate all 432 within-group specimen permutations (`2!*3!*3!*3!`, identity included). Keep target curves, specimen/group labels, folds, and target scales fixed; jointly reassign the complete pair of non-target source-SOC change curves from one donor to one recipient within group. Joint movement preserves the two sources' mutual covariance and marginal curves while breaking their physical linkage to the target. Rerun all outer/inner fits, offset/loading learning, tuning, and predictions for every allocation. P may be cached only after exact equality checks.

For each target compute upper-tail exact p-values for `Gcommon` and `Gint` as `count(T_perm>=T_obs)/432`. Apply Holm correction across the three target SOCs separately for the common-information family and the interaction family. These are conditional sharp-null linkage tests, not randomized-experiment or population p-values. Their scientific interpretation requires unverified within-group exchangeability conditional on the documented protocols.

Using `numpy.random.Generator(PCG64(20260923))`, draw 10,000 resamples independently within groups at sizes 2/3/3/3, using common cell multiplicities for P/A/L1 and all targets. From frozen outer losses compute individual intervals and a 95% max-standardized simultaneous band across the six target gains (`Gcommon[20/50/80]`, `Gint[20/50/80]`). These describe sensitivity to weighting the observed cells; they omit refitting, between-group uncertainty, and measurement repeatability.

Separately delete each specimen and rerun the complete nested observed analysis on the remaining ten. Report every gain, selected penalty, interaction observability, and loading similarity. Run the rank-2, `lambda`-grid extension, raw-MAD floor `{5e-7,2e-6}` ohm, and equal-group-weight sensitivities. Any primary classification reversal is inconclusive.

As a structural comparator, repeat observed P/A/L1 held-cell fitting on BoL `ReZ_Ohm` surfaces rather than `dR`, with all parameters learned anew and no MoL data. Similar BoL and change patterns prohibit a claim that the interaction emerged through ageing; different patterns are descriptive because scales and outcomes differ. No comparator result establishes mechanism.

## Frozen falsification and outcome branches

A target has **stringent common-specimen information** only if `Gcommon[s]>=0.10`, its three-test Holm p-value is at most 0.05, the simultaneous lower band is above zero, every deletion preserves positive gain and at least 8 of 11 deletion gains remain at or above 0.10, and floor/group-weight sensitivities preserve classification.

A target has a **required stable interaction** only if `Gint[s]>=0.10`, its three-test Holm p-value is at most 0.05, the simultaneous lower band is above zero, every deletion preserves positive gain and at least 8 of 11 remain at or above 0.10, `Gtotal[s]>=0.10` with a positive simultaneous lower band, median score data fraction is at least 0.20, every outer loading has absolute cosine at least 0.50 with the full-data descriptive loading, and all frozen sensitivities preserve direction and classification.

- **Supportive for adequate separability:** all three targets have stringent common-specimen information; every `Gint` simultaneous upper bound is below 0.10; no interaction Holm test is significant; L1 does not materially worsen any target (`Gint` lower bound above -0.10); and sensitivities agree. Conclude only that, for these cells and this index-based smooth resolution, a common specimen change plus SOC offsets reconstructs held targets and no practically important rank-1 interaction is resolved.
- **Adverse / separability falsified:** at least one target has a required stable interaction. Name each target. Conclude that a specimen-common change plus fixed SOC offsets is inadequate for that target and that a reproducible low-rank specimen-by-SOC term improves held-cell reconstruction. If other targets do not pass, call the result target-specific, not a universal three-SOC latent state.
- **Adverse / specimen linkage not identified:** neither A nor L1 has a 10% total gain over P for any target with linkage support, or all relevant simultaneous upper bounds are below 0.10. Conclude that this archive/model does not identify useful held-specimen cross-SOC structure. This is not evidence of physical separability.
- **Inconclusive:** every other valid outcome, including margin-spanning bands, permutation/uncertainty disagreement, deletion dependence, unstable loadings, weak score observability, tuning-boundary dependence, rank sensitivity, or common information at only some targets without a stable interaction decision. Preserve mixed and unfavorable results.

Failure of L1 alone never proves separability. Conversely, a lower in-sample reconstruction error never establishes interaction; the adverse branch requires held-cell improvement, correct linkage, practical magnitude, and stability.

## Scientific meaning and limits

Supportive separability would justify a narrower diagnostic-design assumption: within these 11 cells, the two measured nominal SOC changes share enough cell-specific information to reconstruct the third without a material rank-1 smooth interaction. A required-interaction result would show that cell identity changes the SOC contrast in a repeatable predictive way, making one-size-fits-all anchor reasoning scientifically incomplete. Either result advances beyond choosing the best source anchor because it adjudicates the representation that makes anchor policies meaningful.

No result identifies SEI growth, lithium plating, LLI, LAM, a frequency region, or an equivalent-circuit process. `ReZ_Ohm` is a measured real-impedance column; `dR` is a derived checkpoint difference; `m`, `delta`, `z`, and `L` are fitted statistical states. Stronger claims about physical SOC, ageing-specific emergence, causal protocol effects, or external cells require authoritative frequency vectors, acquisition order/timestamps, SOC equilibration/accuracy, replicate spectra, exposure/health matching at MoL, capacity/throughput records, and an independent prospective cohort. Practical anchor choice additionally requires acquisition time, safety, cost, and measurement-noise data.

## Alternatives and selection record

P and A are the simple comparators: P removes held identity entirely; A retains an unrestricted specimen-common curve but allows only fixed smooth SOC offsets. L1 is selected as the substantive learned alternative because it can expose a recurring specimen-specific SOC contrast that A necessarily averages away, while estimating only one held-cell score from the two available source curves.

Rank 2 is retained only as sensitivity. A full specimen-by-SOC 3x35 interaction, outcome-tuned PCA dimension, tensor neural network, nonlinear kernel, or per-group loading could fit idiosyncrasies with 11 cells and would not answer whether a minimal repeatable interaction is identifiable. Revisit those methods with a larger prospectively held-out cohort and repeat spectra. Equivalent-circuit and DRT alternatives are deferred because row-level frequency and imaginary-impedance semantics are unavailable. GPU use adds no scientific value for this small linear-algebra experiment.

The observed-only pilot supports selecting, not accepting, L1: it showed a possible aggregate gain but opposite target behavior and regularization at the grid boundary. That is exactly why target-specific calibration, score-observability checks, and frozen adverse/inconclusive branches are required.

## Deliverable, compute, and verification

Completion requires newly fitting all 33 outer P/A/L1 predictions with nested tuning, all 1,296 target-specific linkage allocations, 10,000 conditional resamples, 11 deletion reruns, all frozen sensitivities, and the BoL comparator. Required outputs are:

`source_manifest.csv`, `duplicate_audit.json`, `normalized_eis.parquet`, `joined_change.parquet`, `basis_audit.json`, `outer_predictions.parquet`, `outer_losses.csv`, `offsets_and_loadings.parquet`, `interaction_diagnostics.json`, `inner_tuning.csv`, `linkage_permutations.parquet`, `conditional_stability.parquet`, `deletion_metrics.csv`, `sensitivity_metrics.csv`, `bol_comparator_metrics.csv`, `metrics.json`, and `conclusion.json`.

Use 8 CPU cores, 16 GiB RAM, no GPU, deterministic BLAS/thread settings, and allocation-level parallelism over permutations with checkpoints after each target and every 108 allocations. The native export measured 15.47 s and the bounded observed diagnostic measured 2.2 s on CPU. The complete optimized experiment is estimated, not measured, at 30-90 minutes and is designed to remain below the configured 9,000 science-second envelope.

The verifier can recompute source hashes, expected internal-variable selection, duplicate equality, joins, basis rank, all splits, offsets, SVD orientation/scaling, score inference, tuning, predictions, losses, permutations, multiplicity, resamples, deletions, sensitivities, and frozen-rule wording. It must accept supportive, adverse, or inconclusive results when correctly computed and reject correct numbers paired with unsupported mechanistic, frequency, causal, population, or practical claims. Exchangeability, SOC validity, measurement comparability, latent-mode physical meaning, and external importance require scientific adjudication or additional data; automation cannot establish them.

## Inspected evidence

- Raj and Howey, *Path Dependent Battery Degradation Dataset 1*, DOI `10.5287/bodleian:v0ervBv6p`: admitted README, catalog inventory, ZIP member list, and all 66 selected native tables were inspected.
- Raj et al. (2020), *Investigation of Path-Dependent Degradation in Lithium-Ion Batteries*, DOI `10.1002/batt.202000160`: only the curated repository/paper summary and public metadata were available here; publisher full text and supplementary methods were not acquired and are not claimed read.
- The project seed review notes that EIS can depend on SOC and that predictive impedance features do not by themselves identify microscopic degradation. This proposal treats that as motivation and preserves a nonmechanistic interpretation.
