# Zhang2020 prospective rate-shape experiment

## Objective

Perform the complete frozen scientific investigation, not a prerequisite audit. Determine whether a current within-cell update in the observed V-to-IX transition clock and/or the current IX-minus-V impedance update carries held-cell predictive information about prospective measured discharge-capacity trajectory shape beyond capacity history and all eligible clock/spectral observations through cycle `c-1`.

The confirmatory hypothesis is:

> Conditional on capacity history and all clock/spectral measurements through cycle `c-1`, adding the current clock update and/or current IX-minus-V update reduces family-balanced held-cell MAE by at least 10% for both near- and late-future changes from the preceding fade rate, or by at least 10% for the late-minus-near rate change, with specimen-level simultaneous uncertainty excluding zero and no material family reversal.

This is an open-ended estimation task. No fitted result or reference answer is supplied. A favorable result is not preferred. Preserve supportive, adverse, endpoint-only, no-value, falsified, and inconclusive outcomes.

## Evidence boundary

Existing source audits establish feasibility only: 2,786 complete I/V/IX triples in the frozen ten-cell cohort, 2,054 H10 origins, 1,974 H20 origins, exact contiguous target availability, and variation in the proposed outcomes. They do **not** establish diagnostic-update benefit, population-wide acceleration, mechanism, causality, safety value, or practical utility.

The strongest claim this experiment can support is conditional predictive information about the measured-capacity trajectory in these ten archived coin cells under the specified held-cell procedure. Here “acceleration” means curvature of measured capacity versus cycle. It is not a knee, safety event, microscopic transition, or degradation mechanism.

## Runtime and resources

Use Python 3.11 and the supplied `numpy`, `pandas`, `scipy`, `scikit-learn`, and `joblib` packages. The intended envelope is 16 CPUs, 64 GiB RAM, zero GPUs, and at most seven hours. Cap numerical-library threads and parallelize outer folds. The full nested-fit runtime is an estimate, not a measured benchmark.

Inputs are read-only under `/data`; write all work and required outputs under `/workspace`.

## Frozen population and time boundaries

Confirmatory cells are exactly:

`25C01, 25C04, 25C05, 25C06, 25C07, 25C08, 35C01, 35C02, 45C01, 45C02`.

Temperature family is the numeric prefix 25, 35, or 45. EIS tokens `25C02` and `25C03` are excluded before all confirmatory fitting, preprocessing, tuning, interval calibration, and inference. Their two alternative identity mappings are sensitivity analyses only.

For every origin cycle `c`, enforce:

`capacity(c-1) discharge end < I(c) start < V(c) end < IX(c) start < IX(c) end < capacity(c) charge start < capacity(c) discharge end`.

The landmarks are:

- LV, end of V(c): Q through c-1, I(c), V(c), cycles 1–5 anchors, and c-1 diagnostics are available. Freeze A1 here.
- LD, start of IX(c): `D(c)=IX_start(c)-V_end(c)` and `U_D` become available. Freeze AD here. IX(c) impedance is unavailable.
- LX, end of IX(c): IX-minus-V and `U_X` become available. Freeze AX-side and ADX here.

Q[c] and later capacity values are outcomes and must never enter deployable features, preprocessing, tuning, calibration, or feature selection.

## Exact bound sources

Use only:

- `/data/17d989a618-zhang-eis.zip`, SHA-256 `b9d0b000bd9a90b1e18a1ce1f5763babbd54f2668c9cd902b505bbe46dfda751`
- `/data/cd7217778f-zhang-capacity.zip`, SHA-256 `1b43100ff5695338a103c9c96c0798f71eade889a20a0eb27cd35afe876a942d`
- `/data/a90f68c3f0-catalog-v06.json`, SHA-256 `02afcb6c55ac8d6d1801f4d4ed51adaa45743e5a3461f9c468a1ecf85cf4d8b5`

For token T, use archive members `EIS data/EIS_state_I_T.txt`, `EIS data/EIS_state_V_T.txt`, `EIS data/EIS_state_IX_T.txt`, and `Capacity data/Data_Capacity_T.txt`. Exact table IDs, fields, and expected risk sets are in `data-contract.md`.

EIS joins are exact on (frozen cell token, integer cycle, state, exact frequency), never nearest-time or row-order joins. Fields 0–4 are time/s, cycle, frequency/Hz, Re(Z)/Ohm, and stored -Im(Z)/Ohm. Headed 25 C files have seven fields. Headerless 35/45 C files must reproduce the seven-field layout and grid; this is reproducibility, not independent validation of unresolved semantics. Every spectrum has 60 finite unique descending frequencies from 20,004.453 to 0.01999 Hz. JSON-encode the 60-float list with compact separators; its SHA-256 must be `651b878c886a5deb40c50a612343b25bbd45ff97c5919d49a76419517d54d226`. Preserve ohms and the stored negative-imaginary sign.

Capacity joins are exact on (frozen cell token, integer cycle). Four-field rows are time/s, cycle, ox/red, capacity/mA.h. Six-field rows insert Ewe/V and I/mA before final-field capacity. Define Q as the maximum finite positive final-field capacity for ox/red=0; where current exists verify it is negative on this branch. Q is measured cycler discharge capacity, not charge return, SOC, a BMS estimate, a fitted state, or a mechanism label. Do not invent an SOC anchor.

## Outcomes

For ten capacities `q[0:10]`, define positive fade rate in mAh/cycle:

`g(q) = -median((q[k]-q[j])/(k-j) for 0 <= j < k <= 9)`.

At each origin:

- `g_pre = g(Q[c-10:c])`
- `g_near = g(Q[c:c+10])`
- `g_late = g(Q[c+10:c+20])`
- `A_near = g_near - g_pre`
- `A_late = g_late - g_pre`
- `A_shape = g_late - g_near`
- `L10 = Q[c-1]-Q[c+9]`
- `L20 = Q[c-1]-Q[c+19]`
- secondary `R10 = Q[c]-Q[c+9]`, `R20 = Q[c]-Q[c+19]`.

A_near uses the 2,054-origin H10 set. A_late and A_shape use the 1,974-origin H20 set. Use the 1,974-origin common set for paired persistence claims. Keep negative outcomes. Never impute censored future capacity.

## Predictors and rungs

For z equal to scalar D or the 120-component `X=IX-V` vector ordered as Re then stored -Im on the exact frequency grid:

- `S_z[i] = componentwise median(z[i,1],...,z[i,5])`
- `P_z[i,c] = z[i,c-1]-S_z[i]`
- `U_z[i,c] = z[i,c]-z[i,c-1]`.

Require `S+P+U=z(c)` to absolute error at most 1e-9 s for D and 1e-12 ohm for X. These are observed summaries, not latent calibration, degradation state, or physical innovation.

History B contains c, log(1+c), numeric and one-hot family, Q0, Q[c-1], Q[c-1]/Q0, all ten Q[c-10:c-1]/Q0 values, nine first differences, five- and ten-cycle OLS slopes, their difference, a ten-cycle quadratic coefficient and residual SD, and predeclared family-by-age/level/slope interactions. Current V and `dI=V-I` enter at LV.

Fit identical rows and folds for:

- A1: B + current V + current dI + S_D + P_D + S_X + P_X
- AD: A1 + U_D
- AX-side: A1 + U_X
- ADX: A1 + U_D + U_X.

Also retain the chronological A1→AD→ADX comparison. Side comparisons, not order, adjudicate clock- or IX-specific information.

For target Y define family-balanced held-cell relative MAE gains:

- `Delta_D,Y=(E(A1,Y)-E(AD,Y))/E(A1,Y)`
- `Delta_X,Y=(E(A1,Y)-E(AX-side,Y))/E(A1,Y)`
- `Delta_joint,Y=(E(A1,Y)-E(ADX,Y))/E(A1,Y)`.

Also report absolute MAE changes in target units.

## Required model families

1. Persistence null: predict all three A outcomes as zero and predict future capacity as `Q[c-1]-h*g_pre`.
2. Primary direct model: weighted ridge fitted separately to A_near, A_late, A_shape, L10, and L20. Standardize on outer-training cells only. Tune alpha in {0.01,0.1,1,10,100} and cubic age-spline df in {3,5,7} using inner leave-one-training-cell-out family-balanced cell MAE. Fit both full spectra and a sparse representation using Re and stored -Im at exactly 17.79613 and 2.16054 Hz.
3. Functional nonlinear alternative: on H20 origins predict `T_h=Q[c+h]-Q[c-1]` for h=0,…,19 at each rung. Represent training targets in a fixed six-degree-of-freedom cubic B-spline basis over h. Fit weighted PCA separately to V, dI, S_X, P_X, and U_X, retaining the smallest rank reaching 99% weighted training variance capped by tuned {10,20}. Apply an RBF Nystroem map and multi-output ridge. Tune gamma in {0.5,1,2} times inverse median squared training distance, landmarks in {128,256} capped by training rows, ridge alpha on the direct grid, and roughness penalty in {0,0.1,1,10}. Seed all randomized operations with 20260923. Derive A predictions from each reconstructed trajectory and observed g_pre.

Evaluate functional integrated 20-step MAE and derived outcome errors. It can reveal coordinated bends discarded by independent scalar fits. It is not mechanistic evidence. Functional-only support is exploratory; a sign reversal against primary ridge makes the affected conclusion inconclusive.

## Splits, weights, and evaluation

Use ten outer leave-one-confirmatory-cell-out folds. Every row, cycle, frequency, spectrum, origin, and overlapping window from a cell stays in that cell's fold. The held cell supplies only prediction-time observations available at the landmark. It supplies no outcomes for training, scaling, PCA, spline-target fitting, Nystroem landmarks, hyperparameters, residual calibration, feature selection, or tuning. Inner validation leaves one training cell out.

For training origin (i,c), assign weight `1/(F*n_f*n_i)`, where F is represented families, n_f is training cells in its family, and n_i is eligible origins for cell i; renormalize weights to the training-row count. Use weights in ridge loss, spline tuning, weighted PCA, and weighted landmark sampling.

Evaluation first averages origins within cell, then cells equally within family, then the three families equally. Report origin-, cell-, family-, age-third-, and aggregate MAE, RMSE, bias, and 90% interval coverage/width/interval score. Overlapping origins are never independent specimens.

For each outer fold/model/target, construct symmetric 90% intervals only from inner held-cell residuals. Reduce each of m inner calibration cells to its 90th-percentile absolute residual (NumPy method `higher`), sort those m values, and select one-indexed rank `ceil(0.90*(m+1))` clipped to m.

For the eleven claim-gating primary-ridge contrasts (D, X, joint for each A target plus joint L10 and L20), run 10,000 paired stratified cell bootstraps, sampling cells with replacement within each family, seed 20260923. Recompute family-balanced deltas. For a deterministic simultaneous 95% max-deviation band, compute each draw's maximum absolute deviation in relative-delta units across all eleven contrasts from the observed vector; use the 95th percentile with method `higher` as common radius. Save all draws. Also enumerate all 2^10 shared cell-level sign assignments on paired cell absolute-error gains and save every signed family-balanced contrast as a finite-cohort sensitivity. These coarse ten-cell summaries do not create more independent specimens.

## Mandatory controls

Run and save all of these without changing the confirmatory population:

1. A_near on the H20 set; the all-cell common-support window is c=10–15.
2. Replace Theil-Sen by OLS slope and median adjacent-cycle loss.
3. Repeat outcomes with Q/Q0 and with ox/red=1 extraction.
4. Replace cycles 1–5 anchors by cycle 1 and cycles 1–3; replace U by zero, one-cycle lag, and five-cycle pre-origin slope.
5. Add absolute experiment time and I/V/IX sweep timing only where available.
6. Remove highest-frequency complex translation; use highest-frequency only; compare direct I/V/IX with difference coordinates.
7. Permute whole U trajectories among cells within family on common-support windows, never origins.
8. Hash and reject exact train/test spectrum duplicates.
9. Run family holdout and age-forward cutoffs tau={50,100,150}.
10. Report target availability and baseline covariates for censored tail origins.
11. Run both disputed 25C02/03 identity mappings as non-confirmatory sensitivities.

Refit preprocessing and models inside each applicable training fold. Record controls even when adverse or inconclusive.

## Decision rules

The 10% relevance and 5% no-value margins are design choices, not literature facts. Use the simultaneous primary-ridge bands and the following gates exactly.

- Persistent rate-change support for D, X, or joint requires Delta≥0.10 for A_near on H10 and A_late on H20; both simultaneous lower bounds >0; A_near gain >0 on the H20 common set; gain in at least two families and no family below -0.10; coverage for both outcomes in [0.80,1.00]; and no negative-direction reversal under OLS-slope or normalized-capacity refits. A_late is scored, not inferred from A_near.
- Within-future acceleration support requires Delta≥0.10 for A_shape; simultaneous lower bound >0; gain in at least two families and none below -0.10; coverage in [0.80,1.00]; and positive-direction agreement under OLS and the functional alternative.
- A side contrast can support its named modality. A joint-only result supports combined acquisition information and cannot assign modality. Sequential AD→ADX is descriptive when blocks overlap.
- Endpoint-only information is supported only when at least one joint endpoint comparator passes its inherited 10% gate (point Delta≥0.10 and lower bound >0) while every joint A contrast has simultaneous upper bound ≤0.05.
- No useful current trajectory information is supported only when every joint A upper bound is ≤0.05, coverage is acceptable, and no family has >0.10 gain.
- A named block is adverse when its relevant simultaneous upper bounds are ≤0 with no common-support reversal.
- The global hypothesis is falsified as posed only when joint simultaneous upper bounds are <0.10 for A_near, A_late, and A_shape. A negative mean A_shape is not falsification because both signs are predicted.
- Otherwise classify the affected claim inconclusive, including an interval crossing zero or a margin, family conflict, H10/H20 conflict, poor calibration, identity dependence, target-definition reversal, side/joint conflict, direct/functional conflict, or too few effective specimens.

A valid conclusion can be supportive, adverse, endpoint-only, no-value, falsified, or inconclusive. Do not “rescue” a failed primary gate with another model or sensitivity.

## Required outputs

Produce every file listed in `submission-contract.md` and obey its exact schemas. In summary, submit source and software manifests; executable analysis code; source-derived ledgers; fold/tuning/preprocessing manifests; every held-cell direct, sparse, functional, and sensitivity prediction; inner calibration predictions; bootstrap/sign-flip draws; independently reproducible metrics and uncertainty; and `conclusion.json` linking each claim to exact metric and interval IDs. `report.md` must explain results and uncertainty, including adverse and null findings.

The verifier independently rebuilds Q and primary outcomes from the ZIPs, audits exact cells/origins and held-cell splits, recomputes metrics and decision labels from submitted held-cell predictions, and checks conclusions against those results. Correct numbers with unsupported conclusions fail. Malformed, canned, leaky, row-split, or truth-as-predictor submissions fail.

## Claims outside computation

Automatic checks cannot establish the physical identity of 25C02/03, validate headerless field meanings, determine protocol operations inside D, establish that 10% is practically meaningful, identify a safety-relevant knee, value acquisition burden, infer causality or microscopic degradation, or generalize beyond these ten coin cells. Those require data-owner/electrochemical review, protocol logs, measurement-resolution evidence, independent compatible specimens, controlled intervention, and/or another study. Do not claim them.

# Zhang2020 prospective rate-shape experiment: do current clock or IX-minus-V updates forecast a persistent change in fade rate?

## Scientific decision and falsifiable question

“Persistent fade” defined only as a robust slope over the same interval as a fixed-horizon loss would be mostly a reparameterization. The new read-only audit confirms that concern: on the 1,974 H20 origins, the future 20-point Theil-Sen fade rate correlates 0.9855 with the corresponding endpoint rate. That scalar is retained only as a noise-robust guardrail.

The viable scientific advance is instead prospective trajectory shape. At each origin, compare three non-overlapping ten-capacity windows: the observed past, the near future, and the late future. Ask whether the current within-cell update in the observed V-to-IX transition clock and/or the current IX-minus-V impedance update predicts whether fade rate changes promptly and remains changed, or changes again within the next 20 cycles.

The confirmatory hypothesis is:

> Conditional on capacity history and all clock/spectral measurements through cycle c-1, adding the current clock update and/or current IX-minus-V update reduces family-balanced held-cell MAE by at least 10% for both the near- and late-future changes from the preceding fade rate, or by at least 10% for the late-minus-near rate change, with specimen-level simultaneous uncertainty excluding zero and no material family reversal.

These are two separately adjudicated claims: persistent rate-change information and within-future acceleration information. A result need not confirm either. Positive values mean faster measured-capacity loss, negative values mean slowing; the model is scored on both. “Acceleration” here means curvature of the measured capacity trajectory, not a battery knee, safety event, causal transition, or microscopic mechanism.

This matters because a single future capacity can move because of endpoint fluctuation while the surrounding trajectory does not change. A repeatable prospective warning of a sustained rate change could inform when another diagnostic or maintenance decision is warranted. Zhang et al. (2020; DOI 10.1038/s41467-020-15235-7; inspected full-text source ID 33086e0650f9774d98a2853f7973f0a88c4e8c045703abb09e08fa21aadabf79, SHA-256 ef60f78e673d5bc5c93aecf68520f4b018343f2d4465b56acb0ca6be71ac0144) establishes the 12-cell, multi-state EIS setting and EIS-based capacity/RUL prediction. It does not establish this prospective rate-shape claim. No unavailable supplement or inaccessible knee-review text is treated as inspected evidence.

## What the evidence already supports, and what remains untested

The parent established 2,786 complete same-token, same-cycle I/V/IX triples on one exact 60-frequency grid, universal I-before-V-before-IX ordering, a 0.000995–0.002005 s IX-end to next capacity-cycle charge handoff, and 2,054 H10 / 1,974 H20 eligible origins in ten conservatively identified cells. It also established complete cycles 1–5 and c-1 for all origins and an exact observation-based decomposition of clock and IX-minus-V measurements into early anchor, prior change, and current update.

The new audit, `zhang_rate_shape_audit.py` (SHA-256 `cc73000c275cb79639c4df95542759a68b2e804540ddf66090c1d81e4f446416`) and `zhang_rate_shape_audit.json` (SHA-256 `aaa58343cb45a3f9a38d6259bf097658b151dbe1b44a894582b824a2c2b7921a`), verifies:

- every retained capacity file has an unbroken exact integer-cycle sequence from cycle 0 to its last recorded cycle;
- requiring all ten future capacities leaves exactly the parent's 2,054 H10 origins; requiring all twenty leaves exactly its 1,974 H20 origins;
- H20 pooled descriptive correlations with endpoint loss are 0.3752 for near-minus-past rate change, 0.3553 for late-minus-past rate change, and only 0.06235 for late-minus-near rate change;
- near and late rate changes have the same sign for 73.20% of origins, while only 33.28% are positive in both windows; pooled medians are slightly negative and both signs are common.

These repeated-origin summaries establish availability, non-algebraic redundancy, and outcome variation only. They are not held-cell prognostic evidence, do not establish a cohort-wide acceleration, and do not make 1,974 overlapping origins independent. The unresolved claim is whether current D or IX-minus-V updates carry cell-transferable prospective information about these rate changes after all prior observations.

## Population, landmarks, and exact outcomes

The confirmatory physical-cell keys remain exactly:

`25C01, 25C04, 25C05, 25C06, 25C07, 25C08, 35C01, 35C02, 45C01, 45C02`.

EIS tokens 25C02 and 25C03 remain excluded before fitting because their capacity filenames conflict with acquisition-clock continuity. They cannot enter tuning, preprocessing, interval construction, or confirmation. A row, frequency, cycle, spectrum, origin, or overlapping future window is not an independent specimen.

For origin cycle c, preserve the exact chronology:

`capacity(c-1) discharge end < I(c) start < V(c) end < IX(c) start < IX(c) end < capacity(c) charge start < capacity(c) discharge end`.

Landmarks remain:

1. **LV, end V(c):** Q through c-1, I(c), V(c), and every cycle-1:5 anchor and c-1 prior diagnostic are available; freeze the no-current-update forecast.

- `S_z[i]=componentwise median(z[i,1],...,z[i,5])`;

- `U_z[i,c]=z[i,c]-z[i,c-1]`.

Current V and `dI=V-I` enter at LV.

Use four matched rungs:

- **A1 (LV):** B + current V + current dI + S_D + P_D + S_X + P_X.
- **AD (LD):** A1 + U_D.
- **AX-side (LX):** A1 + U_X.
- **ADX (LX):** A1 + U_D + U_X.

Also fit the chronological A1→AD→ADX ladder. Side and joint fits prevent order from assigning shared information to one modality. Refit every rung on identical rows and folds.

For outcome Y, define `Delta_D,Y=[E(A1,Y)-E(AD,Y)]/E(A1,Y)`, `Delta_X,Y=[E(A1,Y)-E(AX-side,Y)]/E(A1,Y)`, and `Delta_joint,Y=[E(A1,Y)-E(ADX,Y)]/E(A1,Y)`, where E is family-balanced held-cell MAE. ## Baseline and scientifically substantive alternative

**Simple physical-history baseline.** Extrapolate the observed `g_pre`: predict A_near=A_late=A_shape=0 and predict future Q by `Q[c-1]-h*g_pre`. This is the persistence null and needs no fitting.

**Primary auditable learned model.** Standardize continuous inputs on outer-training cells only. Fit weighted ridge separately to A_near, A_late, and A_shape; tune alpha in {0.01, 0.1, 1, 10, 100} and cubic age-spline df in {3, 5, 7} by inner leave-one-training-cell-out family-balanced cell MAE. Fit full and the parent's exact two-frequency sparse representations (17.79613 and 2.16054 Hz).

**Functional nonlinear alternative.** On the same origins, inputs, landmarks, and folds, predict the entire 20-vector `T_h=Q[c+h]-Q[c-1]`, h=0,...,19. Represent each training trajectory in a fixed six-degree-of-freedom cubic B-spline basis over h; fit the coefficients from training outcomes only. As in the parent, fit weighted PCA separately to V, dI, S_X, P_X, and U_X (smallest 99%-variance rank capped by tuned {10,20}), then an RBF Nystroem map plus multi-output ridge. Tune gamma in {0.5,1,2} times inverse median squared training distance, landmarks in {128,256} capped by training rows, ridge alpha on the same grid, fixed seed 20260923, and basis roughness penalty in {0, 0.1, 1, 10}. Derive predicted A_near, A_late, and A_shape from the reconstructed trajectory and observed g_pre.

The functional model can reveal a coordinated bend or persistent rate shift that independent scalar fits discard; evaluate integrated 20-step MAE and derived rate-change errors. It is not evidence of mechanism. A learned-only positive result is exploratory; disagreement with primary ridge makes attribution inconclusive. A neural sequence model is deferred because ten independent specimens cannot support its flexibility. Equivalent-circuit fitting is deferred because topology and identifiability are unvalidated and would not make fitted parameters microscopic truth. Revisit either with more independent cells or validated circuit evidence.

Estimated full workload is 16 CPUs, 64 GiB RAM, zero GPUs, and <=7 hours. The audit completed in 15.2 s. The full nested-fit estimate is unmeasured; CPU is selected because there are ten specimens and compact tabular/spline fits, not because GPU methods are prohibited.

## Splits, fitting weights, uncertainty, and controls

Primary evaluation is ten outer leave-one-confirmatory-cell-out folds. The held cell may supply only prediction-time measurements available by the stated landmark, including its cycles 1–5 anchors and values through c-1. It supplies no outcomes, scaling, PCA, spline-target basis fitting, Nystroem landmarks, hyperparameters, residual calibration, or feature selection. Inner validation is leave-one-training-cell-out. Random row, cycle, spectrum, frequency, origin, or window splits are prohibited.

Training origin weights are `1/(F*n_f*n_i)`, with F represented temperature families, n_f training cells in the origin's family, and n_i eligible origins for that cell; renormalize to training-row count. Evaluation averages origins within cell, cells equally within family, then the three families equally. Report every origin and cell, family, age third, target MAE/RMSE/bias, endpoint MAE, functional trajectory MAE, and 90% interval coverage/width/score. Overlapping origins remain within specimen and never inflate inferential n.

Construct prediction intervals from inner held-cell residuals using the parent's cell-reduced finite-sample rule. Use 10,000 fixed-seed paired bootstraps resampling cells within family and all 2^10 cell-level sign-flip assignments. Construct one simultaneous 95% max-deviation band over eleven claim-gating ridge contrasts: D-side, X-side, and joint additions for A_near, A_late, and A_shape (nine), plus joint L10 and L20 endpoint contrasts (two).

Mandatory sensitivities:

1. repeat A_near on the 1,974-origin H20 common set; common support is c=10–15 for all ten cells;
2. replace Theil-Sen slopes with OLS slopes and with median adjacent-cycle loss; disagreement changes the result to definition-sensitive;
3. repeat with Q/Q0 and ox/red=1 capacity extraction;
4. use cycle-1 and cycles-1:3 anchors; replace U blocks by zero, one-cycle lags, and five-cycle pre-origin slopes;
5. add available absolute experiment time and I/V/IX sweep timing only at the correct landmark;
6. remove each spectrum's highest-frequency complex translation, use highest-frequency-only, and compare direct I/V/IX with difference coordinates;
7. permute whole U trajectories among cells within temperature family on common-support windows, never origins independently;
8. hash spectra and reject train/test exact duplicates;
9. run family holdout and age-forward cutoffs tau={50,100,150};
10. report outcome availability and baseline covariates for censored tail origins; never impute a future capacity.

The two disputed identity maps remain non-confirmatory sensitivity outputs only. The three-cell all-nine-state branch is not revisited.

## Decision rules and interpretation

The 10% relevance margin and 5% no-value margin are design choices, not literature facts.

- **Persistent rate-change information:** support for a named block (D, X, or joint) requires >=10% MAE reduction for A_near on H10 and A_late on H20, simultaneous lower bounds >0, positive direction for A_near on the H20 common set, improvement in at least two temperature families with none worse than -10%, acceptable 0.80–1.00 coverage, and no reversal under OLS/normalized-capacity sensitivities.
- **Within-future acceleration information:** support requires >=10% MAE reduction for A_shape on H20, simultaneous lower bound >0, improvement in at least two families with none worse than -10%, acceptable coverage, and no reversal under OLS and functional-trajectory analyses.
- **Clock-specific or IX-specific attribution:** use the corresponding side contrast. A joint-only result supports combined current-acquisition information but cannot assign modality. Sequential AD→ADX is descriptive only when side blocks overlap.
- **Endpoint-only information:** if the parent L10/L20 joint contrast passes its original gate but every trajectory-shape contrast has simultaneous upper bound <=5%, conclude that the observed gain does not extend to persistent rate-change or acceleration under these definitions.
- **No useful current trajectory information:** support only if all joint trajectory contrast upper bounds are <=5%, coverage is acceptable, and no family has >10% gain.
- **Adverse:** report a block as harmful when its relevant simultaneous upper bounds are <=0 with no common-support reversal.
- **Falsification:** the global “current updates anticipate persistent or accelerating fade” hypothesis is falsified as posed when the joint upper bounds are <10% for both persistent components and A_shape. It is not falsified merely by a negative mean acceleration; prediction includes both signs.
- **Inconclusive:** intervals crossing zero or a relevance margin, family conflict, H10/H20 conflict, poor calibration, identity dependence, target-definition reversal, side/joint disagreement, simple/functional disagreement, or too few effective specimens.

Support means conditional predictive information about measured-capacity trajectory shape in this archive. It does not mean the cohort is generally accelerating, D is a discharge duration, IX-V identifies a mechanism, or acquisition has positive net utility. Preserve adverse and null results.

## Deliverable, readiness, and verification boundary

The scientific deliverable is newly fitted held-cell predictions at LV, LD, and LX for A_near, A_late, and A_shape; reconstructed 20-cycle trajectories from the functional alternative; the matched endpoint comparator; specimen/family-balanced uncertainty; and a machine-readable conclusion mapping each claim to outputs. Completion requires:

- immutable source/catalog/software/seed manifests and all member/table bindings;
- parser, field-width, header, sign, unit, integer-cycle, grid-hash, chronology, identity, and exclusion tests;
- Q and acquisition-clock ledgers and proof of all 30 exact cycles c-10 through c+19 for every H20 origin;
- analytic tables with every capacity index, target component, censoring flag, landmark mask, S/P/U provenance, and reconstruction check;
- outer/inner split, weight, tuning, transform, PCA, Nystroem, spline-basis, calibration, thread, and seed manifests;
- all held-cell predictions and every control, bootstrap/sign-flip draw, simultaneous band, adverse result, executable code, and `conclusion.json`.

Readiness must reproduce source hashes, exact members and layouts, the 60-bin grid, 2,786 triples, 2,054/1,974 risks, all per-cell ranges above, chronology, anchor/lag completeness, imports, held-cell isolation, and a two-cell end-to-end fit. Readiness is packaging and bounded computation, not a solved scientific result.

An automatic verifier can recompute parsing, joins, Q extraction, contiguity, Theil-Sen targets, splits, transforms, predictions, metrics, uncertainty, decision thresholds, and claim/output mappings. It must accept correctly computed supportive, adverse, endpoint-only, or inconclusive outcomes, and reject leakage from Q[c] or later, row-wise splitting, treating origins as specimens, unsupported modality attribution, calling D discharge duration, or attaching knee/mechanistic claims to correct calculations.

Automatic verification cannot establish the physical identity of 25C02/03, validate unresolved headerless semantics, determine operations inside D, choose a practically meaningful rate-change margin, establish a safety-relevant knee, value acquisition cost, infer causality or microscopic degradation, or generalize beyond these coin cells. Those require data-owner/electrochemical review, protocol logs, measurement-resolution evidence, independent compatible specimens, controlled intervention, and/or another study.

## Selection record

The fixed-endpoint-only evolution is rejected as insufficient: robust future slope is too correlated with endpoint loss to be the substantive advance. The selected design instead tests matched past/near/late rate changes and a late-minus-near shape outcome that the endpoint cannot determine. It retains the parent's ten-cell policy, exact bindings, chronology, S/P/U attribution, matched ridge and nonlinear alternatives, family-balanced specimen inference, and non-mechanistic boundary.

Revisit a simple robust-rate-only study if measurement-resolution evidence shows endpoint capacity is unusually noisy but trajectory shape is not estimable. Revisit neural sequence models with materially more independent cells; circuit models with validated topology; knee/event classification with a prevalidated threshold and enough events; and operational stopping only with time, energy, interruption, safety, and utility data. Population, temporal boundaries, outcomes, estimands, analysis, and falsification criteria are frozen for compilation; changing them requires a Lead-approved scientific child.

# Proposal: row-permutation-invariant distributional transport of Oxford longitudinal impedance identity

## Question, hypothesis, and substantive advance

For the 11 Oxford NCR18650BD specimens with paired beginning-of-life (BoL) and ordinal middle-of-life (MoL) real-impedance measurements at nominal 20%, 50%, and 80% SOC, does the **unordered empirical distribution** of the 35 supplied `ReZ_Ohm` values retain specimen-specific longitudinal information after documented protocol is removed?

This is a substantive child of `candidate-a2659fcff9a1240ac2eb5189`. The parent separates scale-free directional persistence from raw-ohm amplitude, but both tracks first impose smoothness on source `point_index` and compare BoL and MoL at equal stored indices. The admitted data contain no row-level frequency field, and the README does not establish row order, spacing, or cross-table row correspondence. The parent's scientific result is therefore conditional on an unavailable semantic fact: that equal stored rows represent comparable locations on a common frequency grid. Orthogonal-basis and global-scale invariance do not repair that dependence.

This child changes the estimand rather than adding a prose caveat. Each SOC table becomes an equally weighted empirical measure of its 35 observed real-impedance values. Sorting supplies its canonical empirical quantile function; no source-row identity is retained or joined. Three-SOC contrasts of those quantile functions ask whether a cell's *distribution of observed real impedance across the documented acquisition* has a longitudinal fingerprint. The question is narrower than frequency-resolved curve identity but identifiable from the admitted numeric values.

The primary hypothesis is **material scale-free distributional identity**: after fold-local protocol adjustment and normalization, scalar persistence S or a two-parameter conformal transport R reduces held-specimen MoL directional loss by at least 10% versus protocol-only P, and the selected gain is unusual among all 432 within-protocol whole-BoL-bundle relinkings.

A gated secondary hypothesis is **coherent redistribution of SOC distributional contrasts**: R improves at least 10% over S and estimates a stable nonzero rotation between prespecified linear-SOC and curvature-SOC axes.

A separately adjudicated companion hypothesis is **material full-scale distributional identity in ohms**: fixed unit transport U or a learned scalar A reduces held-specimen equal-quantile MoL loss by at least 10% versus its own protocol-only P. Neither track may rescue the other.

## What is supported, what remains unresolved

The inspected Oxford README supports 12 NCR18650BD 3 Ah NCA/graphite cells, a 24 degC chamber setpoint, four schedule/rate groups, and EIS at supplied BoL and MoL checkpoints and 20%, 50%, and 80% SOC. It reports 100 mA peak-to-peak excitation from 5 kHz to 10 mHz at six points per decade. The admitted EIS ZIP has complete paired coverage for 11 of the Group 1–4 specimens.

A new registered native export, job `job-b345c63ec1b5da2a700f95f2`, requested exactly 66 containers and completed in 30.05 s. It produced 74 table objects, including 66 canonical expected-name tables, each with 35 rows and columns exactly `ReZ_Ohm,N_A`; all selected `ReZ_Ohm` values are finite and duplicate internal objects are equal. Native conversion and availability are established. Frequency vectors, the meaning/unit of `N_A`, acquisition order, repeatability, and cross-table row correspondence are not.

A bounded, archive-informed screen formed the proposed unordered representation and used final-like 11-fold nuisance removal with fixed ridge alpha 1. On the full 35 empirical ranks, S gained 11.29% and R 8.49% over directional P; the max-selected within-protocol relinking tail fraction was 2/432 = 0.00463, but S improved only 8/11 held cells. The minimum held residual-to-unadjusted norm ratio was 0.0889. In the raw-ohm companion, U gained -5848% and A gained 6.37%; A improved 8/11 cells, while its max-selected relinking tail fraction was also 2/432. Removing one extreme at each tail changed S/A gains to 16.90%/8.73%; removing three changed them to 20.35%/11.39%. An explicit independent source-row shuffle changed the sorted representation by exactly 0 ohm.

These results justify the estimand and expose tail-policy and breadth questions. They do not answer either hypothesis: the amplitude screen did not perform nested tuning, and neither track included registered resampling, deletion, all sensitivities, or independent confirmation. The strongest current claim is computational feasibility and exact source-row-permutation invariance. The unresolved claims are material, specimen-broad distributional linkage and, conditionally, coherent SOC-plane redistribution.

## Population and temporal boundary

Use exactly these independent specimens:

- Group 1, C/2, one cycling day plus five calendar days: `G1_C15,G1_C20`;
- Group 2, C/4, short blocks: `G2_C3,G2_C4,G2_C8`;
- Group 3, C/2, two cycling days plus ten calendar days: `G3_C10,G3_C11,G3_C14`;
- Group 4, C/4, long blocks: `G4_C12,G4_C18,G4_C19`.

Exclude `G1_C9` because no admitted paired MoL member exists. Exclude Groups 5–10 because they are outside the README-described four-group longitudinal experiment and do not have the required paired coverage in this archive.

The acquisition clock is only `stage in {BoL,MoL}`, with BoL preceding MoL. There is no admitted timestamp, elapsed duration, cycle count, throughput, capacity, common-health threshold, or acquisition sequence that makes MoL a shared physical-age boundary. Outcomes concern absolute ordinal-MoL distributions, not rates of change. Cells are independent units; SOCs and empirical quantile ranks are repeated coordinates.

## Exact read-only binding

Use:

- ZIP `[private path]`, SHA-256 `64d1fc94dcd3b2403d3f84b88666781a4f6153068e2ef4311d7cde97106a6d27`, runtime `/data/e05ee114fa-oxford-eis.zip`;
- README `[private path]`, SHA-256 `59489534eaa5cddd2cef74b057855d2074bbef802d3aa12db6e082f9886dc59c`, runtime `/data/4a245ba1d6-oxford-readme.txt`;
- catalog `[private path]`, SHA-256 `02afcb6c55ac8d6d1801f4d4ed51adaa45743e5a3461f9c468a1ecf85cf4d8b5`, runtime `/data/a90f68c3f0-catalog-v06.json`.

For each listed specimen, `stage in {BoL,MoL}`, and `SOC in {20,50,80}`, read exactly:

`EIS/{stage}/Group{group}_{stage}_Cell{cell}_SOC{SOC}.mat`

and select only internal table:

`Group{group}_{stage}_Cell{cell}_SOC{SOC}`.

Require exact container-to-internal-name agreement, 35 rows, columns exactly `ReZ_Ohm,N_A`, and finite numeric `ReZ_Ohm`. Preserve `N_A` as `channel2_raw` for audit only; do not use it scientifically.

The three G2_C3 MoL containers each expose all three G2_C3 SOC variables; G3_C11 MoL SOC20 also exposes SOC50 and SOC80. Select the internal variable matching the container stem. Require duplicate copies to be exactly equal; disagreement fails readiness.

Normalize source rows to:

`group,cell_id,specimen_key,stage,SOC_label_pct,source_row_index,ReZ_Ohm,channel2_raw,cycling_rate_C,cycling_block_days,calendar_block_days,periodicity_class`.

Require 66 canonical tables, 2,310 stage rows, 11 specimens, two stages, three SOC tables per specimen-stage, and 35 values per table. The table key is `(group,cell_id,stage,SOC_label_pct)`. **Do not join BoL and MoL on `source_row_index`.** After tablewise sorting, derive `quantile_rank=1..35`; transformed BoL and MoL arrays may be compared on `(group,cell_id,SOC_label_pct,quantile_rank)` only as empirical-quantile coordinates, not as matched acquisitions or frequencies.

SOC is supplied nominal metadata, not independently validated physical SOC, coulomb-counted SOC, or a BMS estimate. Current sign, charge return, capacity normalization, equilibration, measurement order, repeatability, exact frequency support, and row weighting by log-frequency interval are unavailable.

## Frozen row-permutation-invariant representation

For each specimen (c), stage (t), and SOC (s), define the empirical measure

`μ_cts = (1/35) Σ_j δ[ReZ_Ohm_ctsj]`.

Let `q_cts,k` be the kth order statistic and `p_k=(k-0.5)/35`. For each specimen-stage form the 3-by-35 matrix `Q_ct` in SOC order 20, 50, 80 and increasing empirical quantile rank. Sorting is performed independently within every table. It is not an estimate of frequency order.

Use fixed orthonormal SOC contrasts:

- `h_L=(-1,0,1)/sqrt(2)`;
- `h_Q=(1,-2,1)/sqrt(6)`;
- `H=[h_L,h_Q]`.

Define the 2-by-35 distributional-contrast profile:

`Z_ct = H' Q_ct`.

The equal-rank squared distance between two original SOC empirical quantile functions is the one-dimensional equal-mass empirical Wasserstein-2 distance. The loss on `Z` is the corresponding equal-quantile Euclidean geometry after projecting away the three-SOC common quantile profile. It is not a frequency-domain distance and does not localize where a difference occurs.

This representation has exact, testable properties:

- arbitrary independent permutations of the 35 source rows in every table leave `Q`, `Z`, all predictions, and all losses unchanged;
- adding the same 35-point quantile profile to all three SOCs of a specimen-stage leaves `Z` unchanged;
- orthogonal re-expression of the two SOC-contrast axes leaves scalar/Frobenius predictions and losses unchanged when R is transformed covariantly;
- multiplying all BoL and/or all MoL values by independent positive constants scales raw-ohm quantities equivariantly and leaves the directional track unchanged after normalization.

It is not invariant to unknown frequency coverage, unequal row inclusion probabilities, SOC-specific offsets, nonlinear calibration, or changes in the set of sampled frequencies. These remain scientific limits.

## Directional experiment: P, S, and informative R

Use 11 leave-one-specimen-out outer folds. Code `r=+1/-1` for C/2/C/4, `p=+1/-1` for short/long blocks, and `rp`. In each outer fit, standardize nonconstant nuisance columns on training specimens. Separately fit multi-output ridge models with unpenalized intercept and fixed `alpha_P=1` from `[r,p,rp]` to vectorized BoL and MoL `Z`. These are protocol adjustments, not causal protocol effects.

Let `x_i` and `y_i` be BoL and MoL residual profiles from the training-fitted nuisance models. Normalize `xhat_i=x_i/||x_i||_F` and `yhat_i=y_i/||y_i||_F`. Held MoL enters only its outcome and loss.

A fold is unstable if any required training or held residual norm is at most 1% of the corresponding fitting-set median unadjusted `||Z||_F`. Any primary-fold failure makes directional classification inconclusive. Repeat 0.5% and 2% as sensitivities.

Fit competitors on training specimens with equal total weight per documented group:

- **P, protocol-only baseline:** predict zero residual direction; loss is exactly 1.
- **S, simple linked persistence:** predict `b*xhat`; estimate one unrestricted global `b`. `b=0` nests P.
- **R, informative conformal transport:** predict `b*xhat+c*J*xhat`, where `J=[[0,-1],[1,0]]` acts on the linear/curvature SOC rows. Report `a=sqrt(b^2+c^2)` and `theta=atan2(c,b)`.

R can reveal a coherent redistribution between monotonic and curved SOC dependence that S necessarily loses, while adding only one global coefficient. Require weighted design rank 2, condition number at most `1e8`, and at least six independent within-protocol specimen contrasts in every outer fit. R is otherwise scientifically unidentifiable and its claim inconclusive.

For model `m` and held cell `i` use `L_mi=||yhat_i-pred_mi||_F^2`, `E_m=mean_i L_mi`, `G_S=1-E_S/E_P`, `G_R=1-E_R/E_P`, and `D_RS=1-E_R/E_S`. Select `W_D` by larger observed gain, S on a tie. Report all held losses, predictions, norms, group gains, coefficients, and reconstructed centered three-SOC quantile profiles `H Zhat`.

## Raw-ohm distributional companion: P, U, and A

Use the same raw `X_i=Z_i,BoL` and `Y_i=Z_i,MoL`, folds, protocol codes, and 70 equal-quantile coordinates.

- **P, protocol baseline:** `Y=D(r,p,rp)+e`.
- **U, unit linked transport:** `Y=X+D(r,p,rp)+e`.
- **A, learned scalar transport:** `Y=gamma X+D(r,p,rp)+e`.

For each fitting set estimate A only from within-group specimen deviations:

`gamma = [Σ_g Σ_i< X_i-Xbar_g, Y_i-Ybar_g >_F] / [Σ_g Σ_i ||X_i-Xbar_g||_F^2]`.

Require a finite denominator above `1e-12 Ohm^2`. After fixing `gamma` to 0, 1, or the fitted value, fit the protocol residual by multi-output ridge. Tune `alpha in {1e-4,1e-3,...,1e4}` using inner leave-one-specimen-out mean raw-ohm equal-quantile MSE; ties choose the larger alpha. Recompute standardization, zero-variance column removal, gamma, and coefficients in every inner, outer, relinked, and deletion fit. No held MoL data enter tuning or fitting.

Use `L_mi=(1/70)||Y_i-Yhat_mi||_F^2 Ohm^2`; report `sqrt(E_m)` in ohms, `G_U=1-E_U/E_P`, `G_A=1-E_A/E_P`, and `G_AU=1-E_A/E_U`. Select `W_A` by larger gain, U on a tie. Also report loss/gain for each linear/curvature axis and for each row of the centered three-SOC reconstruction `H Z`.

This track tests absolute magnitude of cross-SOC empirical-distribution contrasts. It does not test frequency-resolved impedance magnitude or the SOC-common level removed by H.

## Relinking, uncertainty, deletion, and sensitivities

For each track enumerate all `2!3!3!3!=432` allocations, identity included. Within each group, move a donor's complete BoL bundle—three SOC tables and all 35 values per table—to a recipient with fixed protocol and MoL. Rerun sorting, nuisance fits, outer fits, and all nested tuning. P must remain invariant.

For directional identity use `T_id=max(G_S,G_R)` and `p_id=#{T_id,a>=T_id,obs}/432`. For rotation use `T_rot=D_RS` and its upper-tail fraction, tested only after identity support. For amplitude use `T_amp=max(G_U,G_A)` and `p_amp=#{T_amp,a>=T_amp,obs}/432`. These are exact conditional no-linkage relinking fractions under unverified within-group exchangeability, not treatment-randomization or population p-values.

With `numpy.random.Generator(PCG64(20260923))`, draw 10,000 group-stratified specimen resamples of sizes 2/3/3/3. Apply common multiplicities to frozen outer-loss vectors and report percentile intervals for all gains and group gains. Separately refit full-data S/R/A parameters in every resample and report coefficient intervals/failures. These are observed-cell weighting-stability summaries, not population confidence intervals.

Delete each specimen and rerun the complete observed outer pipeline, including inner amplitude tuning. Classification uses fixed selected winners and observed-linkage deletion gains. Deleted-set relinking fractions are diagnostic rather than required.

Frozen representation and modeling sensitivities are:

1. trim the lowest and highest one order statistic per table (33 ranks);
2. trim the lowest and highest three (29 ranks);
3. replace 35 ranks with seven prespecified consecutive five-rank means;
4. nuisance ridge `alpha_P in {0.1,10}`;
5. additive nuisance `[r,p]`;
6. equal-cell rather than equal-group transport fitting;
7. amplitude alpha grid extended once to `1e-5,...,1e5`;
8. residual gates 0.5% and 2%;
9. exact independent source-row shuffles, including at least 1,000 seeded shuffles, which must reproduce every primary value to numerical tolerance;
10. independent positive BoL/MoL scale multipliers in `{0.1,10}`.

The parent's source-index spline quotient is retained only as a non-rescuing comparator. Agreement would show convergence of two estimands; disagreement would show dependence on unavailable row semantics. It cannot upgrade or rescue the permutation-invariant primary.

## Frozen outcome rules

The 10% margin is a dataset-scale materiality threshold, not validated engineering utility. Report descriptive 5% and 20% thresholds without changing classification.

**Scale-free distributional identity is supportive** only if:

- `max(G_S,G_R)>=0.10` and `p_id<=0.05`;
- the fixed-`W_D` 95% conditional-stability lower bound is above zero;
- `W_D` beats P in at least 9/11 held cells;
- every deletion has positive fixed-`W_D` gain and at least 9/11 deletion gains are at least 0.10;
- no protocol-group gain is at or below -0.10;
- all residual-norm and identifiability gates pass;
- both trimming analyses and the seven-bin, nuisance, weighting, row-shuffle, and scale checks preserve a fixed-`W_D` gain of at least 0.10 without supportive/adverse reversal.

The warranted claim is only that correctly linked BoL cross-SOC empirical `ReZ_Ohm` distributional direction predicts ordinal-MoL within-protocol residual direction in these cells, independent of source-row ordering and global positive stage scale.

**Coherent SOC redistribution** additionally requires R=`W_D`, `D_RS>=0.10`, `p_rot<=0.05`, positive stability lower bound, R beating S in at least 9/11 folds and every deletion aggregate, and the interval for c excluding zero with one sign across deletions. Theta remains a distributional electrical descriptor, not a mechanism.

Directional status is **adverse for the 10% margin** only if selected gain is below 0.10, its stability upper bound is below 0.10, `p_id>0.05`, the winner beats P in at most 7/11 cells, no group has stable multiplicity-compatible 0.10 gain, norm/identifiability gates pass, and no registered permutation-invariant sensitivity is supportive. All other valid patterns are **inconclusive**, including exactly 8/11 improved cells, tail-policy dependence, margin-spanning stability, relinking/stability disagreement, deletion dependence, group opposition, or apparent rotation without primary identity.

**Full-scale distributional identity is supportive** only if:

- `max(G_U,G_A)>=0.10` and `p_amp<=0.05`;
- fixed-`W_A` stability lower bound is above zero;
- `W_A` beats P in at least 9/11 held cells;
- every deletion gain is positive and at least 9/11 are at least 0.10;
- every reconstructed SOC-row gain is positive and none is at or below -0.10;
- trimming, seven-bin, extended-alpha, weighting, row-shuffle, and basis checks preserve the winner, positive gain, and no adverse SOC row; all except exact row shuffling retain the 0.10 margin.

A stronger scalar-transport label requires A=`W_A`, `G_AU>=0.10`, A beating U in at least 9/11 cells and every deletion aggregate, and gamma's refit interval excluding both 0 and 1. Attenuation requires that interval and every deletion gamma lie in (0,1); amplification requires all exceed 1; sign reversal requires all be below 0.

Amplitude status is **adverse for the 10% margin** only if selected gain is below 0.10, its stability upper bound is below 0.10, `p_amp>0.05`, the winner beats P in at most 7/11 cells, no projected SOC row has stable 0.10 gain, and no registered permutation-invariant sensitivity is supportive. Every other valid result is **inconclusive**.

Report the ordered pair `(directional status, amplitude status)`. Neither status changes the other. A supportive directional/adverse amplitude result means relative distributional geometry persists without material full-scale prediction. Adverse directional/supportive amplitude means only an amplitude-sensitive distributional association is identified. Adversity in both rejects both registered margin-qualified distributional fingerprints. Any inconclusive component retains its exact failed gate.

An adverse unordered result does **not** reject a frequency-localized fingerprint: sorting deliberately discards frequency identity. A supportive result does **not** prove the source rows share a frequency grid.

## Alternatives considered and selection record

P is the simple no-linkage baseline. S is the minimal one-parameter linked model. R is the scientifically informative learned alternative: it can reveal coherent conversion between linear and curved SOC distributional contrasts that S loses, while remaining estimable with six within-group specimen contrasts per outer fit.

The full 35-rank empirical quantile profile is selected over mean/variance/quantile summaries because it preserves all admitted real-value distribution information and has a canonical one-dimensional optimal-transport geometry. Seven five-rank means are retained as a lower-resolution sensitivity: they reduce tail and rank granularity but lose within-bin distributional shape. Tail trimming directly adjudicates the observed sensitivity to extremes.

The source-index spline estimator is deferred from primary status because its required row-frequency/order correspondence is unavailable, not because spline models are intrinsically unsuitable. Equivalent-circuit, DRT, and frequency-localized models remain scientifically unavailable until authoritative frequency and complex-impedance semantics are acquired. A full 70-by-70 map, kernel, or neural encoder could exploit nonlinear distributional patterns but adds no separately identifiable scientific claim with 11 cells; revisit it with a larger external cohort or stable residual structure. GPU use is not prohibited, but gives no expected advantage for the selected small linear models.

## Deliverable, resources, and verification

Completion requires newly fitting:

- all 11 directional P/S/R outer folds and raw-ohm P/U/A nested folds;
- both 432-allocation max-selected relinking experiments and the gated rotation statistic;
- 10,000 group-stratified loss resamples and coefficient refits;
- 11 specimen deletions;
- every registered representation, nuisance, weighting, tuning, scale, and exact row-shuffle check;
- the non-rescuing source-index comparator;
- a deterministic two-axis conclusion trace tied to computed fields.

Required outputs are:

- source: `source_audit.json`, `member_manifest.csv`, `duplicate_audit.json`, `normalized_eis.parquet`;
- representation: `empirical_quantiles.parquet`, `distributional_contrasts.parquet`, `permutation_invariance_audit.json`;
- directional: `directional_outer_predictions.parquet`, `directional_outer_losses.csv`, `directional_fits.csv`, `directional_relinkings.parquet`, `directional_stability.parquet`, `directional_coefficients.parquet`;
- amplitude: `amplitude_outer_predictions.parquet`, `amplitude_outer_losses.csv`, `amplitude_scalar_fits.csv`, `amplitude_tuning.parquet`, `amplitude_relinkings.parquet`, `amplitude_stability.parquet`;
- robustness: `deletion_metrics.csv`, `sensitivity_metrics.csv`, `source_index_comparator.json`;
- synthesis: `metrics.json` and `conclusion.json` with sentence-to-field provenance.

Use 8 CPUs, 32 GiB RAM, zero GPUs, deterministic BLAS/thread settings, and allocation-level parallelism. Native export measured 30.05 s; the Python bounded screen, including both 432-allocation tracks, measured 6.7 s. The complete nested, deletion, resampling, and sensitivity experiment is estimated at 45–120 CPU minutes and fits the 28,800-second solver envelope. Checkpoint every 36 allocations. Discovery measurements do not substitute for solver completion.

The verifier can check source hashes, exact member/internal-variable selection, duplicate equality, counts, independent tablewise sorting, no source-row join, SOC contrasts, permutation/scale invariance, specimen splits, nuisance fits, P/S/R and P/U/A calculations, nested tuning, all 432 allocations, resamples, deletions, sensitivities, breadth gates, and deterministic conclusions. It must accept supportive, adverse, or inconclusive results when warranted and reject correct computation paired with frequency, mechanism, fixture, causal, population, or deployment claims.

Scientific adjudication remains necessary for equal weighting of the 35 acquired values, whether the reported frequency coverage was identical across tables, within-group exchangeability, the importance of a 10% gain, SOC accuracy/equilibration, and MoL comparability. Stronger frequency-resolved, mechanistic, causal, or transferable conclusions require authoritative per-row frequency and complex-impedance fields, acquisition order and repeat spectra, fixture/contact controls, common-horizon capacity/throughput records, assignment provenance, expert review, and an independent prospective cohort.

## Inspected provenance

Inspected on 2026-09-23: `datasets/README.md`; Oxford dataset guide and metadata; the full admitted Oxford README; binding template and catalog provenance; the assigned parent and the directional, amplitude, and separability context candidates; research-ambition and method/compute guidance; the registered 66-container native export; and the bounded row-invariant screen. # Proposal: Can condition-matched peers act as strictly earlier sentinels of a specimen's next level-free room-EIS shape?

## Unresolved question and scientific advance

The selected parent establishes a feasible retrospective question: within 44 opaque KIT conditions, triplicate specimens may share nonlinear evolution in frequency- and SOC-resolved complex room-EIS geometry after per-SOC level and positive scale are removed. Its primary reconstruction, however, allows contemporaneous peer information through the same elapsed-day bin. It therefore cannot answer whether a peer measurement already complete at a real decision cutoff improves a target specimen's next measurement.

The strongest claim supported by evidence is currently only readiness. Luh and Blank's inspected full public XML (Scientific Data 2024, DOI `10.1038/s41597-024-03831-x`; PMCID `PMC11405776`; frozen source `5c3de8fa937542c503c49aa0d7832107792c4f28fc8e9ad7cdadfe7403cbeabd`, SHA-256 `e55315f55e0b3ac2ce10deb1bcbe58a9babcac5e00a252ac058d27ee975ea115`) supports a 228-cell NMC/C-SiO ageing study over 76 conditions with check-up impedance measurements. The configured ZIP and catalog establish the exact selected EIS records below. The new outcome-free audit reproduces the parent's cohort, verifies source timing fields, and enumerates forecast support; it checks only required-coordinate finiteness and timing; it does not summarize shape values, fit a forecast, or estimate peer value.

The unresolved hypothesis is:

**H-sentinel:** On strict next-measurement forecasts in previously unseen KIT conditions, assimilating only fully completed, condition-matched peer shapes available before each target cutoff reduces condition-balanced original-coordinate RMSE by at least 10% relative to a strong own-history dynamic model, reduces RMSE by at least 5% relative to an exact peer-timing/metadata shadow without peer impedance, and retains at least a 5% gain in the prespecified zero-same-bin-peer stratum.

This is a substantive advance over the parent. Support would show that replicate measurements can provide temporally leading information about a shared level-free spectral-shape process, motivating staggered sentinel designs in replicated ageing experiments. Failure would distinguish retrospective shared geometry from prospective usefulness. Neither outcome establishes capacity prognosis, safety value, protocol causality, or a degradation mechanism.

## Exact read-only binding

- Source ZIP: `[private path]`; runtime `/data/75850054cd-kit-corrected-eis.zip`; 17,307,136 bytes; SHA-256 `21f7942224c99bbcadb6c1ba3d229d5591a034c2d8785bfaf659fc8281078d34`.

Evaluate persistence of the last target shape and damped local-velocity extrapolation from its last two completed shapes. These require no peer data and expose whether fitted models beat trivial smoothness.

### B-own: strong own-history baseline

Use an irregular-time multivariate local-linear-trend state-space model for the K fold-defined shape scores. It contains a training-condition-estimated smooth elapsed-day mean, specimen intercept/slope, K-dimensional nonlinear specimen state, and regularized history-only nuisance effects for observed room temperature, OCV, calendar week, `timestamp_origin`, duplicate status and acquisition-order rank. `cyc_charged` is audited as constant 1 and is not informative. At each held-condition cutoff, filter only the target specimen's completed visits. No peer identity, timing, metadata or shape is available to B-own.

This is a strong baseline: it learns nonlinear marginal dynamics and measurement noise from other conditions while adapting online to the target's own history.

### M-peer: timing/metadata shadow

Use the same B-own state and target, plus only the admissible peers' completion lags, elapsed anchors, temperature, OCV, `timestamp_origin`, duplicate indicators, peer counts and same-bin availability class. It receives no peer impedance, PCA score, removed level or scale. This control asks whether schedule/acquisition order rather than peer spectral shape explains any apparent gain.

### H-peer: shared dynamic sentinel alternative

Use the identical fold-local representation, own-history mean/nuisance equation, observation model, total score-wise process intensity, target times and optimizer as B-own. H-peer contains M-peer exactly: every admissible peer timing/metadata field enters through the same feature map and penalty grid, and the only additional information block is the admissible peer's level-free shape. Decompose each score process into condition-shared `G_ck(t)` and specimen-specific `U_crk(t)` local-linear states with
`q_shared,k=rho*q_k` and `q_individual,k=(1-rho)*q_k`, `rho in [0,1]`.
Thus the dynamic alternative adds cross-specimen shape information without adding marginal roughness. With the peer-shape block disabled H-peer reduces exactly to M-peer; with both peer metadata and shape blocks disabled, its own-history dynamic core reduces to B-own. Record this containment in `model_spec.json`.

At each cutoff H-peer filters the target's history and every fully completed peer shape strictly before the cutoff, carrying exact source provenance and availability masks. The learned shared state can reveal an early condition-level innovation localized by PCA loading to frequency, complex channel and SOC; B-own loses that information because it observes only the target. Loadings and latent paths are descriptive, not mechanistic.

Fit Student-t and Gaussian observation versions. Profile `rho`, use multiple optimizer starts and record boundary solutions. A fixed six-knot cubic spline over log-frequency per channel/SOC with the same independent/shared dynamic decomposition is the representation sensitivity if fold PCA subspace congruence is below 0.85.

## Splits, metrics and uncertainty

Use leave-one-condition-out outer evaluation: every specimen, visit and target from one condition is held out together. Fit coordinate preprocessing, PCA, nuisance terms, process/observation covariance, `rho`, penalties and any hyperparameter using only the other 43 conditions, with inner condition-grouped validation. For a held condition, issue each forecast sequentially using only records available at that cutoff. Predictions from later cutoffs cannot revise earlier predictions.

All P0, B-own, M-peer and H-peer models use the same 1,804 target rows, future anchor, fold, K, weighting and outcome. Define condition-balanced
`MSE_m=(1/44) sum_c (1/3) sum_r (1/n_cr) sum_t ||W_hat_m-W||^2/180`
and `RMSE_m=sqrt(MSE_m)`. Primary contrasts are
`G_total=1-RMSE_H-peer/RMSE_B-own`,
`G_shape=1-RMSE_H-peer/RMSE_M-peer`, and
`G_zero`, the H-peer versus B-own gain on the 601 zero-same-bin-peer examples.

Report original-coordinate RMSE, MAE, cosine distance, score RMSE, log predictive density, 50%/90% coverage, interval width, condition effects, same-bin class, target replicate, horizon, age and long-gap strata. Every example receives one out-of-fold prediction.

Use paired whole-condition resampling with 10,000 deterministic bootstrap draws for loss contrasts and simultaneous one-sided 95% max-root bounds across the three primary gains. Report all 44 paired condition effects, leave-one-condition-out ranges, effective condition count and model/optimizer sensitivity. Repeated visits, SOCs, frequencies and specimens are never treated as independent cells. The estimand is the equal-weight average over these 44 designed opaque conditions; bootstrap intervals are stability summaries, not proof of a random condition superpopulation.

## Controls and falsification

- **False peers:** replace both peer trajectories with whole trajectories from different conditions, matched without post-cutoff outcomes on first-three-visit shape distance, elapsed schedule, temperature, `timestamp_origin`, duplicate pattern and available-history length. Re-index only by elapsed time, enforce the same availability mask, generate 5,000 deterministic SHA-256-seeded assignments, and report match failures. True-peer gain must exceed the 95th percentile of this null.
- **No-same-bin test:** remove every same-bin peer even when complete. This is the prespecified 601-example `G_zero` test and a full-cohort one-visit-lag ablation.
- **Shared-linear ablation:** permit a peer-informed shared intercept/slope but no shared nonlinear innovations. H-sentinel requires gain beyond shared baseline geometry and drift.
- **Acquisition-order controls:** compare M-peer; stratify by zero/one/two peers and target replicate; remove calendar week/order terms; restrict to first-acquired and last-acquired targets; use timestamp-only gating only as an explicitly less conservative sensitivity.
- **Quality/representation controls:** K=8/16; original 180 coordinates; fixed frequency splines; SOC-50 only and leave-one-SOC-out; frequency-block deletion; raw amplitude/phase Cartesian reconstruction; positive-scale-only and unnormalized level controls; 24/72 h visits; ±0.25/±1 day bins; exclude duplicate/mixed-origin visits; 23–27 °C; omit/strengthen temperature and OCV adjustment; Gaussian/Student-t noise; primary 1,804 versus broader 1,926 examples.
- **Leak tests:** assert every target feature source finishes by cutoff, every admitted peer finishes strictly before it, every target visit starts later, fold preprocessing contains no held condition, and a future-peer canary causes verifier failure.

## Decision rules

The scientific relevance margins are prespecified, not known operational optima.

- **Supportive:** simultaneous lower 95% bounds exceed 10% for `G_total`, 5% for `G_shape`, and 5% for `G_zero`; H-peer beats the shared-linear ablation and the 95th percentile of false-peer nulls; MAE and calibration are not materially worse; and no condition deletion, target-replicate, timing, SOC/frequency, correction or representation control reverses direction. Conclude only that strictly earlier condition-matched level-free shapes provide next-measurement information in this finite cohort.
- **Adverse:** a simultaneous upper bound is below 5% total gain or 2% peer-shape gain, H-peer is worse, or true peers are typical of false peers. If gain appears only with same-bin peers while the upper bound for `G_zero` is below 2%, reject a longitudinal-sentinel interpretation and report only possible short-lag contemporaneous transfer. If M-peer captures the gain, attribute it to observed timing/metadata rather than peer EIS.
- **Inconclusive:** intervals cross margins; only one acquisition-order, replicate, condition, SOC/frequency block, correction, long-gap group or representation drives gain; calibration deteriorates; false-peer matching is inadequate; optimizer/boundary behavior is unstable; or fewer than 36 conditions remain in a required quality analysis. Preserve negative and mixed results without threshold shopping.

A positive result does not prove that the condition caused the common path, that the peers predict capacity or safety, or that a particular arc reflects a named degradation mode. An adverse result does not disprove retrospective sharedness; it shows that sharedness is not prospectively useful under these cutoffs, horizons and margins.

## Actual deliverable, alternatives and resources

The solver must newly fit P0, B-own, M-peer, H-peer and the shared-linear ablation. Completion is established by:
`source_manifest.csv`, `frequency_map.csv`, `spectrum_audit.json`, `duplicate_provenance.csv`, `visits.parquet`, `forecast_examples.parquet`, `availability_audit.json`, `folds.json`, `shape_transform.json`, `pca_loadings.parquet`, `model_spec.json`, `fitted_hyperparameters.json`, `forecast_provenance.parquet`, `predictions.parquet`, `metrics.json`, `uncertainty.json`, `false_peer_null.parquet`, `sensitivities.csv`, and rule-linked `conclusions.json`.

The fixed-spline dynamic model is retained as a substantive representation sensitivity. A permutation-invariant peer encoder plus GRU was specified on the same histories, target, folds and metrics, but deferred because only 44 independent conditions constrain representation learning; revisit it if learning curves stabilize and state-space residuals show repeatable nonlinear interactions. DRT/equivalent-circuit fitting is deferred because corrected spectra, opaque conditions and missing equilibration/raw logs make physical attribution nonunique.

The audit used 4 CPUs, 32 GiB, no GPU, and 27.78 s. Full execution requests 16 CPUs, 64 GiB, zero GPUs and up to 28,800 s, checkpointed after extraction, folds, each outer model, nulls and sensitivities. CPU is adequate for these state-space fits; GPU use would add no scientific information. If execution is incomplete, report it rather than weakening chronology, changing the target, dropping conditions or reducing required controls.

An automatic verifier can check source hashes, members, schema, keys, frequencies, shape invariance, frozen cohort, duplicate provenance, `timestamp_s+eis_duration_s` arithmetic, strict cutoffs, immediate-next filtering, fold isolation, model nesting/equal marginal intensity, predictions, weights, metrics, resampling, null construction and conclusion-rule consistency. It must accept appropriate supportive, adverse and inconclusive conclusions and reject any forecast claim based only on the readiness audit.

It cannot establish timestamp semantics beyond the source fields, advance knowledge of future schedules, condition causality, electrochemical versus instrument origin, capacity/safety relevance, practical optimality of the margins, or transport outside these 44 conditions. Those require source-author/data-dictionary confirmation, protocol and schedule logs, raw EIS quality/equilibration records, independent capacity/pulse outcomes, expert electrochemical review, more specimens, randomized acquisition order and an external cohort.
